confirmed.title: REPORTS_FULL capacity guard in begin_draw() submits after begin_pre_draw() already built the frame → framebuffers[-1] and descriptor_sets[base-1]
confirmed.description: begin_draw()'s query-partition capacity guard calls pgraph_vk_finish(VK_FINISH_REASON_REPORTS_FULL) + pgraph_vk_ensure_command_buffer(). But begin_pre_draw() has ALREADY run for this draw: it created the framebuffer (`if (r->framebuffer_index == 0) create_frame_buffer(pg);`, draw.c:2231) and wrote/advanced the descriptor sets. pgraph_vk_finish() then does `destroy_flight_framebuffers(pg, next); r->framebuffer_index = 0;` (draw.c:2029-2030), advances the flight slot, sets `r->descriptor_set_index = r->flight[next].descriptor_set_base` and `r->last_bound_*_descriptor_set_index = -1` (draw.c:2024-2027). pgraph_vk_ensure_command_buffer() only begins a CB — it does NOT recreate a framebuffer, and `r->framebuffer_dirty` is left false (finish never sets it; the only setters are in surface.c bind/unbind_surface). Control then falls into `if (!r->in_render_pass) begin_render_pass(pg);` (draw.c:2298), whose `nv2a_vk_assert(r->framebuffer_index > 0)` is compiled to `((void)0)` in every build (debug.h:66 `#define NV2A_VK_PERF_BUILD 1`). Two out-of-bounds uses follow.
confirmed.evidence:
draw.c:2270-2274:
```
    if (!pg->clearing && pg->zpass_pixel_count_enable &&
        r->num_queries_in_flight >= pgraph_vk_queries_per_slot(r) - 1) {
        pgraph_vk_finish(pg, VK_FINISH_REASON_REPORTS_FULL);
        pgraph_vk_ensure_command_buffer(pg);
    }
```
draw.c:1857 (begin_render_pass):
```
        .framebuffer = r->flight[r->current_flight].framebuffers[r->framebuffer_index - 1],
```
with `r->framebuffer_index == 0` this reads `flight[slot].framebuffers[-1]`, which by the struct layout at renderer.h:632-638 is the 8 bytes of `VkSemaphore semaphore` — a semaphore handle passed to vkCmdBeginRenderPass as a VkFramebuffer.
draw.c:1646-1658 (bind_descriptor_sets) then binds `r->descriptor_sets[r->descriptor_set_index - 1]`; after the finish `descriptor_set_index == flight[next].descriptor_set_base`, i.e. `descriptor_sets[-1]` whenever the new slot is 0, and a stale slot-0 set whenever it is 1.
confirmed.proposed_fix: Move the capacity guard out of begin_draw() to the top of begin_pre_draw() (before create_pipeline/create_frame_buffer/update_descriptor_sets), where alloc_report()'s identical guard already sits safely; or, if it must stay in begin_draw(), follow the finish with `r->framebuffer_dirty = true;` and re-run the begin_pre_draw() framebuffer + descriptor-set setup before begin_render_pass(). Also note the debug-marker imbalance the current shape creates: pgraph_vk_begin_debug_marker() was issued on the previous CB and pgraph_vk_end_debug_marker() lands on the new one.
confirmed.apple_impact: none — the bug and the fix are platform-neutral; macOS is equally exposed (the guard's own comment records the original pool overrun crashing inside MoltenVK's visibility-buffer encode). Note this contradicts the validation recorded in the architecture contract ("forcing MAX_QUERIES=64 ... guard fire ~3312x/interval with no crash") — re-run `XEMU_MAX_QUERIES=64` on both platforms.
confirmed.verifier_notes: Move the guard block (draw.c:2259-2274) to the very top of begin_pre_draw() (draw.c:2199), before create_pipeline/create_clear_pipeline. At that point in_draw is false, debug_depth == 0 (call sites begin the debug marker only AFTER begin_pre_draw returns, e.g. 2607-2608 and 3143/3155, so pgraph_vk_finish's `nv2a_vk_assert(r->debug_depth == 0)` holds and no marker straddles two CBs), and the existing `if (r->framebuffer_index == 0) create_frame_buffer(pg);` (2231), pgraph_vk_update_descriptor_sets (2229) and pgraph_vk_ensure_command_buffer (2235) then rebuild everything for the new slot naturally. Drop the trailing pgraph_vk_ensure_command_buffer from the guard since begin_pre_draw already ends with one. Keep the `- 1` reserve: the primer query in pgraph_vk_begin_command_buffer consumes one index after the guard runs. Side benefit: in the inline-elements path (3143-3156) copy_remapped_attributes_to_inline_buffer/get_emulated_indices_buf currently write staging data BEFORE the finish resets the staging offsets to the new slot's base (draw.c ~2050), so moving the guard ahead of begin_pre_draw also keeps this draw's inline data in the slot that will be submitted with it. Alternative if the guard must stay in begin_draw: after the finish set r->framebuffer_dirty = true and call begin_pre_draw(pg) again (marker imbalance would remain when debug utils are enabled). Also consider making nv2a_vk_assert(r->framebuffer_index > 0) and nv2a_vk_assert(r->descriptor_set_index >= 1) use nv2a …[truncated; full text in the session workflow journal]

confirmed.title: create_pipeline() early-return can leave the CLEAR pipeline bound for a subsequent real draw (fork replaced upstream's vertex-description memcmp with a dirty flag)
confirmed.description:
create_clear_pipeline() overwrites `r->pipeline_binding` with the clear pipeline node (draw.c:870 / :1039). On the next real draw, create_pipeline() takes the fast path `if (r->pipeline_binding && !pipeline_dirty) { r->pipeline_binding_changed = false; return; }` — leaving the CLEAR pipeline as `r->pipeline_binding`. begin_draw() then binds it (`must_bind_pipeline` is forced true because end_draw ended the render pass after the clear) and the guest's geometry is drawn with the clear pipeline (quad_vert/solid_frag, no vertex input state, CONSTANT_COLOR blending, no descriptor sets).

Upstream was protected by accident: its check_pipeline_dirty() memcmp'd `r->vertex_attribute_descriptions` against `r->pipeline_binding->key.attribute_descriptions`, and the clear key is memset to 0 (draw.c:857-859), so the comparison always reported dirty after a clear. The fork replaced that memcmp with the `r->vertex_state_dirty` flag (draw.c:1095, set by update_vertex_layout_dirty() in vertex.c:68 purely from a previous-draw snapshot), so nothing in check_pipeline_dirty() any longer distinguishes `PipelineKey.clear == true` from `false`.
confirmed.proposed_fix: Add a `clear` axis to the fast-dirty test, e.g. keep a `bool pipeline_binding_is_clear` set in create_clear_pipeline()/create_pipeline() and make check_pipeline_dirty() return true when `r->pipeline_binding_is_clear != pg->clearing`; or simply have create_clear_pipeline() stash/restore the draw pipeline binding in a separate field (`r->clear_pipeline_binding`) so `r->pipeline_binding` is never clobbered by a clear.
confirmed.apple_impact: none — the fix is platform-neutral and restores upstream's effective behaviour; macOS is exposed to the identical bug today.

confirmed.title: Dynamic-state skip caches are invalidated at CB begin but not when a pipeline that specifies the same state STATICALLY is bound
confirmed.description:
The 2026-08-09 fix poisons cached_line_width / cached_depth_bias_* / cached_blend_constants at pgraph_vk_begin_command_buffer (draw.c:2148-2154) to close the cross-command-buffer hole. The remaining hole is within one CB: the caches are not invalidated when vkCmdBindPipeline binds a pipeline whose VkPipelineDynamicStateCreateInfo does NOT list that state. Per the Vulkan dynamic-state rules, pipeline state that is not declared dynamic is applied to the command-buffer state at bind time (and on every desktop driver the static value is baked into the pipeline's pushed register state), so the cached value stops describing GPU state and the skip renders with the wrong value.

Three concrete reachable paths:
1. BLEND CONSTANTS: draw pipelines always declare VK_DYNAMIC_STATE_BLEND_CONSTANTS (draw.c:1415-1418), but a non-partial CLEAR pipeline declares only `dynamicStateCount = partial_color_clear ? 3 : 2` (draw.c:996), i.e. static blendConstants = {0,0,0,0}. Every full-colour or depth-only clear therefore programs {0,0,0,0}. begin_draw() skips the whole `if (!pg->clearing)` block for clears, so cached_blend_constants keeps the last draw's value; the next draw with the same value skips vkCmdSetBlendConstants and blends against {0,0,0,0}. Guest-reachable: pgraph_blend_factor_vk_map (constants.h:67-70) maps NV2A factors to VK_BLEND_FACTOR_CONSTANT_COLOR/ALPHA and their inverses.
2. LINE WIDTH: has_dynamic_line_width is per-pipeline (draw.c:1425-1430); non-line pipelines and clear pipelines carry static `.lineWidth = 1.0f` (draw.c:1274 / :929). line-pipeline → triangle-pipeline → line-pipeline with an unchanged scale factor skips vkCmdSetLineWidth and draws at 1.0 instead of `surface_scale_factor`.
3. DEPTH BIAS: has_dynamic_depth_bias is per-pipeline (draw.c:1420); pipelines without polygon offset carry static depthBiasEnable=FALSE and zeroed bias factors. offset-pipeline → plain-pipeline → offset-pipeline with unchanged ZOFFSETBIAS/ZOFFSETFACTOR skips vkCmdSetDepthBias → decal z-fighting.
confirmed.evidence: draw.c:2356-2364, 2368-2381, 2383-2394 all gate solely on `!r->dynstate_cache_valid || <value differs>`, and draw.c:2407 sets `r->dynstate_cache_valid = true;` unconditionally at the end of every begin_draw() — including clear draws, which never evaluate the blend-constant branch. The only invalidation site is draw.c:2148-2154 (`r->cached_line_width = NAN; ... r->cached_blend_constants[3] = NAN;`) inside pgraph_vk_begin_command_buffer, i.e. once per CB.
confirmed.proposed_fix: In begin_draw(), inside `if (must_bind_pipeline) { ... }` right after vkCmdBindPipeline, poison the caches for every state the newly bound pipeline does NOT declare dynamic: `if (!r->pipeline_binding->has_dynamic_line_width) r->cached_line_width = NAN; if (!r->pipeline_binding->has_dynamic_depth_bias) { r->cached_depth_bias_constant = NAN; r->cached_depth_bias_slope = NAN; }` and, for clear pipelines, poison cached_blend_constants (add a `has_dynamic_blend_constants` flag to PipelineBinding, set from `partial_color_clear` in create_clear_pipeline and true in create_pipeline). Cost is a few stores on pipeline change only.
confirmed.apple_impact: none — MoltenVK also applies a pipeline's static rasterizer/blend state at bind (MVKGraphicsPipeline only skips the state it recorded as dynamic), so macOS has the same defect today and the fix is a strict improvement there. No macOS fast path is removed; the skip still fires for every consecutive draw on the same pipeline.
confirmed.verifier_notes: In begin_draw() right after vkCmdBindPipeline (draw.c:2310), poison the caches for every dynamic state the newly bound pipeline specifies statically: `if (!r->pipeline_binding->has_dynamic_line_width) r->cached_line_width = NAN; if (!r->pipeline_binding->has_dynamic_depth_bias) { r->cached_depth_bias_constant = NAN; r->cached_depth_bias_slope = NAN; }` and add a `has_dynamic_blend_constants` flag to PipelineBinding (renderer.h:95-96), set to `partial_color_clear` in create_clear_pipeline (~1036) and `true` in create_pipeline (~1420); poison `cached_blend_constants[0..3] = NAN` when it is false. Because clear pipelines have both has_dynamic_* flags false, this single rule also covers the clear -> draw transitions. A simpler alternative that is also correct: poison all three caches whenever a pipeline is bound (only a few stores per pipeline change; loses the skip only on consecutive different-pipeline binds, which already pay a vkCmdBindPipeline). Update the VUID reference in comments/docs: line width is VUID-vkCmdDraw-None-08617 in the current spec (07833 is the older number). apple_impact: none — MoltenVK likewise applies statically specified state at bind, so macOS has the same latent defect and the fix is gated to pipeline-change events only; the per-draw skip on an unchanged pipeline is untouched. | Fix in hw/xbox/nv2a/pgraph/vk/draw.c begin_draw(), inside `if (must_bind_pipeline)` immediately after `vkCmdBindPipeline(...)` (draw.c:2311) and BEFORE the line-width compare  …[truncated; full text in the session workflow journal]

confirmed.title: Bulk vkCmdResetQueryPool resets the whole 2048-query slot partition on every command buffer, not just the indices actually used
confirmed.description: pgraph_vk_begin_command_buffer() unconditionally resets `pgraph_vk_queries_per_slot(r)` = 2048 occlusion queries at the start of every command buffer. On MoltenVK this is bookkeeping; on a native driver vkCmdResetQueryPool is real GPU work (a write of the result + availability slots, and on some drivers a small pipeline flush). Command buffers are submitted several times per flip (surface changes, NEED_BUFFER_SPACE, PRESENTING, FLIP_STALL, REPORTS_SUBMIT), while typical usage is a handful of queries per CB plus the primer. The slot knows how many indices its previous submission actually used (`r->flight[slot].query_count`), and unused indices are already in the reset/unavailable state, so resetting only `max(prev_used, 1)` is correct.
confirmed.evidence:
draw.c:2100-2102:
```
    vkCmdResetQueryPool(r->command_buffer, r->query_pool,
                        pgraph_vk_slot_query_base(r, r->current_flight),
                        pgraph_vk_queries_per_slot(r));
```
with reports.c:37 `r->max_queries_in_flight = 4096;` and renderer.h:1205-1208 `return r->max_queries_in_flight / NUM_FLIGHT_SLOTS;` → 2048 per CB.
confirmed.proposed_fix: Track a per-slot `int queries_reset_high_water` (initialised to pgraph_vk_queries_per_slot for the first CB, since a freshly created pool is uninitialised) and reset only `MAX(1, high_water)` indices, updating it from `r->num_queries_in_flight` at submit. Measure with XEMU_NV2A_NSPROF on the Windows box before/after — if the delta is inside noise, drop the change rather than carrying the complexity.
confirmed.apple_impact: none — fewer reset commands is at worst neutral for MoltenVK; the primer query at draw.c:2115-2124 and its index are untouched, so Invariant 3 is unaffected.
confirmed.verifier_notes: If pursued: add `int query_reset_hw` to the flight slot struct (renderer.h ~687), initialise to pgraph_vk_queries_per_slot(r) in pgraph_vk_init_reports (reports.c:54-57) so each slot's FIRST command buffer still fully resets its partition (fresh pool state is undefined); at submit (draw.c:2005, next to `r->flight[slot].query_count = r->num_queries_in_flight;`) set `r->flight[slot].query_reset_hw = r->num_queries_in_flight;`; at draw.c:2100 reset `MAX(1, r->flight[r->current_flight].query_reset_hw)` instead of queries_per_slot. Do NOT read flight[slot].query_count at begin time - it is already zeroed by the drain in pgraph_vk_wait_for_previous_flight (command.c:244 -> reports.c:222). Re-initialise on pool recreation (finalize/init pair, renderer.c:75/104). Expected GPU saving is tens of KB of fill per CB; measure with XEMU_NV2A_NSPROF and drop if inside noise as the finder proposes. Apple impact: none - primer query and index layout unchanged (Invariant 3 intact).

confirmed.title: primitiveRestartEnable=VK_TRUE for strip/fan topologies is a fork-only divergence with no NV2A basis and no GL-renderer counterpart
confirmed.description: create_pipeline() enables primitive restart for TRIANGLE_STRIP / LINE_STRIP / TRIANGLE_FAN, justified by a comment asserting 'NV2A supports an "index restart" marker in indexed draws (matching Vulkan's 0xFFFF / 0xFFFFFFFF semantics)'. No such handling exists anywhere else in the tree — `grep -rn 'PRIMITIVE_RESTART|primitive_restart' hw/xbox/nv2a/` returns nothing, so the OpenGL renderer never enables GL_PRIMITIVE_RESTART and upstream's Vulkan renderer had `primitiveRestartEnable = VK_FALSE`. Two consequences: (a) the two renderers now disagree on the meaning of index 0xFFFFFFFF, which NV097_ARRAY_ELEMENT32 can deliver into pg->inline_elements; (b) with VK_INDEX_TYPE_UINT32 the restart value is 0xFFFFFFFF, so the guest's 16-bit 0xFFFF (zero-extended into inline_elements) never matches — the feature cannot do the job the comment claims while still costing whatever index-assembly fast path the driver gives up. Low impact on Pascal (hardware restart), but it is an unjustified behaviour change on the newly-live Windows path.
confirmed.evidence:
draw.c:1243-1261:
```
    VkPrimitiveTopology topology = get_primitive_topology(pg);
    bool restart_enable =
        topology == VK_PRIMITIVE_TOPOLOGY_TRIANGLE_STRIP ||
        topology == VK_PRIMITIVE_TOPOLOGY_LINE_STRIP ||
        topology == VK_PRIMITIVE_TOPOLOGY_TRIANGLE_FAN;
    ...
        .primitiveRestartEnable = restart_enable ? VK_TRUE : VK_FALSE,
```
vs the clear pipeline at draw.c:915 which keeps `VK_FALSE`, and the absence of any GL counterpart.
confirmed.proposed_fix: Either revert to VK_FALSE (matching upstream and the GL renderer), or keep it and back the claim: cite the NV2A method that programs the restart index and make the GL renderer do the same, plus note that a UINT32 index buffer built from 16-bit guest elements can never carry the restart value. As it stands the comment is unverifiable and the two renderers diverge.
confirmed.apple_impact: none — reverting restores upstream behaviour on both platforms; no macOS-specific path depends on it (MoltenVK maps it to MTLPrimitiveTopologyClass restart handling, also inert for the same index-width reason).
confirmed.verifier_notes: Simplest fix: restore `.primitiveRestartEnable = VK_FALSE` in create_pipeline() (hw/xbox/nv2a/pgraph/vk/draw.c:1243-1260), delete the `restart_enable` computation and the unverifiable NV2A comment, and drop the corresponding "Primitive restart" bullet added to the docs by commit da115cc35f. This is a pure revert to upstream behaviour and matches the GL renderer; apple_impact = none (MoltenVK path also had it VK_FALSE upstream, and the restart value could never fire for 16-bit guest indices anyway). If the author believes NV2A does have an index-restart marker, the alternative is to keep it but cite the NV097 method that programs the restart index, implement the same marker handling in pgraph.c / the GL renderer (GL_PRIMITIVE_RESTART + glPrimitiveRestartIndex), and translate the guest 16-bit marker into 0xFFFFFFFF when ARRAY_ELEMENT16 fills inline_elements — without that translation the feature is inert for 16-bit indices. Do not change the clear pipeline (draw.c:915) or display.c:862, which are correctly VK_FALSE.

confirmed.title: BUFFER_STAGING_DST/SRC grew 64 MiB → 512 MiB each and are now both persistently mapped: ~1 GiB of dedicated, committed, mapped host memory at startup
confirmed.description: The fork raised BUFFER_STAGING_DST from `4096 * 4096 * 4` (64 MiB) to `512 * 1024 * 1024`, with BUFFER_STAGING_SRC mirroring it, and added both to the persistently-mapped list. Both use `host_alloc_create_info`, which carries VMA_ALLOCATION_CREATE_DEDICATED_MEMORY_BIT, so each is its own eagerly-committed VkDeviceMemory. On Windows that is ~1 GiB of committed (pagefile-backed) address space plus 1 GiB of mapped views, present from renderer init regardless of the surface scale factor in use — on top of the guest's 128 MiB VRAM mirror (BUFFER_VERTEX_RAM) and the 512 MiB of device-local compute buffers. The size bump carries no justifying comment (the compute buffers, reduced in the same change, do have one: 'Worst case at 10x scale of 640x480: 6400*4800*5 ~ 147 MiB'). 32 GB on the target machine absorbs it; an 8 GB Windows box will not, and docs §R already lists the sibling 'BUFFER_COMPUTE 256 MiB cap' as a suspected-latent item.
confirmed.proposed_fix: Size the staging pair from the same worst case the compute buffers document (max scaled surface bytes at the configured surface_scale_factor, e.g. `640*480*scale*scale*4` rounded up, clamped) instead of a flat 512 MiB, and record the derivation in a comment. If a flat size is preferred, drop DEDICATED_MEMORY so VMA can suballocate, and consider mapping STAGING_DST lazily (it is only read on surface download).
confirmed.apple_impact: none — on Apple Silicon the same allocation comes out of unified memory; a smaller, derived size is strictly better there too and no macOS path depends on the 512 MiB constant.
confirmed.verifier_notes: Keep the finding but correct the proposed fix: (a) decouple BUFFER_STAGING_DST from BUFFER_STAGING_SRC — DST is single-surface, synchronous (surface.c:408-410, 572-578), so size it from the same worst case the compute buffers already document (e.g. `640*480*scale*scale*4`, clamped to ~147-256 MiB at 10x scale, or a flat 256 MiB matching BUFFER_COMPUTE) and add the derivation comment; (b) do NOT shrink BUFFER_STAGING_SRC to a per-surface size — it is a per-flight-slot bump pool (command.c:259-278, texture.c:889-914) and shrinking it converts memory into extra VK_FINISH_REASON_NEED_BUFFER_SPACE finishes; if reducing it, do so with XEMU_NV2A_NSPROF / texture-streaming measurement of finish counts, and record the derivation in a comment next to the 192-GB-M2-Ultra tuning origin (commit 3b57e3322c); (c) optionally drop VMA_ALLOCATION_CREATE_DEDICATED_MEMORY_BIT for the staging pair so VMA can suballocate, though with 256+ MiB buffers the benefit is marginal. apple_impact: none — same code path on both platforms; a right-sized DST is strictly a footprint reduction on unified memory too, and SRC behaviour is unchanged.

confirmed.title: GPU surface unswizzle is silently discarded (and its output overwritten) for swizzled Z24S8 zeta uploads — depth uploaded from still-swizzled bytes
confirmed.description: `use_gpu_unswizzle` (surface.c:1902) and `use_compute_to_convert_depth_stencil_format` (surface.c:1931) are computed independently and are not mutually exclusive. When both are true the GPU-unswizzle block (1967-2011) copies STAGING_SRC -> BUFFER_COMPUTE_DST, unswizzles into BUFFER_COMPUTE_SRC and sets `upload_src_buffer = BUFFER_COMPUTE_SRC`; then the depth-stencil block at 2038 unconditionally re-copies `copy_buffer->buffer` (STAGING_SRC, which still holds the *swizzled* bytes because `gl_read_buf = buf` at 1922) into BUFFER_COMPUTE_DST, unpacks it into BUFFER_COMPUTE_SRC (`unpack_buffer`), and overwrites `upload_src_buffer = unpack_buffer->buffer` at 2141. The unswizzle result is thrown away and the depth image is filled from Morton-ordered garbage. Upstream always CPU-unswizzled first, so this is a fork regression. It is reachable: `target->swizzle` is set from `pg->surface_type` for zeta as well as color (surface.c:2329), swizzled surfaces are always power-of-two (`get_surface_dimensions`, surface.c:194-197), and Z24S8 has `bytes_per_pixel == 4` (constants.h:392) with host format D24_UNORM_S8_UINT / D32_SFLOAT_S8_UINT. The fork's own comment at surface.c:2484 documents exactly such a title (Azurik ping-ponging a zeta between a 1280x480 scene and a 256x256 swizzled RTT pass). Secondarily, the two blocks also share BUFFER_COMPUTE_DST/SRC with no WAR barrier between the unswizzle dispatch's SHADER_READ of COMPUTE_DST and the depth path's TRANSFER_WRITE of the same buffer (a sync-validation hazard on native drivers, tolerated by MoltenVK's serialised queue).
confirmed.evidence:
surface.c:1902 `bool use_gpu_unswizzle = surface->swizzle && (surface->fmt.bytes_per_pixel == 4 || surface->fmt.bytes_per_pixel == 2) && r->compute.unswizzle_pipeline != VK_NULL_HANDLE && ...;`
surface.c:1921 `} else { gl_read_buf = buf; }`  /* raw swizzled VRAM */
surface.c:2038 `if (use_compute_to_convert_depth_stencil_format) { ... vkCmdCopyBuffer(cmd, copy_buffer->buffer, r->storage_buffers[BUFFER_COMPUTE_DST].buffer, 1, &buffer_copy_region);`
surface.c:2141 `upload_src_buffer = unpack_buffer->buffer;`
constants.h:392 `[NV097_SET_SURFACE_FORMAT_ZETA_Z24S8] = { 4 },`
confirmed.proposed_fix: Add `&& !use_compute_to_convert_depth_stencil_format` to the `use_gpu_unswizzle` predicate (hoist the depth-stencil test above line 1902), so a swizzled Z24S8/D32S8 zeta falls back to the CPU `unswizzle_rect` path exactly as upstream. Z16 zeta and colour surfaces keep the GPU path. Optionally add an `nv2a_vk_assert(!(use_gpu_unswizzle && use_compute_to_convert_depth_stencil_format))` to pin the invariant.
confirmed.apple_impact: none — the same defect exists on macOS today; the fix restores correct depth content on both platforms and only removes a (currently wasted) compute dispatch.
confirmed.verifier_notes: In hw/xbox/nv2a/pgraph/vk/surface.c, move the `use_compute_to_convert_depth_stencil_format` computation (currently 1931-1933) above the `use_gpu_unswizzle` predicate at 1902, and add `&& !use_compute_to_convert_depth_stencil_format` to `use_gpu_unswizzle`. Then a swizzled D24S8/D32S8 zeta takes the existing CPU `unswizzle_rect` branch (1910-1918) so STAGING_SRC holds linear packed data for the unpack compute. Optionally `nv2a_vk_assert(!(use_gpu_unswizzle && use_compute_to_convert_depth_stencil_format));`. Alternative (keeps GPU unswizzle for depth) would be to feed the unswizzle output back as the unpack source, but that needs an extra COMPUTE_SRC->COMPUTE_DST copy plus WAW barriers; not worth it for a rare path. Drop the secondary "missing WAR barrier" point from the finding — the COMPUTE->TRANSFER execution dependency in `post_compute` already orders it. Apple impact: none/positive — identical defect on macOS, fix is platform-independent and only removes a wasted dispatch. Severity lowered to medium because the default zeta_shape_discard path already skips the cited Azurik upload and guests usually clear depth after binding; the corruption surfaces mainly on evict->download->recreate round-trips of a swizzled Z24S8 target or CPU writes into its range. | Proposed fix is correct and minimal; adopt it. Concretely in hw/xbox/nv2a/pgraph/vk/surface.c: move the `bool use_compute_to_convert_depth_stencil_format = ...` declaration (currently :1931-1933) up above :1902, then add `& …[truncated; full text in the session workflow journal]

confirmed.title: Surface upload writes BUFFER_STAGING_SRC at absolute offset 0, ignoring the flight-slot partition, and races the still-in-flight command buffer left by the pipelined pgraph_vk_finish
confirmed.description: `pgraph_vk_upload_surface_data` memcpys into `copy_buffer->mapped` at offset 0 and issues all its buffer barriers/copies with `bufferOffset`/`srcOffset` 0, i.e. it treats BUFFER_STAGING_SRC as exclusively its own. But the fork partitions BUFFER_STAGING_SRC per flight slot (command.c:260-289: `staging_per_slot = buffer_size / NUM_FLIGHT_SLOTS`, slot 0 = [0, 256 MiB)) and `upload_texture_image` bump-allocates texture staging from the *current slot's* base (texture.c:906-913), recording `vkCmdCopyBufferToImage` reads of those bytes into the main command buffer. The fork's `pgraph_vk_finish` no longer waits for the CB it submits — it submits slot A, flips to slot B and waits only B's fence (draw.c:2021-2022) — so after the finish at surface.c:1873 slot A's CB is still executing. When A is slot 0 (every other finish), the host memcpy at offset 0 overwrites the exact bytes slot A's pending `vkCmdCopyBufferToImage` calls are reading. Upstream was safe because its `pgraph_vk_finish` ended with `vkWaitForFences(... command_buffer_fence ...)`, leaving the GPU idle. display.c already implements the correct pattern (`VkDeviceSize staging_base = r->flight[r->current_flight].staging_buffer_base;` at display.c:546, plus a finish when the bump has advanced); surface.c was never updated. Note the bounds check at surface.c:1929 also uses `copy_buffer->buffer_size`, not the slot limit, confirming the whole-buffer assumption.
confirmed.evidence:

confirmed.title: Compute descriptor-set partition guard checked once before a loop that consumes num_layers * levels sets

confirmed.title: prune_invalid_surfaces destroys the newest quarantined surfaces first (inverted relative to upstream)
confirmed.description: `invalidate_surface_full` does `QTAILQ_INSERT_HEAD(&r->invalid_surfaces, ...)`, so the list is newest-first, and `get_any_compatible_invalid_surface` walks from the head to prefer the freshest reusable image. The rewritten `prune_invalid_surfaces` also walks from the head and destroys entries until `invalid_surface_count <= keep` — i.e. it destroys the *newest* entries and keeps the stalest. Upstream counted from the head and destroyed only entries beyond `keep`, keeping the newest. The consequence is that once the pool exceeds `num_invalid_surfaces_to_keep` the reuse pool retains only stale, most-likely-incompatible images while destroying exactly the images the deferred zeta-shape eviction was designed to hand back — turning the quarantine's fast reuse into a create/destroy churn (`create_surface_image` + two `vmaCreateImage` per miss). The retirement gate partially masks this (the newest entries are also the most likely to be un-retired and thus `continue`d), which is why it has not shown up as a regression.
confirmed.evidence:
surface.c:1741-1743 `QTAILQ_FOREACH_SAFE(surface, &r->invalid_surfaces, entry, next) { if (r->invalid_surface_count <= keep) { break; }`
surface.c:1114 `QTAILQ_INSERT_HEAD(&r->invalid_surfaces, surface, entry);`
upstream/master surface.c `num_surfaces += 1; if (num_surfaces > keep) { QTAILQ_REMOVE(...); destroy_surface_image(...); }`
confirmed.proposed_fix: Restore upstream's ordering: keep a running index and only destroy entries whose position exceeds `keep` (skipping, but still counting, entries held back by `surface_image_in_recording_cb` / `evict_submit_seq`), so destruction proceeds oldest-first from the tail while the head stays available for `get_any_compatible_invalid_surface`.
confirmed.apple_impact: none — same code path on both platforms; restoring oldest-first eviction can only improve quarantine hit rate.
confirmed.verifier_notes: In prune_invalid_surfaces (surface.c:1738), iterate from the tail so destruction proceeds oldest-first while the head remains for reuse: replace `QTAILQ_FOREACH_SAFE(surface, &r->invalid_surfaces, entry, next)` with `QTAILQ_FOREACH_REVERSE_SAFE(surface, &r->invalid_surfaces, entry, next)` (defined in include/qemu/queue.h:488), keeping the existing `count <= keep` break and both `continue` gates (recording-CB and evict_submit_seq) exactly as they are. The keep=0 drain at pgraph_vk_surface_flush (line 2827) is unaffected because it destroys everything anyway. Alternatively restore upstream's positional counter (count every entry, including gated ones, and destroy only when position > keep and retired). Platform-independent change; apple_impact none (same code path, can only improve quarantine hit rate on both platforms). No VUID involvement — the retirement gate already makes destruction spec-valid; this is purely a pool-policy issue.

confirmed.title: copy_zeta_surface_to_texture's narrowed barrier sizes under-count the alignment padding before the stencil plane
confirmed.description: The fork replaced `.size = VK_WHOLE_SIZE` with `.size = copied_image_size` on four buffer barriers, but `copied_image_size` is computed as `scaled_w * scaled_h * host_bytes_per_pixel + stencil_buffer_size`, whereas the stencil plane is actually written at `stencil_buffer_offset = ROUND_UP(scaled_w * scaled_h * 4, minStorageBufferOffsetAlignment)`. When that ROUND_UP adds padding P (i.e. `scaled_w * scaled_h * 4` is not a multiple of `minStorageBufferOffsetAlignment`), the real written range ends at `copied_image_size + P`, so the barriers cover P bytes less than the data they are supposed to order, and `nv2a_vk_bounds_check(dst_storage_buffer->buffer_size >= copied_image_size)` under-counts by the same amount. On the target GPU `minStorageBufferOffsetAlignment` is 16 and typical surface pixel counts are multiples of 4, so P is 0 for 640x480; it becomes non-zero for odd clip dimensions. MoltenVK's automatic hazard tracking hides an under-sized barrier entirely; a native driver honours the stated range.
confirmed.evidence:
texture.c:1216 `size_t copied_image_size = scaled_width * scaled_height * surface->host_fmt.host_bytes_per_pixel;`
texture.c:1236 `stencil_buffer_offset = ROUND_UP(scaled_width * scaled_height * 4, r->device_props.limits.minStorageBufferOffsetAlignment);`
texture.c:1240 `copied_image_size += stencil_buffer_size;`
texture.c:1284/1315/1343/1379 `.size = copied_image_size`
confirmed.proposed_fix: Compute the covered range from the actual layout, e.g. `size_t covered = stencil_buffer_size ? stencil_buffer_offset + stencil_buffer_size : scaled_width * scaled_height * surface->host_fmt.host_bytes_per_pixel;` and use `covered` for the four barrier `.size` fields and the bounds check (the surface.c download path already does this correctly by deriving `image_copy_size` from `copy_regions[1].bufferOffset`).
confirmed.apple_impact: none — widening a barrier range is a no-op on MoltenVK.
confirmed.verifier_notes: In C:\Users\ms\Documents\xemu-macos\hw\xbox\nv2a\pgraph\vk\texture.c, after the stencil region is set up (line ~1253), derive the covered range from the actual layout instead of summing plane sizes: `size_t covered_size = stencil_buffer_size ? stencil_buffer_offset + stencil_buffer_size : copied_image_size;` (or simply set `copied_image_size = stencil_buffer_offset + stencil_buffer_size;` inside the `if (aspect & STENCIL)` block in place of the `+=` at line 1240). Use it for the bounds check at 1255 and the four barriers at 1284, 1315, 1343, 1379 (the two BUFFER_COMPUTE_SRC barriers using packed_image_size are already correct). This mirrors surface.c:393-401 (`image_copy_size = copy_regions[1].bufferOffset + w*h`). Behaviour on Apple (D32_SFLOAT_S8_UINT, hbpp=8) narrows from an over-covering range to the exact written range, which is still valid; no macOS regression. Verify with the Vulkan validation layer's synchronization validation on an odd clip-size D24S8 surface (e.g. 641x480 or 640x479) on the NVIDIA machine.

confirmed.title: Surface-expiry throttle samples QEMU_CLOCK_REALTIME on every draw
confirmed.description: `pgraph_vk_surface_update` runs per draw (draw.c:47 and draw.c:2584) and unconditionally calls `qemu_clock_get_ns(QEMU_CLOCK_REALTIME)` just to test a 33 ms throttle. On Windows that is `QueryPerformanceCounter` plus a `muldiv64` (include/qemu/timer.h `get_clock()` under `_WIN32`). At ~400-500 draws/flip and 60 flips/s this is 30-60k QPC calls per second on the PFIFO thread. On the target (Haswell + Win10, invariant-TSC-backed QPC) that is ~25-50 ns each, ~0.1-0.3% of the thread — small but pure overhead; on any machine where QPC falls back to the HPET (BIOS quirk or `bcdedit /set useplatformclock true`, ~500-1000 ns/call) the same code costs 3-6% of the PFIFO thread. The clock read is only needed when the throttle could actually expire.
confirmed.evidence:
surface.c:2683-2685 `int64_t now_ns = qemu_clock_get_ns(QEMU_CLOCK_REALTIME);\n    const int64_t surface_expire_interval_ns = 33 * 1000 * 1000;\n    if (now_ns - r->last_expire_ns >= surface_expire_interval_ns) {`
draw.c:47 `pgraph_vk_surface_update(d, true, true, depth_test || stencil_test);`
confirmed.proposed_fix: Gate the clock read behind a cheap counter, e.g. only sample when `++r->surface_update_ticks >= 64` (reset on sample) or when `pg->frame_time != r->last_expire_frame_time` — either keeps the wall-clock backstop that motivated the throttle (the level-load burst case documented in the comment) while cutting QPC calls by ~2 orders of magnitude.
confirmed.apple_impact: none — `mach_absolute_time` on macOS is already cheap, and the backstop semantics are unchanged.
confirmed.verifier_notes: Keep at low; expected payoff is ~1.3 ms/s of PFIFO-thread time (~0.13%, ~35 us/frame), which is below the fork's measurable threshold — treat as a trivially safe cleanup, not a claimed win. In hw/xbox/nv2a/pgraph/vk/surface.c:2685, gate the clock read: e.g. `if (++r->surface_update_ticks >= 64 || pg->frame_time != r->last_expire_frame_time) { r->surface_update_ticks = 0; r->last_expire_frame_time = pg->frame_time; int64_t now_ns = qemu_clock_get_ns(QEMU_CLOCK_REALTIME); if (now_ns - r->last_expire_ns >= 33ms) { ...existing body... } }` — use the OR form (not counter-only) so low-draw scenes still get a per-flip sample and the archaeology-1.4 burst backstop still fires within 64 draws of expiry. Add the two fields to PGRAPHVkState in renderer.h next to `last_expire_ns` (renderer.h:1018). Platform-neutral, no ifdef; apple_impact none (mach_absolute_time is cheap there, semantics unchanged). Note the finder's call-count (30-60k/s) is ~2x high — draw.c:2584 is per clear, blit.c:84 per blit; the HPET-fallback cost figure is hypothetical and does not apply to the target (measured 10 MHz TSC-backed QPC). If pursued, also consider that 27 of the 48 ns is the `(__int128)a * 1e9 / clock_freq` divide in host-utils.h:56, so hoisting the read is the right lever rather than swapping clock sources.

confirmed.title: PVIDEO upload calls pgraph_vk_finish() while the display aux command buffer is open — assert abort / recording-state corruption on Windows
confirmed.description:
The fork moved the PVIDEO overlay upload from its own single-time command buffer (upstream `upload_pvideo_image`) into the display command buffer (`upload_pvideo_to_cmd(pg, state, cmd)`, called at display.c:1635 *after* `cmd = pgraph_vk_begin_single_time_commands(pg)` at display.c:1628). `upload_pvideo_to_cmd` then does its own staging-space reclaim by calling `pgraph_vk_finish()` at display.c:546-550 — i.e. a nested finish while `r->in_aux_command_buffer == true` and `cmd == r->aux_command_buffer` is mid-recording.

Both branches of `pgraph_vk_finish` (draw.c:1942-1993) break:
- `aux_has_work == true` -> it calls `pgraph_vk_begin_single_time_commands(pg)`, whose first statement is `assert(!r->in_aux_command_buffer)` (command.c:83) -> abort.
- `aux_has_work == false` -> `if (r->in_aux_command_buffer) { vkEndCommandBuffer(r->aux_command_buffer); r->in_aux_command_buffer = false; }` (draw.c:1983-1986) — it *ends and drops* the half-recorded display CB without submitting it. Control then returns to `upload_pvideo_to_cmd`, which keeps recording `vkCmdPipelineBarrier`/`vkCmdCopyBuffer`/`vkCmdDispatch` into a command buffer that is no longer in the recording state, and `pgraph_vk_end_single_time_commands(pg, cmd)` then trips `assert(r->in_aux_command_buffer)` (command.c:99).

Secondarily, `pgraph_vk_finish` rotates the flight slot (`r->current_flight = (r->current_flight + 1) % NUM_FLIGHT_SLOTS`, draw.c:2021) and `pgraph_vk_select_flight_slot` repoints `r->aux_command_buffer` at the *other* slot, while the local `staging_base` (read at display.c:546, before the finish) still names the old slot's staging region. The subsequent `r->storage_buffers[BUFFER_STAGING_SRC].buffer_offset = staging_base;` at display.c:549 then points the bump allocator into the other flight slot's staging range, which the just-submitted CB is still reading.

This is Windows/Linux/Apple-GL specific: on the default macOS path `async_compositor = xemu_present_is_metal() && r->present_timeline_event` is true (display.c:1622-1625) so `cmd` comes from `pgraph_vk_begin_compositor_commands`, which does not set `in_aux_command_buffer`, and the nested finish takes the normal aux path harmlessly. On Windows `async_compositor` is compiled out (`#if HAVE_IOSURFACE_SHARING`) and is always false. QEMU never defines NDEBUG, so `assert()` is live in the release MSYS2 build too — the user sees a hard abort.
confirmed.proposed_fix: Hoist the staging reclaim out of `upload_pvideo_to_cmd` into `render_display`, before the command buffer is opened: compute `need_pvideo_upload` (the memcmp) first, and if it is true and `r->storage_buffers[BUFFER_STAGING_SRC].buffer_offset > r->flight[r->current_flight].staging_buffer_base`, call `pgraph_vk_finish(pg, VK_FINISH_REASON_NEED_BUFFER_SPACE)` there. `upload_pvideo_to_cmd` then re-reads `staging_base` after any rotation and must never call `pgraph_vk_finish` itself. Optionally add `nv2a_vk_assert(!r->in_aux_command_buffer)` at the top of `pgraph_vk_finish` so a future nested finish is caught at the source.
confirmed.apple_impact: none — pure reordering. macOS's default Metal/compositor-CB path never took the broken branch; macOS's GL-present fallback gets the same fix. No behavioural change to the Metal present chain, MetalFX, or the push ring.
confirmed.verifier_notes:
The finder's hoist is the right shape. Concretely, in `render_display` (display.c ~1620), before `pgraph_vk_begin_single_time_commands`:
- compute `bool need_pvideo_upload = disp->pvideo.state.enabled && memcmp(&disp->pvideo.state, &disp->pvideo.last_uploaded_state, sizeof(PvideoState)) != 0;`
- if `need_pvideo_upload && r->in_command_buffer && r->storage_buffers[BUFFER_STAGING_SRC].buffer_offset > r->flight[r->current_flight].staging_buffer_base` -> `pgraph_vk_finish(pg, VK_FINISH_REASON_NEED_BUFFER_SPACE)`. (Finish already resets buffer_offset to the new slot base at draw.c:2054-2056, so no manual `buffer_offset = staging_base` is needed — delete line 549's assignment entirely; it is what introduces the cross-slot aliasing.)

Why the finish is still required at all: the open main CB's pending `vkCmdCopyBufferToImage`s reference `[staging_base, buffer_offset)`; writing the YUV frame at `staging_base` without first submitting them would corrupt those textures. A cheaper alternative that avoids the finish in the common case: sub-allocate the PVIDEO frame from the bump allocator (`ROUND_UP(buffer_offset, 16)`) and only finish when `offset + yuv_size > staging_buffer_limit`; since `pgraph_vk_end_single_time_commands` waits on the aux fence synchronously, the region can be released immediately after. confirmed.title: PVIDEO overlay freezes: the upload cache keys on the register state only, never on the VRAM contents
confirmed.description:
The fork added a skip-if-unchanged cache around the PVIDEO YUV upload keyed on `memcmp` of the whole `PvideoState` struct. `PvideoState` (renderer.h:316-340) contains only PVIDEO register values — `base`, `limit`, `offset`, `pitch`, `format`, in/out sizes and positions, scale and colour key — and nothing derived from the pixel data. `NV_PVIDEO_OFFSET` is a single fixed register (nv2a_regs.h:680), not a per-buffer pair, so a title that decodes successive video frames into the same VRAM buffer at a constant offset produces a byte-identical `PvideoState` every frame. The overlay then displays the first uploaded frame forever while audio and the 3D layer keep running.

Upstream's Vulkan `upload_pvideo_image` uploaded unconditionally every time `state.enabled` was true, and the GL renderer's `render_display_pvideo_overlay` (gl/display.c:165) still does. This is a fork-only divergence and it diverges from the fork's own GL path, so a Windows user switching `display.renderer` between VULKAN and OPENGL sees different video.
confirmed.proposed_fix: Either drop the cache (restoring upstream/GL behaviour) or extend the key with the source contents. The cheap, correct version: keep the struct compare as a fast reject, and additionally hash the source span (`fast_hash(d->vram_ptr + state.base + state.offset, state.pitch * state.in_height)`) into `last_uploaded_state`'s companion field, or simply hook PVIDEO source pages into the existing guest dirty-tracking bitmap and re-upload when the span is dirty. Do not keep a register-only key.
confirmed.apple_impact: none — the same freeze exists on macOS; the fix restores correct video on both. If the memcpy cost matters on Apple, the content hash keeps the skip whenever the frame really is identical.
confirmed.verifier_notes: Minimal correct fix: in hw/xbox/nv2a/pgraph/vk/display.c render_display, do not use the register-struct compare alone as the skip condition. Options, in order of preference: (a) keep the struct compare as a fast reject but also compare a hash of the source span (`d->vram_ptr + state.base + state.offset`, `state.pitch * state.in_height` bytes, or `in_width*2` per row when pitch != row bytes) stored alongside `last_uploaded_state` (e.g. add `uint64_t last_uploaded_hash` to the `pvideo` struct in renderer.h:403-410); reset both at display.c:2224 and on savestate load; (b) hook the overlay source pages into the existing guest dirty-tracking (memory_region_test_and_clear_dirty over the span) and re-upload when dirty; (c) simply revert to upstream/GL behaviour (unconditional upload while enabled) — cost is one memcpy of ~in_width*2*in_height bytes (~600 KB for 640x480) plus the compute dispatch per present. Any of these is platform-neutral; apple_impact none/gated (macOS has the same freeze and benefits equally). Also consider clearing `last_uploaded_state` in the post-load path so restored guest VRAM is re-uploaded. | Preferred fix: delete the gate and restore upstream semantics -- in hw/xbox/nv2a/pgraph/vk/display.c:1632-1638 call `upload_pvideo_to_cmd(pg, disp->pvideo.state, cmd)` unconditionally when `state.enabled`, remove `PvideoState last_uploaded_state;` from renderer.h:405 and the reset at display.c:2224. confirmed.title: draw_time early-out in pgraph_vk_render_display skips PVIDEO/register-only display changes entirely on non-Apple
confirmed.description:
The fork added an early return at the top of `pgraph_vk_render_display` keyed purely on `surface->draw_time == disp->draw_time`. On Apple the guarded block still does interpolation stepping; on Windows/Linux `HAVE_IOSURFACE_SHARING` is 0 so the whole body compiles out and the function simply returns.

Everything that changes the composited output *without* redrawing the NV2A colour surface is therefore dropped: PVIDEO overlay enable/disable, overlay position/size/scale/colour-key changes, and (per the previous finding) new overlay frames. Upstream re-ran `render_display` on every sync. A title that parks a static 3D layer (paused menu, DVD/video playback screen, an attract loop that stops redrawing) while driving the overlay through registers gets a stale composited frame.

A second, smaller consequence: the early-out runs *before* the resolution is recomputed (`d->vga.get_resolution` at display.c:2213 and the `disp->width != width` recreate at display.c:2222), so a guest mode change is only picked up on the first sync after a new draw.
confirmed.proposed_fix: Widen the early-out condition so it also fires only when the display inputs are unchanged: compare the freshly computed `get_pvideo_state(pg)` against `disp->pvideo.state` (and the requested width/height) in addition to `draw_time`, e.g. `if (disp->image && surface->draw_time == disp->draw_time && memcmp(&new_pvideo, &disp->pvideo.state, sizeof(PvideoState)) == 0 && width == disp->width && height == disp->height)`. That keeps the skip in the common no-change case and restores upstream behaviour whenever anything the composite pass reads has moved.
confirmed.apple_impact: none — the Apple branch inside the guard is preserved verbatim; only the condition guarding it is tightened, and on Apple the same staleness bug exists today.

confirmed.title: SPIR-V disk cache uses bare fopen() instead of qemu_fopen() — silently never works under a non-ASCII Windows profile path
confirmed.description:
The fork's new SPIR-V disk cache builds its path from `xemu_settings_get_base_path()` (SDL_GetPrefPath, UTF-8 on Windows) and creates the directory with `g_mkdir_with_parents`, which is UTF-8-aware on Windows (GLib converts to UTF-16 and calls `_wmkdir`). It then opens the files with plain `fopen`, which on Windows interprets the byte string in the process ANSI code page, not UTF-8.

For any user whose profile path contains non-ASCII characters (`C:\Users\Müller\AppData\Roaming\xemu\xemu\...`), GLib creates the correct directory but `fopen` targets a differently-named (nonexistent) directory: `save_spirv_to_cache` silently does nothing (`if (f)` swallows it) and `load_spirv_from_cache` always misses. The shader cache is permanently cold — every pipeline miss pays a full glslang compile, which is exactly the long first-run stutter the cache was added to remove. The sibling pipeline cache in draw.c:469/510 already uses `qemu_fopen` for this reason, so this is an internal inconsistency, not a design choice.
confirmed.proposed_fix: Replace both `fopen` calls in glsl.c with `qemu_fopen` (already declared in include/qemu/osdep.h and a plain inline forwarder to `fopen` on POSIX). Same one-line change for any future cache file in this renderer.
confirmed.apple_impact: none — `qemu_fopen` is a static inline that expands to `fopen` on non-_WIN32, so macOS codegen is byte-identical.
confirmed.verifier_notes: Change `fopen(path, "rb")` at hw/xbox/nv2a/pgraph/vk/glsl.c:84 and `fopen(path, "wb")` at glsl.c:112 to `qemu_fopen(...)`. `qemu/osdep.h` is already transitively included (renderer.h -> qemu/osdep.h), and `qemu_fopen` is a static inline `fopen` on non-Windows, so macOS codegen is unchanged. confirmed.title: SPIR-V cache is written non-atomically and read back unvalidated — a torn file is a permanent hard crash via VK_CHECK's __builtin_trap
confirmed.description:
`save_spirv_to_cache` writes straight to the final path with no temp-file + rename, and does not check the `fwrite`/`fclose` result. `load_spirv_from_cache` accepts any file with `size > 0` — it verifies neither `size % 4 == 0` (required by VUID-VkShaderModuleCreateInfo-codeSize-08735) nor the SPIR-V magic word 0x07230203 — and the blob goes straight into `vkCreateShaderModule` as `codeSize = spv->len` (glsl.c:342) and into SPIRV-Reflect via `init_layout_from_spv`.

If xemu is killed, crashes, or the machine loses power mid-write (or two xemu instances write the same file concurrently, which is easy on Windows), the next launch reads a truncated blob. On a native NVIDIA driver `vkCreateShaderModule` fails or SPIRV-Reflect walks off the end; the fork's `VK_CHECK` now ends in `__builtin_trap()` (debug.h) rather than a recoverable error, so the process dies with an illegal-instruction exception. Because the bad file persists, this reproduces on every subsequent launch until the user finds and deletes the cache directory by hand — there is no self-heal and no message identifying the cache as the cause. The sibling pipeline cache in draw.c already does write-then-rename with an explicit comment about exactly this hazard, so the discipline exists in the tree and was just not applied here.
confirmed.proposed_fix: Mirror draw.c's `save_pipeline_cache_to_disk`: write to `"<path>.tmp"`, check `fwrite == len` and `fclose() == 0`, then `g_rename(tmp, path)` (g_rename replaces an existing target on Windows, plain rename() does not) and `g_unlink(tmp)` on any failure. In `load_spirv_from_cache`, reject the blob unless `size >= 20 && (size % 4) == 0 && ((uint32_t*)data)[0] == 0x07230203`, and on rejection `g_unlink(path)` and return NULL so the next compile self-heals the entry.
confirmed.apple_impact: none — the cache is platform-neutral code; the change only makes the same path robust on macOS too (glslang compiles are the slowest cold-start item there as well).
confirmed.verifier_notes:

(b) load_spirv_from_cache: reject unless size >= 20 && (size % 4) == 0 && ((uint32_t *)data)[0] == 0x07230203 (SpvMagicNumber); on rejection g_unlink(path) and return NULL so the next compile overwrites the entry. confirmed.title: SPIR-V cache key omits display.vulkan.debug_shaders, so the debug-shader option silently no-ops against a warm cache
confirmed.description:
The cache key is `fast_hash(glsl)` folded into a directory name carrying the xemu version and the glslang version (`SPIRV_COMPILER_ID`). The in-file comment explicitly reasons about key completeness ("that compiler's identity belongs in the cache key... any A/B of the change measures nothing") but misses the compile-*options* axis: `pgraph_vk_compile_glsl_to_spv` changes its output based on `g_config.display.vulkan.debug_shaders` (glsl.c:305-317 sets `disable_optimizer`, `generate_debug_info`, `emit_nonsemantic_shader_debug_info`, and calls `glslang_program_add_source_text`), and none of that reaches the key.

Consequences on Windows: turning `debug_shaders` on after any normal run serves optimized, debug-info-free SPIR-V from the warm cache, so the option appears to do nothing and RenderDoc/validation-layer shader debugging is impossible without manually wiping the cache dir. The reverse is worse for perf: shaders first compiled with `debug_shaders = true` are cached unoptimized-with-debug-info and then served to every subsequent normal run, silently inflating pipeline compile time and shader size — and quietly poisoning any Windows A/B baseline, which the fork's own change-control rules depend on.
confirmed.proposed_fix: Fold the compile options into the key. Cheapest: append a suffix to the cache directory name in `get_spirv_cache_dir()` — `g_strdup_printf("%sspirv_cache_v%d.%d.%d-%s%s", ..., g_config.display.vulkan.debug_shaders ? "-dbg" : "")` — which also keeps the two variants' entries from evicting each other. Alternatively mix the option bits into `glsl_hash` before lookup. The shader stage is also absent from the key; adding it costs nothing and removes a (remote) cross-stage collision.
confirmed.apple_impact: none — same key change applies on macOS; existing macOS caches simply fall cold once and repopulate.
confirmed.verifier_notes: In get_spirv_cache_dir() (glsl.c:61-70) append a variant suffix to the directory name, e.g. `"%sspirv_cache_v%d.%d.%d-%s%s"` with `g_config.display.vulkan.debug_shaders ? "-dbg" : ""`. Using a separate directory (rather than mixing a bit into glsl_hash) keeps the two variants from evicting each other and leaves existing normal-mode caches warm on both macOS and Windows (no cold-start for anyone with debug_shaders=false). Optionally also mix the glslang stage into the hash (`glsl_hash ^= stage` or fold it in via fast_hash over a small header) for completeness; that one does cause a one-time cold cache so weigh it against the near-zero collision risk. Apple impact: gated/none — identical key logic on both platforms, no behavioural change for default config.

confirmed.title: VK_KHR_external_semaphore_win32 is a hard device requirement but is never used; the VK->GL present handoff has neither the required GL semaphore nor a layout/ownership transfer
confirmed.description:
`required_device_extensions` demands `VK_KHR_EXTERNAL_SEMAPHORE_WIN32_EXTENSION_NAME` on Windows (and the FD equivalent on Linux), and `check_device_support_required_extensions` hard-fails device selection without it. A tree-wide grep finds no other reference: no `vkGetSemaphoreWin32HandleKHR`, no `glImportSemaphoreWin32HandleEXT`, no `glWaitSemaphoreEXT`/`glSignalSemaphoreEXT`. The extension is a pure compatibility tax today.

Two things follow. (a) Perf: because there is no cross-API semaphore, the only ordering between the Vulkan composite pass and the GL presenter is the blocking `vk_wait_for_fence_or_die` inside `pgraph_vk_end_single_time_commands` (command.c:113), which stalls the PFIFO thread once per present. Apple already has the async alternative — `pgraph_vk_begin_compositor_commands` / `pgraph_vk_end_compositor_commands_async` plus the exported timeline (`create_present_timeline`, display.c) — but it is fenced behind `HAVE_IOSURFACE_SHARING`. The Windows equivalent (export a binary VkSemaphore, `glImportSemaphoreWin32HandleEXT`, `glWaitSemaphoreEXT` before the presenter samples the texture) would let the existing compositor-CB ring be reused unchanged on Windows and remove the per-present PFIFO stall. (b) Correctness: EXT_external_objects requires an explicit ownership/layout transfer via `glWaitSemaphoreEXT`'s `srcLayouts` before GL samples an image the Vulkan side left in `VK_IMAGE_LAYOUT_SHADER_READ_ONLY_OPTIMAL` (display.c:1690-1693). Today nothing performs it; the GL driver is entitled to assume `GL_LAYOUT_GENERAL_EXT`. It happens to work on NVIDIA because the two layouts are hardware-identical, which is exactly the class of latent invalidity this audit is hunting.
confirmed.evidence:
instance.c:43-52:
```c
static char const *const required_device_extensions[] = {
#if HAVE_EXTERNAL_MEMORY
#ifdef WIN32
    VK_KHR_EXTERNAL_MEMORY_WIN32_EXTENSION_NAME,
    VK_KHR_EXTERNAL_SEMAPHORE_WIN32_EXTENSION_NAME,
#else
    VK_KHR_EXTERNAL_MEMORY_FD_EXTENSION_NAME,
    VK_KHR_EXTERNAL_SEMAPHORE_FD_EXTENSION_NAME,
#endif
#endif
```
grep -rn "SemaphoreWin32|glImportSemaphore|glWaitSemaphore|glSignalSemaphore|GetSemaphoreFd" hw/xbox/ ui/  ->  only the two declarations above.
command.c:110-117 (the stall it should replace):
```c
    VK_CHECK(vkQueueSubmit(r->queue, 1, &submit_info, r->aux_fence));
    nv2a_profile_inc_counter(NV2A_PROF_QUEUE_SUBMIT_AUX);
    int64_t nsprof_t0 = nsprof_begin();
    vk_wait_for_fence_or_die(r->device, r->aux_fence,
                             "pgraph_vk_end_single_time_commands");
```
confirmed.proposed_fix: Short term (zero risk): confirm with nsprof `NSPROF_AUX_FENCE_WAIT` how much the per-present stall actually costs on the target box before building anything. Medium term: create one exportable binary `VkSemaphore` at init, export it with `vkGetSemaphoreWin32HandleKHR`, import it once into GL with `glGenSemaphoresEXT` + `glImportSemaphoreWin32HandleEXT`, signal it from the composite submit (`pSignalSemaphores`) instead of fence-waiting, and have the GL presenter call `glWaitSemaphoreEXT` with `srcLayouts = GL_LAYOUT_SHADER_READ_ONLY_EXT` for the display texture before sampling — this closes the ownership-transfer gap and removes the stall in one change. If that is deferred, at minimum move `VK_KHR_EXTERNAL_SEMAPHORE_*` out of `required_device_extensions` into the optional list so an ICD lacking it does not hard-fail device selection for an unused feature.
confirmed.apple_impact: none — `HAVE_EXTERNAL_MEMORY` is 0 on Apple, so both the required-extension list and any GL-semaphore path are compiled out. macOS keeps its existing MTLSharedEvent/compositor-CB handoff untouched.
confirmed.verifier_notes:

If porting: create one exportable binary VkSemaphore at display init (VkExportSemaphoreCreateInfoKHR, handleType OPAQUE_WIN32), export with vkGetSemaphoreWin32HandleKHR, import once in the GL context with glGenSemaphoresEXT + glImportSemaphoreWin32HandleEXT (GL_HANDLE_TYPE_OPAQUE_WIN32_EXT). 3. Enforce strict 1:1 pairing: publish a "composite submitted this sync" flag alongside sync_complete so the UI thread calls glWaitSemaphoreEXT(sem, 0, NULL, 1, &gl_texture_id, &GL_LAYOUT_SHADER_READ_ONLY_EXT) exactly once per Vulkan signal, and never when render_display early-returned (display.c:1607-1609) or the 8 ms gate skipped the composite (renderer.c:162). confirmed.title: use_hw_depth is derived from need_geometry_shader, silently changing native-driver fragment depth for POINTS primitives
confirmed.description:
The fork threads a new `use_hw_depth` flag into the pixel-shader key, described in the surrounding comment as a MoltenVK fallback ("Tell the fragment shader to fallback to hardware depth interpolation (gl_FragCoord.z) if Geometry Shaders were bypassed (like on macOS)"). But the expression is `!need_geometry_shader`, and `need_geometry_shader = r->supports_geometry_shaders && pgraph_glsl_need_geom(&binding->state.geom)`. On Windows `supports_geometry_shaders` is true (the `#else` branch of instance.c requires `geometryShader`), yet `pgraph_glsl_need_geom` returns **false for `PRIM_TYPE_POINTS`** (glsl/geom.c:90-91). So on a native NVIDIA driver, point primitives now take the dFdx/dFdy depth approximation instead of upstream's barycentric `vtxPos0/1/2` path — an ungated shared behaviour change, not an Apple fallback.

The change may well be an improvement (for a point primitive `dFdx(gl_FragCoord.z)` is 0, and upstream's path reads `vtxPos0/1/2` varyings that no geometry shader wrote), but it is not what the comment claims and it has never been validated on a native driver. Worth pinning because it silently alters depth output for a whole primitive class on the Windows default renderer.
confirmed.proposed_fix: Either (a) make the intent explicit and keep native behaviour identical to upstream — `key.psh.state.use_hw_depth = !r->supports_geometry_shaders;` — so the fallback fires only where geometry shaders genuinely do not exist, or (b) keep the current expression, fix the misleading comment to say it also covers the GS-not-needed case on capable drivers, and record a point-primitive depth check in the needs-real-HW list. Decide with a title that draws points (particle/HUD effects) on the Windows box; do not leave the code and the comment disagreeing.
confirmed.apple_impact: none under (b). Under (a), macOS is unaffected because `supports_geometry_shaders` is false there, so `use_hw_depth` stays true for every primitive exactly as today.
confirmed.verifier_notes:
Bumped from low to medium because there is a concrete wrong-output case, not just an unvalidated equivalence: under z_perspective (w-buffering) point primitives on the native Vulkan path get depth = vtxPos.z instead of upstream's vtxPos0.w (upstream psh.c:1015-1044 vs fork psh.c:1009-1014). Still edge-case (points + w-buffer + depth test), hence medium not high.

Recommended fix = finder's option (a), which restores byte-identical upstream shader behaviour on every GS-capable driver and is a no-op on macOS:

hw/xbox/nv2a/pgraph/vk/shaders.c:419
-    key.psh.state.use_hw_depth = !need_geometry_shader;
+    key.psh.state.use_hw_depth = !r->supports_geometry_shaders;

and reword the comment at shaders.c:417-418 to "hardware-depth fallback when the device has no geometry shaders (MoltenVK/Metal)". Rationale: when supports_geometry_shaders is true but no GS is needed (POINTS), the vertex shader already emits valid vtxPos0/1/2 = vtxPos and triMZ = 0 (glsl/vsh.c:408-411), so upstream's z_perspective/non-perspective branches are fully correct without a GS; there is no reason to substitute the approximation there.

apple_impact: none. On Apple `F(geometryShader, false)` makes supports_geometry_shaders false, so use_hw_depth stays true for all primitives exactly as today. Shader cache keys on macOS are unchanged.

Separately (out of scope for this finding, macOS-only): the use_hw_depth branch itself ignores z_perspective, so w-buffered titles on MoltenVK write z rather than w for all p …[truncated; full text in the session workflow journal]

confirmed.title: nv2a_vk_bounds_check compiles to __builtin_unreachable() in every build, converting guest-driven bounds guards into optimization licences
confirmed.description:
`NV2A_VK_PERF_BUILD` is hardcoded to 1 with no meson/NDEBUG override anywhere in the tree, so `nv2a_vk_bounds_check(x)` expands to `if (!(x)) __builtin_unreachable();` in the release MSYS2 build *and* in `--debug` builds. That is not a no-op: it tells GCC it may assume the condition, so the compiler is free to delete downstream code that would only matter if the bound were exceeded, and a violation is undefined behaviour rather than a bounded failure.

The call sites are guest-controlled. `pgraph_vk_upload_surface_data` uses it on the staging-buffer capacity check for a surface whose dimensions come from guest registers (surface.c:1929: `nv2a_vk_bounds_check(uploaded_image_size <= copy_buffer->buffer_size)`). On a native driver with -O2 this becomes a silent out-of-bounds `memcpy_image` into host-visible mapped memory instead of a diagnosable abort. The header's own comment already says guest-boundary checks "should use regular assert()", so the classification of these sites is the bug, not the macro.
confirmed.evidence:
debug.h:
```c
#define NV2A_VK_PERF_BUILD 1
...
#if NV2A_VK_PERF_BUILD
#define nv2a_vk_bounds_check(x)               \
    do {                                       \
        if (!(x)) {                            \
            __builtin_unreachable();           \
        }                                      \
    } while (0)
```
surface.c:1927-1929 (guest-dimension-driven):
```c
    size_t uploaded_image_size = surface->height * surface->width *
                                 surface->fmt.bytes_per_pixel;
    nv2a_vk_bounds_check(uploaded_image_size <= copy_buffer->buffer_size);
```
No NDEBUG anywhere: `grep -rn NDEBUG meson.build configure` returns nothing, so plain `assert()` is live in release and there is no cost argument for the unreachable form.
confirmed.proposed_fix: Reclassify: leave `nv2a_vk_bounds_check` for genuinely internal invariants, and switch the guest-boundary sites (starting with surface.c:1929) to plain `assert()` or to an explicit early-return-with-log. If the branch cost is ever measured to matter, use `if (G_UNLIKELY(!(x))) { fprintf(...); return; }` — a predictable-not-taken branch, not a UB licence. Alternatively make `NV2A_VK_PERF_BUILD` a meson option so `--debug` builds get the abort form.
confirmed.apple_impact: none — identical semantics change on both platforms; the branch is never taken in correct operation, so there is no measurable macOS cost. Can be gated behind a meson option if any doubt remains.
confirmed.verifier_notes: Raised from low to medium because the affected set is larger than the finder listed: besides surface.c:1929 (staging capacity) the DMA bounds/sanity checks at surface.c:2318-2322 and the download-side capacity checks at surface.c:408 and texture.c:1255 are also guest-driven and now UB licences, so a guest- or emulator-bug-induced violation becomes a silent heap overwrite of a 512 MiB VMA mapping instead of a diagnosable abort. Fix: revert the guest-boundary sites (surface.c:408, 1929, 2318-2322; texture.c:1255) to plain assert() exactly as upstream has them (QEMU guarantees assert is live, cost is one predictable branch per surface upload/download, far off the per-draw hot path), keep nv2a_vk_bounds_check only for the table-index sites in draw.c/texture.c where the index is already masked to the table range. Optionally make NV2A_VK_PERF_BUILD follow a meson option (default 1) so --debug builds get the abort form. apple_impact: none (same branch cost on both platforms; never taken in correct operation).

confirmed.title: create_pvideo_image never records pvideo.width/height, so the overlay image, view and sampler are destroyed and recreated on every upload
confirmed.description:
`create_pvideo_image` guards its teardown with `d->pvideo.width != width || d->pvideo.height != height`, but nothing anywhere in the tree ever assigns `d->pvideo.width` or `d->pvideo.height` (grep finds exactly one occurrence of each, the comparison itself). They stay 0, so the condition is always true for any real overlay size: `destroy_pvideo_image` runs and a fresh `vmaCreateImage` + `vkCreateImageView` + `vkCreateSampler` happens on every single PVIDEO upload.

Upstream had the same dormant bug but paid it every frame; the fork's memcmp cache reduced the frequency to once per PVIDEO state change, which is why it has stayed invisible. It matters more once the cache is fixed to be content-aware (see the PVIDEO freeze finding), because the upload then becomes per-frame again and a full VMA image allocation + sampler creation per frame during video playback is a real cost on a native driver — and `vmaDestroyImage` on the previous image relies on the aux fence having retired it, which is a fragile assumption to be making 30 times a second. The mirror hazard is that if anyone ever *does* assign the fields, the unconditional create below the guard would start leaking an image, view, sampler and VmaAllocation per call.
confirmed.proposed_fix: Assign `d->pvideo.width = width; d->pvideo.height = height;` at the end of `create_pvideo_image`, right after the sampler is created. The existing guard then does what it reads as: reuse the image whenever the overlay size is unchanged, and the destroy/recreate (plus its implicit dependence on the aux fence having retired the previous image) only happens on an actual resize.
confirmed.apple_impact: none — identical saving on macOS, where the same per-state-change rebuild happens today. No change to the Metal/IOSurface path, which does not touch the pvideo image.
confirmed.verifier_notes: In hw/xbox/nv2a/pgraph/vk/display.c `create_pvideo_image` (line 476): restructure the guard so that if `d->pvideo.image != VK_NULL_HANDLE && d->pvideo.width == width && d->pvideo.height == height` the function returns early; otherwise call `destroy_pvideo_image(pg)`, create the image/view/sampler, and then set `d->pvideo.width = width; d->pvideo.height = height;`. Do NOT just add the assignments without the early return — the creation code at lines 505-534 is unconditional and would leak an image, view, sampler and VmaAllocation per call. Also reset `width`/`height` to 0 in `destroy_pvideo_image` (line 454) for hygiene, since it is also called from finalize at line 2065. Behaviour is identical on macOS (same generic path; the compositor ring already waits its own fences before reuse), so apple_impact remains 'none'.

confirmed.title: shader_uniform_inputs_dirty enumeration is incomplete: 7 direct writers of VSH uniform inputs never mark dirty, so the new skip-gate serves stale uniforms
confirmed.description:
The fork added `pg->shader_uniform_inputs_dirty` (pgraph.h:286) and gates `update_shader_uniforms()` on it in BOTH renderers (gl/shaders.c:851 `if (binding_changed || pg->shader_uniform_inputs_dirty)`, vk/shaders.c:652). The header comment enumerates the writers as 'pgraph_reg_w, direct writers of ltctxa / ltctxb / ltc1 / vsh_constants, and writers of each vertex_attributes[].inline_value'. That enumeration misses every other PGRAPHState field that pgraph_glsl_set_vsh_uniform_values() reads. Seven method handlers write a live uniform input with no pgraph_mark_uniforms_dirty():

  pgraph.c:2050  SET_MATERIAL_ALPHA             -> pg->material_alpha             -> VshUniform_material_alpha (vsh.c:509)
  pgraph.c:2340  SET_SPECULAR_PARAMS (slot 5)   -> pg->specular_power             -> VshUniform_specularPower (vsh.c:579)
  pgraph.c:2364  SET_POINT_PARAMS               -> pg->point_params[]             -> VshUniform_pointParams (vsh.c:505)
  pgraph.c:2535  SET_LIGHT_INFINITE_HALF_VECTOR -> pg->light_infinite_half_vector -> VshUniform_lightInfiniteHalfVector (vsh.c:549)
  pgraph.c:2540  SET_LIGHT_INFINITE_DIRECTION   -> pg->light_infinite_direction   -> VshUniform_lightInfiniteDirection (vsh.c:558)
  pgraph.c:2559  SET_LIGHT_LOCAL_POSITION       -> pg->light_local_position       -> VshUniform_lightLocalPosition (vsh.c:566)
  pgraph.c:2564  SET_LIGHT_LOCAL_ATTENUATION    -> pg->light_local_attenuation    -> VshUniform_lightLocalAttenuation (vsh.c:574)

The siblings in the very same switch (SET_LIGHT_AMBIENT/DIFFUSE/SPECULAR_COLOR, SET_LIGHT_LOCAL_RANGE, SET_LIGHT_SPOT_FALLOFF/DIRECTION) did get the mark, which is what makes the omission look like an oversight rather than a deliberate exclusion. `pg->surface_binding_dim.{width,height}` (feeds VshUniform_surfaceSize, vsh.c:520) is a weaker fourth case: written directly at gl/surface.c:1203/1238 and vk/surface.c:2468/2540 with no mark, saved today only because a bound-surface shape change normally implies a preceding register write.

Critically, nothing on the renderer side writes PGRAPH registers during a draw: `grep -n 'pgraph_reg_w\|PG_SET_MASK' hw/xbox/nv2a/pgraph/gl/draw.c hw/xbox/nv2a/pgraph/gl/surface.c hw/xbox/nv2a/pgraph/vk/draw.c` returns nothing. So the only thing that can set the dirty bit between two guest draws is a guest register write whose value actually changes (pgraph_reg_w only marks inside `if (pg->regs_[r] != v)`). A guest that moves a light or fades an object between draws without touching any other register gets a stale UBO.
confirmed.proposed_fix: Add `pgraph_mark_uniforms_dirty(pg);` to all seven handlers (pgraph.c:2050, 2340, 2364, 2535, 2540, 2559, 2564) and to the four surface_binding_dim write sites (gl/surface.c:1203/1204/1238/1239, vk/surface.c:2468/2469/2540/2541). confirmed.title: GL texture upload creates and destroys a GThreadPool per upload (6x per cubemap); with levels==1 it is pure cross-thread overhead and zero parallelism
confirmed.description:
The fork rewrote upload_gl_texture() to pre-decode mip levels in parallel. Both branches allocate a fresh GThreadPool on every call and free it (waiting) immediately afterwards: gl/texture.c:570 + :600 (2D / cubemap face) and :673 + :705 (3D). upload_gl_texture is called once per cube face (gl/texture.c:814-824), so one mipmapped cubemap upload creates and tears down six pools.

Three problems, all worse on Windows than on macOS:
1. For the very common s.levels == 1 case there is exactly one task, so the code dispatches the unswizzle to another thread and blocks the PFIFO thread in g_thread_pool_free(pool, FALSE, TRUE) - a full producer/consumer round trip (queue push + condvar wake + condvar wake back) with zero parallelism. That is a net loss of several microseconds per upload versus the upstream inline unswizzle_rect.
2. max_threads = MIN(s.levels, g_get_num_processors()) is up to 8 on the target i7-4770K. GLib's shared (non-exclusive) pool retains only g_thread_pool_get_max_unused_threads() idle threads (default 2), so a deep mip chain forces several real OS thread creations per upload. CreateThread on Win32 with the default 8 MiB stack reserve is far more expensive than pthread_create on Darwin.
3. g_thread_pool_new(..., NULL) discards the GError. If pool creation fails, g_thread_pool_push(NULL, ...) silently drops every task, t->decoded_data stays NULL, and glTexImage2D(..., NULL) uploads undefined texture contents with no diagnostic (release builds also compile out the assert(glGetError()...) guards).

The fork's own Vulkan renderer already does this correctly: r->decode_thread_pool is created once in pgraph_vk_init_textures (vk/texture.c:2609, capped at MIN(nproc, 4)) and freed in pgraph_vk_finalize_textures (:2631). The GL path is the outlier, and Windows reaches it both as the documented triage workaround (docs/windows-gating-audit.md section O, option 2) and as the init_renderer fallback when Vulkan init fails (pgraph.c:635-646).
confirmed.proposed_fix: Hoist a single persistent pool into PGRAPHGLState mirroring the VK renderer: create it in pgraph_gl_init_textures with MIN(g_get_num_processors(), 4) and free it in pgraph_gl_finalize_textures; per upload, push tasks and wait on a per-upload completion counter (GMutex/GCond or an atomic count) instead of creating and freeing the pool. Additionally short-circuit to an inline decode when s.levels == 1 (or when total decoded bytes are below a threshold such as 64 KiB) so small / non-mipmapped textures never pay the handoff. Check the g_thread_pool_new return and fall back to the inline path on NULL instead of uploading NULL pixel data. Gate the change behind a measured savestate A/B per the fork's change-control rules.
confirmed.apple_impact: none - the same pool-per-upload cost exists on macOS today and the fix removes it identically there. The uploaded bytes are byte-identical; only the threading topology changes. No Apple-specific code path is touched.
confirmed.verifier_notes:

Recommended change to hw/xbox/nv2a/pgraph/gl/texture.c: add a persistent `GThreadPool *decode_thread_pool` to PGRAPHGLState, create it in pgraph_gl_init_textures with MIN(g_get_num_processors(), 4) and free it in pgraph_gl_finalize_textures, mirroring vk/texture.c:2609/2631; per upload, push tasks and wait on a per-upload GMutex/GCond completion counter (or atomic count + cond) instead of g_thread_pool_new/g_thread_pool_free. confirmed.title: MoltenVK hardware-depth fallback (use_hw_depth) also fires on native Vulkan drivers for point primitives, replacing an exact depth with a dFdx/dFdy approximation
confirmed.description:
The fork added a use_hw_depth branch to the pixel-shader generator (psh.h:74, psh.c:1001) that replaces upstream's barycentric vtxPos0/1/2 + triMZ depth computation with gl_FragCoord.z * clipRange.y plus a dFdx/dFdy slope estimate. The comment says it exists 'When Geometry Shaders are unavailable (e.g. MoltenVK)'. But the flag is set as key.psh.state.use_hw_depth = !need_geometry_shader (vk/shaders.c:419), where need_geometry_shader = r->supports_geometry_shaders && pgraph_glsl_need_geom(&binding->state.geom) (:391). pgraph_glsl_need_geom() returns false for PRIM_TYPE_POINTS (geom.c:90-91) on every device, so on a native NVIDIA/AMD/Intel Vulkan driver - where supports_geometry_shaders is true - point primitives still take the MoltenVK approximation.

That is a behaviour regression versus upstream on Windows. When no GS is emitted the vertex shader itself writes the varyings the upstream path needs: 'vtxPos0 = vtxPos; vtxPos1 = vtxPos; vtxPos2 = vtxPos; triMZ = 0.0;' (vsh.c:408-411). Upstream's barycentric code then degenerates cleanly (three identical positions, inv_bcsum is inf and is clamped to 0, so zvalue == vtxPos0.z / .w) - i.e. the exact per-point depth. The fork's replacement instead uses the rasterizer's window-space z, which is not the same quantity at all in z_perspective (w-buffer) mode, and adds depthFactor * max(|dFdx|,|dFdy|), which is meaningless for a point. The OpenGL renderer never sets use_hw_depth (memset to 0 in pgraph_glsl_get_shader_state, glsl/shaders.c:30), so GL and Vulkan now disagree on point depth on the same Windows machine.

hw/xbox/nv2a/pgraph/vk/shaders.c:419
      key.psh.state.use_hw_depth = !need_geometry_shader;

hw/xbox/nv2a/pgraph/glsl/geom.c:89-91
      switch (state->primitive_mode) {
      case PRIM_TYPE_POINTS:

                         ...

confirmed.title: nsprof never prints under the OpenGL renderer: nsprof_flip_tick() is only wired into the Vulkan flip path
confirmed.description:
nsprof_flip_tick() is the sole driver of the periodic XEMU_NV2A_NSPROF summary - it increments flips, checks the 5 s interval, prints, and resets every counter. It has exactly one call site in the whole tree: pgraph_vk_flip_stall() at hw/xbox/nv2a/pgraph/vk/renderer.c:241. The GL renderer's flip path never calls it.

Consequence on Windows: whenever the OpenGL renderer is live - the documented triage workaround for the Windows Vulkan black-screen report (docs/windows-gating-audit.md section O, option 2), the init_renderer fallback when Vulkan init fails (pgraph.c:635-646), and the user-selectable renderer - XEMU_NV2A_NSPROF=1 produces no output at all. Counters keep accumulating unbounded and are never reset or reported, so there is no way to distinguish 'profiler off' from 'profiler on, workload has no cost'. Several instrumented buckets are renderer-neutral and do accumulate on GL (NSPROF_FLIP_IDLE via nsprof_flip_wait_begin/end at pgraph.c:1311 and pfifo.c:156, plus the UI-thread buckets), so real data is being collected and silently discarded. This directly undermines profiling PFIFO-thread cost on the new Windows target.
confirmed.proposed_fix: Move the tick to the renderer-neutral flip site so both renderers drive it: call nsprof_flip_tick() from DEF_METHOD(NV097, FLIP_STALL) in hw/xbox/nv2a/pgraph/pgraph.c right after nv2a_profile_flip_stall() (line 1310) and delete the vk/renderer.c:241 call; or, for a smaller diff, add the same call to pgraph_gl_flip_stall(). The pgraph.c site is on the PFIFO thread just like the VK one, so nsprof.h's 'almost all instrumented paths run on the PFIFO thread' assumption still holds.
confirmed.apple_impact: none if the tick moves to pgraph.c FLIP_STALL - it is the same PFIFO-thread call one step earlier in the same method, and macOS runs Vulkan so interval semantics are unchanged. Adding a second call site in gl/renderer.c instead would also be inert on macOS (the GL renderer is not used there under the Metal backend).
confirmed.verifier_notes: Either proposed fix is sound. Preferred: in hw/xbox/nv2a/pgraph/pgraph.c DEF_METHOD(NV097, FLIP_STALL), add `nsprof_flip_tick();` after `nsprof_flip_wait_begin();` (line 1311) and delete `nsprof_flip_tick();` from hw/xbox/nv2a/pgraph/vk/renderer.c:241.
