confirmed.title: PFIFO thread scheduling hint is Apple-only; Windows has no equivalent priority bump on the frame-critical thread
confirmed.description:
Architecture-contract Invariant 12 gives the PFIFO thread (and the vblank thread) QOS_CLASS_USER_INTERACTIVE on macOS, on the reasoning that both are frame-critical and the default scheduling class lets the OS deprioritize them under load. On Windows that bump compiles out entirely (#if defined(__APPLE__)), so on the target machine the PFIFO thread runs at THREAD_PRIORITY_NORMAL in a NORMAL_PRIORITY_CLASS process, competing on equal footing with the vCPU/TCG thread, the vblank pacing thread, the SDL/UI thread, the audio thread and the newly added GL texture-decode pool threads - 6+ runnable threads for 4 physical cores on a 4C/8T Haswell.

This matters more here than on Apple silicon because the Windows scheduler round-robins equal-priority threads on a short client quantum, and because the untimed qemu_cond_wait park (pfifo.c:600) makes every PFIFO wake a scheduler dispatch, so dispatch latency lands directly in guest FIFO latency and in the FLIP_STALL -> vblank gap that NSPROF_FLIP_IDLE measures. The gating audit lists this as A6 ('compiled out; no scheduling change') but only as a correctness verdict - it was never revisited as a perf opportunity now that the tree runs natively on Windows. Neither .claude/skills/xemu-failure-archaeology nor docs/optimizations.md records a failed attempt at a Windows thread-priority bump, so this is open, not a known dead end.
confirmed.proposed_fix: Add a `#elif defined(_WIN32)` arm at pfifo.c:503 calling SetThreadPriority(GetCurrentThread(), THREAD_PRIORITY_ABOVE_NORMAL), and the matching one on the vblank thread in ui/xemu.c, behind an escape hatch (e.g. XEMU_THREAD_PRIO=0) so a regression is bisectable. Predict-then-measure per the fork's research discipline: state the kill threshold before the run and measure with a savestate A/B on this machine reporting mean fps plus XEMU_NV2A_NSPROF's flip_idle per flip (which needs the nsprof GL fix above if the A/B runs on the OpenGL renderer). MMCSS (AvSetMmThreadCharacteristicsW(L"Games", ...)) is the heavier alternative but pulls in avrt.dll and a process-wide scheduling category - try SetThreadPriority first. Do not use TIME_CRITICAL: starving the vCPU thread would trade FIFO latency for guest-CPU throughput.
confirmed.apple_impact: none - the new arm is #elif defined(_WIN32), so the existing #if defined(__APPLE__) QoS bump is untouched and Invariant 12 is preserved verbatim on macOS.
confirmed.verifier_notes: If pursued: add `#elif defined(_WIN32)` arms at hw/xbox/nv2a/pfifo.c:502 and ui/xemu.c:891 calling `SetThreadPriority(GetCurrentThread(), THREAD_PRIORITY_ABOVE_NORMAL)` (include <windows.h> is already available via qemu/osdep.h on Windows), behind an env escape hatch (e.g. XEMU_THREAD_PRIO=0 disables). Keep the existing `#if defined(__APPLE__)` block untouched so Invariant 12 is preserved verbatim. State the kill threshold before measuring (e.g. abandon if mean fps gain < 0.5% on a savestate A/B on the TITAN Xp / i7-4770K machine, using XEMU_NV2A_NSPROF flip_idle as the secondary metric). confirmed.title: NV2A_STRIP_PROFILE_COUNTERS defaults to 1 unconditionally, so the in-app NV2A profiling HUD reads zero in every build including debug
confirmed.description:
The fork stripped the NV2A_PROF_* counters to remove a store per draw. The comment says 'Strip profile counters in release builds', but the default is set unconditionally with no dependence on build type, and nothing in the meson/build files ever defines it to 0 (grep -rn NV2A_STRIP_PROFILE_COUNTERS finds only debug.h). So nv2a_profile_inc_counter(cnt) expands to ((void)0) even in build.sh --debug.

The only consumer is the ImGui debug panel (ui/xui/debug.cc:452 nv2a_profile_get_counter_value(i) and the per-counter PlotLine at :455), which now permanently plots flat zeros for every counter - draws, render passes, pipeline binds, finish reasons, shader/UBO dirty ratios. On the freshly supported Windows target that is the first tool a user or triager reaches for, and it silently lies rather than being visibly absent. (mspf / increment_fps still work - they come from nv2a_profile_flip_stall / nv2a_profile_increment, which are real functions in profile.c.) The macro form also silently discards its argument expression: nv2a_profile_inc_counter(finish_reason_to_counter_enum[finish_reason]) at vk/draw.c:1923 no longer evaluates the array index - harmless today (pure lookup) but a trap for a future call site with a side effect.
confirmed.proposed_fix: Either (a) make the default match the comment so the debug build keeps working HUD counters (define NV2A_STRIP_PROFILE_COUNTERS to 1 only for non-debug builds), or (b) if the counters are meant to be permanently dead, remove or grey out the counter plots in ui/xui/debug.cc so the HUD does not present fabricated zeros, and delete the unreachable nv2a_profile_get_counter_value. In either case prefer a typed no-op over a function-like macro so the argument is still type-checked and evaluated: static inline void nv2a_profile_inc_counter(enum NV2A_PROF_COUNTERS_ENUM cnt) { (void)cnt; }
confirmed.apple_impact: none for option (b). For option (a) the debug macOS build regains the per-draw counter store it had before the strip - the intended debug-build cost; macOS release builds are unaffected either way.
confirmed.verifier_notes:
Minimal, zero-risk-to-macOS-release fix in hw/xbox/nv2a/debug.h:151-153: make the default track the build type, e.g.
```
#ifndef NV2A_STRIP_PROFILE_COUNTERS
#  ifdef XEMU_DEBUG_BUILD
#    define NV2A_STRIP_PROFILE_COUNTERS 0
#  else
#    define NV2A_STRIP_PROFILE_COUNTERS 1
#  endif
#endif
```
(XEMU_DEBUG_BUILD is already what build.sh --debug passes via build_cflags at build.sh:492, and it lands in --extra-cflags at :814, so it reaches every TU.) Replace the function-like macro in the stripped branch with a typed no-op so the argument is still type-checked/evaluated: `static inline void nv2a_profile_inc_counter(enum NV2A_PROF_COUNTERS_ENUM cnt) { (void)cnt; }` -- at -O2/-O3 this compiles to nothing on both gcc (MSYS2) and clang (Xcode), so the release hot path is unchanged. Also fix the nsprof.h:4-5 comment if the semantics change. Optionally, if you prefer to keep counters permanently dead, instead gate the `for (int i = 0; i < NV2A_PROF__COUNT; i++)` loop at ui/xui/debug.cc:447 behind `#if !NV2A_STRIP_PROFILE_COUNTERS` (debug.h is already included there via the `extern "C"` block) so the HUD stops plotting zeros. apple_impact: none for release builds either way; option (a) restores the per-draw counter store only in macOS --debug builds, which is the intended debug-build cost.

confirmed.title: Sub-page arm (b) inline NOTDIRTY store-skip has no i386 emitter, so Windows x86_64 forfeits the whole measured +12% draws/s win (the arm-(a) bitmap it needs is already default-on there)
confirmed.description:
The fork ships two sub-page arms. Arm (a) — the O(1) code-block bitmap consult that skips whole-page invalidation in tb_invalidate_phys_range_fast — is host-agnostic C in accel/tcg/tb-maint.c and is default-ON on Windows (`xemu_subpage_dirty_on()` at tb-maint.c:396-408 defaults 1 unless XEMU_SUBPAGE_DIRTY=0). Arm (b) — 'subpage-fast', the inline pre-filter at the head of the store slow-path stub that completes an eligible guest store entirely inline, skipping the ~300 ns notdirty_write round trip — exists only as an AArch64 emitter (tcg/aarch64/tcg-target.c.inc:1748-1935, `sf_out_store_prefilter`). `xemu_subpage_fast_mode()` is called from exactly one place in the tree (tcg/aarch64/tcg-target.c.inc:1941), so on an x86_64 host the function is never invoked, `xemu_sf_init()` never runs, `xemu_sf_block_map` stays NULL, and both `xemu_sf_sync_page()` / `xemu_sf_clear_all()` degrade to their NULL guards. Setting XEMU_SUBPAGE_FAST=1 on Windows does nothing at all — a user-visible knob that silently no-ops.

The measured Apple payoff (+12% draws/s, 6/6 interleaved pairs, ~2M eligible stores/s completed inline) came from renderer-watched guest pages, which is a property of the guest workload and the NV2A dirty-tracking design, not of the host ISA — so a comparable win should be available on the Windows x86_64 target. The i386 backend's ldst slow-path label machinery (`tcg_out_qemu_st_slow_path` / TCGLabelQemuLdst) is structurally analogous, and the pre-filter is pure integer work (TLB comparator test, a bitmap word AND, four dirty-bitmap bit tests, then the direct store), so it ports without any AArch64-specific dependency other than register-pool selection.
confirmed.proposed_fix: Port `sf_out_store_prefilter` to tcg/i386/tcg-target.c.inc's `tcg_out_qemu_st_slow_path`, reusing the existing platform-neutral state (xemu_sf_block_map / xemu_sf_ram_host / xemu_sf_ram_pages / xemu_sf_dirty0 in include/exec/xemu-subpage-fast.h) and the existing C refuter (xemu_sf_refute_st{b,w,l,q} + xemu_sf_ground_truth). Land it default-OFF on non-Apple with XEMU_SUBPAGE_FAST=1 as the opt-in, run the refuter soak (XEMU_SUBPAGE_FAST_REFUTE=1) to 0 violations on the Windows box first, then A/B before flipping the default. As a much cheaper interim step, make the knob honest: warn once at startup if XEMU_SUBPAGE_FAST=1 is set on a host with no emitter, instead of silently doing nothing.
confirmed.apple_impact: none — Apple keeps its existing default-on AArch64 stub untouched; the new i386 emitter is compiled only on x86_64 hosts and would land default-off there.

The pre-filter must therefore (1) load `addr_write` from `[L0 + offsetof(CPUTLBEntry, addr_write)]`, XOR with L1, `cmp $TLB_NOTDIRTY`,  …[truncated; full text in the session workflow journal]

confirmed.title: xemu_inv_ticks() returns a constant 0 on x86_64 hosts, so XEMU_INV_TIMING prints an all-zero notdirty_write timing report on Windows
confirmed.description:
The tick source used by the (b'') notdirty_write body-timing split has only two real implementations: aarch64 (cntvct_el0) and Apple (clock_gettime_nsec_np). Everything else — including the MSYS2 x86_64 Windows target and x86_64 Linux — falls through to `return 0;`. Enabling XEMU_INV_TIMING=1 on the Windows box therefore produces a report where total/inval/rest are all 0.000 ms and 0.0 ns/call, and the self-calibration loop in tb-maint.c's dump (`for (i = 0; i < 4096; i++) { a = xemu_inv_ticks(); b = xemu_inv_ticks(); ... }`) settles on read-pair-floor=0. It does not crash or divide by zero (every consumer guards on xemu_nd_calls / xemu_nd_ticks_total), but the diagnostic that sized the entire sub-page campaign is unusable on the one machine that can now actually run the x86_64 build — which matters because deciding whether to port arm (b) to i386 (see the separate finding) requires exactly this measurement.

x86_64 has a trivially available, lower-overhead source than the Apple one already used: `__rdtsc()` (or `__builtin_ia32_rdtsc()`), available in MinGW-w64 GCC via <x86intrin.h>, with invariant TSC on Haswell.
confirmed.proposed_fix: Add an `#elif defined(__x86_64__) || defined(__i386__)` arm returning `__builtin_ia32_rdtsc()` (with `__asm__ volatile("lfence")` before it to match the `isb` ordering intent), and extend xemu_inv_tick_ns() with a matching x86 arm that calibrates ns/tick once against g_get_monotonic_time() (e.g. a 10 ms spin at first call, cached in a static double) instead of returning 1.0. Both are diagnostic-only paths behind XEMU_INV_TIMING, so there is no production risk.
confirmed.apple_impact: none — the `__aarch64__` arm is checked first and is unchanged; Apple Silicon keeps cntvct_el0.
confirmed.verifier_notes: In accel/tcg/xemu-inv-prof.h add an x86 arm between the `__aarch64__` and `__APPLE__` cases (or after `__APPLE__`, since Apple x86_64 would otherwise take rdtsc — either order is fine, but keep `__aarch64__` first so Apple Silicon is untouched): `#elif defined(__x86_64__) || defined(__i386__)` returning `__builtin_ia32_rdtsc()` (no header needed with GCC/Clang; optionally `__asm__ volatile("lfence" ::: "memory")` before it to mirror the isb intent). In xemu_inv_tick_ns() add a matching arm that calibrates once: spin ~10 ms against g_get_monotonic_time() (QPC-backed on Windows, fine resolution) and cache ns/tick in a static double; return that instead of 1.0. Also fix the stale comment at lines 54-55 ("Elsewhere fall back to the RAW uptime clock") to describe the actual fallbacks. Zero production risk: only reached when XEMU_INV_TIMING=1. apple_impact: none (aarch64 arm unchanged; Apple x86_64 is not a supported target of this fork but would still be correct with either ordering). Temper expectations per archaeology 1497-1503: this makes the Windows report populated, not necessarily decisive.

confirmed.title: temp_load's new F32/F64 constant materialization moves GPR->XMM via TCG_TYPE_I32/I64, which the i386 backend encodes with VEX (requires AVX1) instead of the plain SSE2 encoding available under TCG_TYPE_F32/F64
confirmed.description:
The fork replaced upstream's `assert(0); /* FIXME */` for FP constants in temp_load with a materialize-in-GPR-then-cross-class-move sequence, and the comment states it was written against the AArch64 backend ("use I32 type which handles the GPR(src < 32) -> Vreg(dst >= 32) case in tcg_out_mov via the INS instruction path"). On the i386 backend the two type choices are not equivalent:

  - `tcg_out_mov(s, TCG_TYPE_I32, xmm, gpr)` takes the `case TCG_TYPE_I32:` arm at tcg/i386/tcg-target.c.inc:957-971 and emits `tcg_out_vex_modrm(s, OPC_MOVD_VyEy + rexw, ...)` — a **VEX-encoded** VMOVD/VMOVQ, which #UDs on a host without AVX1.
  - `tcg_out_mov(s, TCG_TYPE_F32/F64, xmm, gpr)` takes the `case TCG_TYPE_F32:` arm at :972-985 and emits `tcg_out_modrm(s, OPC_MOVD_VyEy + rexw, ...)` — the legacy SSE2 encoding, which the backend already advertises unconditionally (`tcg_target_available_regs[TCG_TYPE_F32] = ALL_VECTOR_REGS;` at :5213 is NOT guarded by have_avx1, unlike the V64/V128 sets at :5215-5217).

On the stated target (i7-4770K, AVX2, built with -Dx86_version=3) this is benign — VMOVD executes fine. It matters for (a) a pre-AVX x86_64 host running a baseline `-Dx86_version=1` build, where hard_fpu is default-on (`g_use_hard_fpu = g_config.perf.hard_fpu` under `#if defined(XBOX) && (defined(__x86_64__) || defined(__aarch64__))`, translate.c:5353-5356) and this path would emit an illegal instruction, and (b) as a latent inconsistency: every other FP move in the backend already uses the F32/F64 arm. Reachability is narrow (the i386 frontend materializes FP constants via `tcg_constant_i32/i64` + mov32i_f32, translate.c:1735-1742, so this only fires if optimize.c constant-folds an FP temp), which is why this is low and not higher.
confirmed.proposed_fix: Change both cross-class moves to use the FP type rather than the integer type: `tcg_out_mov(s, TCG_TYPE_F32, reg, tmp)` and `tcg_out_mov(s, TCG_TYPE_F64, reg, tmp)`. AArch64's tcg_out_mov handles TCG_TYPE_F32/F64 with the same INS path (tcg/aarch64/tcg-target.c.inc:1337-1367), so the AArch64 codegen is byte-identical; i386 gains the SSE2 encoding. While there, add `tcg_debug_assert(reg >= 16)` to document the destination-class expectation.
confirmed.apple_impact: none — AArch64's tcg_out_mov reaches the same INS lowering for TCG_TYPE_F32/F64 as it does for TCG_TYPE_I32/I64, so emitted Apple Silicon code is unchanged.
confirmed.verifier_notes: Apply the proposed one-line-each change in tcg/tcg.c:5113 and :5121: `tcg_out_mov(s, TCG_TYPE_F32, reg, tmp)` and `tcg_out_mov(s, TCG_TYPE_F64, reg, tmp)`, and fix the two comments (they reference the AArch64 INS path; the F-type arm uses FMOV on AArch64 and legacy MOVD/MOVQ on i386). Adding `tcg_debug_assert(reg >= 16)` is i386-specific (AArch64 vector regs start at 32), so if added it should be expressed portably or omitted. Optionally note in the commit that no F32/F64 TEMP_CONST creator exists in the tree today, so this is hardening of a currently-unreachable path; if anyone later adds FP constant folding to optimize.c, this path becomes live and the SSE2 encoding matters for -Dx86_version=1 (debug) builds on pre-AVX hosts. Apple: emitted code changes INS -> FMOV Sd,Wn / FMOV Dd,Xn, functionally identical for scalar FP; no gating needed.

confirmed.title: Inline jump-cache probe hardcodes a 16-byte CPUJumpCache entry stride with no build-time assert
confirmed.description: The inline jump-cache probe — which the file's own header comment declares is 'the sole owner of the cache layout' — computes the entry address as `hash << 4`, i.e. it bakes `sizeof(CPUJumpCache::array[0]) == 16` into generated code. That holds today on every 64-bit host (`TranslationBlock *tb` 8 bytes + `vaddr pc` 8 bytes, accel/tcg/tb-jmp-cache.h:26-30), and it is correct on the MinGW-w64 x86_64 target. But it is asserted nowhere: if `vaddr` narrows, a field is added, or a 32-bit host is ever built, the probe silently reads adjacent entries and dispatches to a TB with the wrong pc/flags. Every other layout dependency in the same function is expressed with `offsetof(...)` and therefore self-maintaining; only the stride is a magic number. This is a latent-corruption trap, not a live bug.
confirmed.proposed_fix: Add `QEMU_BUILD_BUG_ON(sizeof(((CPUJumpCache *)0)->array[0]) != 16);` at the top of tcg_gen_xemu_jc_probe_and_goto_ptr (or replace the literal 4 with a shift derived from the sizeof so the two can never disagree).
confirmed.apple_impact: none — a compile-time assertion only; no emitted code changes on any host.
confirmed.verifier_notes:
In tcg_gen_xemu_jc_probe_and_goto_ptr (accel/tcg/xemu-inline-jc.c, top of the function or file-scope after the includes), add:
    QEMU_BUILD_BUG_ON(sizeof(((CPUJumpCache *)0)->array[0]) != 16);
    QEMU_BUILD_BUG_ON(sizeof(vaddr) != 8);   /* line 69/72 load+compare pc as i64 */
Alternatively derive the shift: `tcg_gen_shli_i32(h, h, ctz32(sizeof(((CPUJumpCache *)0)->array[0])));` together with `QEMU_BUILD_BUG_ON(!is_power_of_2(sizeof(((CPUJumpCache *)0)->array[0])));`. Compile-time only; no emitted-code change on any host, so apple_impact is none.

confirmed.title: Windows longjmp restores MXCSR, leaving gen_flcr's cached_fpuc_rc stale: inline x87 silently runs with the wrong rounding mode
confirmed.description: The fork replaced upstream's unconditional per-x87-region LDMXCSR with a cached one: gen_flcr loads env->cached_fpuc_rc, compares it against the TB-constant RC bits and skips the ldmxcsr on a hit (translate.c:1774-1815). The cache is invalidated only in cpu_set_fpuc() (cpu.h:2896), x86_cpu_reset_hold() (cpu.c:8738) and the aarch64 SSE bracket. On Windows, sigsetjmp/siglongjmp are macro-mapped to setjmp/longjmp (include/system/os-win32.h:88-90), and the Win64 _JUMP_BUFFER carries MxCsr + FpCsr, so longjmp RESTORES the host MXCSR. Every cpu_loop_exit() (accel/tcg/cpu-exec-common.c:89 -- taken on every guest exception and every hardware interrupt injection) therefore reverts MXCSR to the value captured at the sigsetjmp in cpu_exec_setjmp (accel/tcg/cpu-exec.c:1551) while env->cached_fpuc_rc still claims the guest RC is programmed. The next x87 TB's gen_flcr compare hits and skips the ldmxcsr, so all subsequent inline x87 arithmetic (ADDSD/MULSD/DIVSD/SQRTSD) and every FIST/FISTP (CVTSD2SI, MXCSR-rounded) run under the stale rounding mode -- for the whole remaining RC epoch, i.e. until the guest issues another FLDCW. A title that sets RC=3 (truncate) once at startup (the MSVC _ftol / XDK idiom) gets round-to-nearest float->int conversions permanently after the first interrupt. Upstream xemu is immune because its gen_flcr re-emits the ldmxcsr unconditionally; this is a fork-introduced Windows regression. Apple Silicon is unaffected (Darwin arm64 setjmp does not save FPCR); Darwin x86_64 setjmp does save mxcsr/fpcw, so Intel macOS has the same hole.
confirmed.proposed_fix: Invalidate the cache on the longjmp-return path, where the host register was clobbered behind TCG's back: in accel/tcg/cpu-exec.c:1551-1553 (and cpu_exec_step_atomic at :1033), after `if (unlikely(sigsetjmp(cpu->jmp_env, 0) != 0)) { cpu_exec_longjmp_cleanup(cpu); ... }`, add an XBOX-gated `cpu_env(cpu)->cached_fpuc_rc = 0xFFFF;` (one store per longjmp, forces exactly one extra ldmxcsr in the next x87 region). Doing it unconditionally is simplest and correct on every host; if you prefer to keep it host-scoped, `#if defined(_WIN32) || (defined(__APPLE__) && defined(__x86_64__))` covers the two setjmp implementations that save MXCSR. Do NOT fix it by dropping the cache -- the cache is the perf win.
confirmed.apple_impact: None on Apple Silicon: Darwin arm64 setjmp does not save FPCR, so the extra invalidation only costs one redundant `msr fpcr` per longjmp (unmeasurable). Intel macOS gets the same correctness fix. No macOS behaviour regresses either way.
confirmed.verifier_notes:
Invalidate the RC cache wherever a host longjmp may have restored MXCSR behind TCG's back: in accel/tcg/cpu-exec.c cpu_exec_setjmp (:1551) inside the `sigsetjmp(...) != 0` branch (after cpu_exec_longjmp_cleanup), and in cpu_exec_step_atomic (:1033) on the non-zero return path, add an XBOX-gated `cpu_env(cpu)->cached_fpuc_rc = 0xFFFF;` (target/i386-only field, so guard with the existing XBOX/i386 build gating or add a tiny tcg_ops hook). Doing it unconditionally is correct on every host and costs one 16-bit store per longjmp plus one extra LDMXCSR in the next x87 region; if host-scoping is preferred, `#if defined(_WIN32) || (defined(__APPLE__) && defined(__x86_64__))` covers the setjmp implementations known to save MXCSR. Keep the cache (it is the perf win over upstream's unconditional ldmxcsr). Alternative equivalent fix: re-arm the cache in cpu_exec_longjmp_cleanup itself. Optionally correct the finding text: hardware IRQs do not longjmp; FXRSTOR also heals; HLT/guest faults are the real triggers. Apple Silicon impact: none (Darwin arm64 setjmp does not save FPCR; the extra invalidation adds one redundant msr fpcr per longjmp). | The proposed fix direction is right (invalidate the cache where the host register was clobbered behind TCG's back; do NOT drop the cache). Improvements:

1. Put the store in ONE place, `cpu_exec_longjmp_cleanup()` (`accel/tcg/cpu-exec.c:991`), rather than at both sigsetjmp sites — it is already the shared landing routine for `cpu_exec_setjmp` (:1552 …[truncated; full text in the session workflow journal]

confirmed.title: The 2026-08-09 x86_64 FIST/FRNDINT directed-rounding fallback is a no-op: it calls the *hard* helper, which is itself RC-blind on x86_64
confirmed.description: gen_fistl_ST0 / gen_fistll_ST0 / gen_fist_ST0 fall back to `gen_helper_fistl_ST0(arg, tcg_env)` for RC 1 (-inf) and RC 2 (+inf) on non-aarch64 hosts, and gen_frndint falls back to `gen_helper_frndint(tcg_env)` for any RC != 0; the comments say the fallback 'honours the guest RC'. But gen_helper_fistl_ST0 / gen_helper_frndint are macro-remapped at translate.c:54/117 to MAP_GEN_HELPER_SOFT_HARD(...), which selects the __hard variant whenever g_use_hard_fpu is set (perf.hard_fpu defaults true). helper_fistl_ST0__hard calls floatx80_to_int32() which the fork #defines to floatx80_to_int32__hard (fpu_helper.c:407), implemented on x86_64 as `(int32_t)llrintl(a.fval)` (fpu_helper.c:185); helper_frndint__hard uses `rintl(a.fval)` (fpu_helper.c:179). Both honour the host x87 control word's RC field -- and nothing in the tree ever programs it on an x86_64 host: the only fesetround() call (fpu_helper.c:1186) is inside `#if defined(XBOX) && defined(__aarch64__)`. So on Windows x86_64 the 'fixed' RC 1/2 FIST and RC != 0 FRNDINT paths still round to nearest, and additionally pay a helper call for it. The fix that landed is effective only on aarch64.
confirmed.proposed_fix: Two options, in preference order. (a) Preferred, and it also removes the fallback entirely: on x86_64 gen_flcr already programs MXCSR bits 14:13 with the guest RC (same encoding as the x87 CW), so a bare CVTSD2SI/CVTSS2SI implements FIST for all four modes -- drop the `rc == 1 || rc == 2` helper fallbacks in gen_fistl_ST0/gen_fistll_ST0/gen_fist_ST0 for `defined(__x86_64__)` and let ops_fpu.h emit `tcg_gen_cvt_f{32,64}_i{32,64}` unconditionally (see the companion perf finding). (b) If a helper fallback is kept, call the soft helper explicitly (`gen_helper_fistl_ST0__soft(arg, tcg_env)` / `gen_helper_frndint__soft(tcg_env)`), which honours env->fp_status's rounding mode set by update_fp_status(). For FRNDINT specifically, (b) is the cheap fix; alternatively extend set_x86_rounding_mode's fesetround call to `defined(__x86_64__)` too -- on mingw fesetround programs both the x87 CW and MXCSR RC, and cpu_set_fpuc already sets cached_fpuc_rc = 0xFFFF so gen_flcr re-fires and the MXCSR side-effect is harmless.
confirmed.apple_impact: None on Apple Silicon: every proposed edit is inside `#if !defined(__aarch64__)` / `defined(__x86_64__)` and the aarch64 FCVTMS/FCVTPS inline path is untouched. Intel macOS gets the same correctness fix.
confirmed.verifier_notes:
Minimal, zero-Apple-impact fix (all edits inside existing `#if !defined(__aarch64__)` blocks in target/i386/tcg/translate.c):
- gen_frndint (translate.c:2216-2218): replace `gen_helper_frndint(tcg_env)` with `gen_helper_frndint__soft(tcg_env)` so the fallback really uses env->fp_status's rounding mode (set by update_fp_status via cpu_set_fpuc). The soft helper reads ST0 as floatx80 high/low, which on x86_64 is bit-identical to the `.fval` long double overlay, and the helper call already forces gen_flush_fp so inline f64 state is spilled via st80f first.
- FIST family (translate.c:2101-2104, 2113-2116, 2135-2138): preferred for x86_64 — drop the RC 1/2 helper fallback and let ops_fpu.h emit the plain `tcg_gen_cvt_f{32,64}_i{32,64}` for every RC (gen_flcr already programs MXCSR RC 14:13 with the guest RC and the backend emits CVTSD2SI/CVTSS2SI, which round per MXCSR). If you keep a fallback, use `gen_helper_fist{,l,ll}_ST0__soft` explicitly.
- Alternative for the helper-based hard FPU as a whole: extend fpu_helper.c:1186 to `#if defined(XBOX) && (defined(__aarch64__) || defined(__x86_64__))` so set_x86_rounding_mode also calls fesetround on x86_64 (mingw-w64's fesetround programs both the x87 CW and MXCSR). This also fixes rintl/llrintl-based hard helpers used when g_use_hard_fpu_inline is off, but it changes host libm rounding for other long-double hard helpers (sinl/cosl etc.) — desirable semantically but needs the =2 differential run on x86_64 before landing. cached_fpuc_rc  …[truncated; full text in the session workflow journal]

confirmed.title: perf: every RC=0 FIST/FISTP emits an x87 FRNDINT memory round-trip on x86_64 where a single CVTSD2SI would do
confirmed.description: For the common RC=0 case ops_fpu.h emits tcg_gen_cvt_rn_i32_f{32,64}. TCG_TARGET_HAS_rint_cvt is 0 for the i386 backend and INDEX_op_cvt_rn_* is gated on it (tcg/tcg.c:2673-2690), so DEFINE_CVT_MODE falls through to tcg_gen_rint_cvt_i32_f64, which expands to `rint` + `cvt64f_i32` (tcg/tcg-op-fp.c:232-241). The i386 backend lowers INDEX_op_rint_f64 to an x87 round-trip: movq [rsp-0x10],xmm / fld qword [rsp-0x10] / frndint / fstp qword [rsp-0x10] / movq xmm,[rsp-0x10] (tcg/i386/tcg-target.c:3255-3266 + tcg_out_fld_xmm/tcg_out_fstp_xmm at :2744/:2758), followed by cvtsd2si. That is 6 host instructions, two store-forwarding round-trips and a microcoded FRNDINT (~11 uops on Haswell) per guest FIST. But gen_flcr has already programmed MXCSR bits 14:13 with the guest RC (translate.c:1811, value `(rc<<13)|0x1f80`), and MXCSR RC uses the identical 2-bit encoding as the x87 CW RC field, so CVTSD2SI *alone* is exactly FIST for all four rounding modes -- including out-of-range, where both forms produce the 0x80000000 integer indefinite. FIST/FISTP is one of the hottest x87 opcodes in Xbox title code (float->int for every index/coordinate/loop bound).
confirmed.proposed_fix: In target/i386/ops_fpu.h gen_fistl_ST0 / gen_fistll_ST0, guard the RC switch with `#if defined(__aarch64__)` and on other hosts emit the plain `glue(glue(tcg_gen_cvt, PRECf), _i{32,64})(arg, get_st0(s))` for every RC -- gen_flcr has already put the guest RC in MXCSR. Then delete the `rc == 1 || rc == 2` helper fallbacks in translate.c:2097/2110/2132 (they become both unnecessary and, per the companion finding, wrong). Leave the FISTTP wrappers (translate.c:2156-2183) on the helper path: FISTTP must truncate regardless of MXCSR, and the Xbox's Pentium III has no SSE3 so the guest never executes it. Validate with the existing XEMU_X87_REFUTE/census harness plus an A/B on the F8 savestate.

confirmed.title: x86_64 SSE host-FP bracket omits the cached_fpuc_rc invalidation its aarch64 twin has, but on x86_64 the inline x87 path is MXCSR-based too
confirmed.description: The aarch64 xemu_hostfp_enter() sets `env->cached_fpuc_rc = 0xFFFF` whenever it rewrites FPCR (fpu_helper.c:3872), because on aarch64 the NEON SSE fast path and the inline x87 share one FPCR. The x86_64 branch (fpu_helper.c:3904-3921) has no such store. docs/windows-gating-audit.md F2 justifies that with 'x86_64 writes MXCSR -- a separate register from the x87 control word -- so no leak is possible there'. That justification is wrong for the x86_64 *inline* path: TCG_TARGET_HAS_fpu is 1 on x86_64 (tcg/i386/tcg-target-has.h:34), so g_use_hard_fpu_inline is on (translate.c:5355) and the inline x87 is SSE/MXCSR-based -- gen_flcr writes MXCSR (translate.c:1811) and add/sub/mul/div/sqrt/cvt lower to ADDSD/MULSD/DIVSD/SQRTSD/CVTSD2SI. xemu_hostfp_enter clears MXCSR.RC and ORs in the guest's FTZ/DAZ, and xemu_hostfp_leave_lazy() deliberately does NOT restore it in mode 1. So after one SSE helper, MXCSR carries FZ/DAZ and RC=0 while cached_fpuc_rc still records the guest x87 RC; the next gen_flcr compare hits and skips the ldmxcsr, and inline x87 then runs with denormal flushing and the wrong rounding. Latent today because XEMU_SSE_HOST defaults to 0 on x86_64, but it is a live landmine for anyone flipping the knob on the Windows box and it invalidates the F2 audit row.

confirmed.title: hard floatx80_to_int32/int64 never raise float_flag_invalid, so FIST's integer-indefinite substitution is dead code and out-of-range conversions wrap
confirmed.description: The fork newly redirects floatx80_to_int32 / floatx80_to_int32_round_to_zero / floatx80_to_int64 to __hard implementations (fpu_helper.c:407-409; upstream's hard build kept the softfloat versions for these). The x86_64 implementation is `(int32_t)llrintl(a.fval)` and the aarch64 one `(int32_t)llrint(d)`. Neither writes env->fp_status's exception flags, so helper_fistl_ST0's `if (get_float_exception_flags(&env->fp_status) & float_flag_invalid) val = 0x80000000;` (fpu_helper.c:810-821) can never fire in the hard build, and helper_fist_ST0's int16 range check gets a wrapped input. Real x87 stores the integer indefinite (0x80000000 / 0x8000000000000000) and raises #IA on an out-of-range FIST; the hard path silently stores a wrapped value. Measured on this machine: `(int32_t)llrintl(1e10L)` = 1410065408 and `(int32_t)llrintl(1e30L)` = 0, where the guest expects 0x80000000 in both cases. Guests do hit this (unclamped float->int on a NaN or an overflowing coordinate), and the wrapped value is far more damaging than the saturating indefinite.
confirmed.proposed_fix: Range-check inside the __hard converters and set the flag, e.g. `long long v = llrintl(a.fval); if (v < INT32_MIN || v > INT32_MAX || !(a.fval == a.fval)) { float_raise(float_flag_invalid, status); return INT32_MIN; } return (int32_t)v;` (and the int64 analogue against the llrintl overflow sentinel). Keep it branch-predictable -- the check is a compare pair on an already-loaded value. Alternatively drop the three #defines and let softfloat handle to_int32/to_int64 (correct but ~20x slower per conversion); the range-check version is the better trade.
confirmed.apple_impact: Gated by nothing today, so the same fix applies on aarch64 -- but behaviour only changes for inputs whose current result is already wrong (out of int32/int64 range or NaN). In-range conversions, which are ~all of them, produce byte-identical results, so no macOS perf or numeric regression on the hot path. If you want zero Apple delta, wrap the new check in `#if !defined(__aarch64__)` and land the aarch64 half after a refuter soak.
confirmed.verifier_notes: Keep the finder's shape: range-check inside the __hard converters and return the x87 integer indefinite. For int32 on both arches: `long long v = llrint[l](x); if (unlikely(v != (long long)(int32_t)v || x != x)) { float_raise(float_flag_invalid, status); return INT32_MIN; } return (int32_t)v;`. confirmed.description: xemu_sse_neon_mode() defaults to 1 only under `#if defined(__aarch64__)`; every other host gets `mode = 0` unless XEMU_SSE_HOST is set explicitly. The Haswell target has SSE2/AVX2, so the vector path is free. Two prerequisites: (a) the missing cached_fpuc_rc invalidation in the x86_64 bracket (separate finding) must land first, otherwise enabling the knob corrupts inline x87 rounding/denormals; (b) a clean XEMU_SSE_HOST=2 differential soak on this machine is the fork's own stated gate.

confirmed.title: Guest-controlled voice handle indexes the host filters[] array out of bounds (wild read, then wild write)
confirmed.description:
The fork rewrote voice_get_mask / voice_get_word / voice_set_mask to first consult a per-voice stack snapshot pointer, `d->vp.filters[voice_handle].voice_buf`. `voice_handle` is a raw 16-bit guest value and is never bounds-checked, but `filters[]` has only MCPX_HW_MAX_VOICES == 256 entries (vp/vp.h:89, apu_regs.h:330). Upstream used the handle only for guest-RAM addressing (`ldl_le_phys(VPVADDR + handle*NV_PAVS_SIZE)`), which is safe for any 16-bit value; the fork turned it into a host array index.

Two guest-reachable vectors:
(a) MMIO. fe_method stores the raw 32-bit argument: `case NV1BA0_PIO_SET_CURRENT_VOICE: qatomic_set(&d->regs[NV_PAPU_FECV], argument);` (vp.c:565-567). Any following `NV1BA0_PIO_SET_VOICE_CFG_VBIN` / `_FMT` / `_ENV*` / `_TAR_*` case then does `voice_set_mask(d, qatomic_read(&d->regs[NV_PAPU_FECV]), ...)` (vp.c:568-600) with no assert — unlike the VOICE_ON path, which is protected by `assert(v < MCPX_HW_MAX_VOICES)` inside is_voice_locked (vp.c:390).
(b) Voice-list walk. mcpx_apu_vp_frame reads the NEXT_VOICE_HANDLE link straight out of guest RAM and feeds it back into voice_get_mask with only a loop-iteration guard, never a value guard (vp.c:2275-2287).

voice_set_mask does not merely read the OOB slot — it dereferences and *writes* through whatever pointer-sized garbage it finds there: `stl_le_p(&buf[offset / 4], new_val);` (vp.c:347). filters[65535] is roughly 90 MB past a ~360 KB array, so the usual outcome is an access violation, but a mapped hit is an arbitrary 4-byte host write.
confirmed.proposed_fix: Add a single guard helper used by all three accessors, e.g. `static inline uint32_t *voice_snapshot(MCPXAPUState *d, uint16_t h) { return h < MCPX_HW_MAX_VOICES ? d->vp.filters[h].voice_buf : NULL; }` and call it in voice_get_mask (vp.c:283), voice_get_word (vp.c:310) and voice_set_mask (vp.c:329). Out-of-range handles then fall through to the existing ram_ldl/ram_stl path, which is exactly upstream's behaviour. Optionally also mask FECV in fe_method (`argument & NV1BA0_PIO_VOICE_ON_HANDLE`) for symmetry with the VOICE_ON path.
confirmed.apple_impact: none — for every in-range handle (all handles a well-behaved title produces) the generated code and the values returned are identical; only the out-of-range path changes, and it changes from UB to upstream semantics.

confirmed.title: Pitch LUT truncates the envelope-modulated pitch and wraps at the int16 boundary, giving a ~2^16 wrong resample rate
confirmed.description:
The fork replaced upstream's `float rate = 1.0 / powf(2.0f, (p + ps * 32 * ef_value) / 4096.0f);` with a 65536-entry LUT keyed on `(uint16_t)(int)(p + ps*32*ef_value)`. `g_pitch_lut[i]` is built as `1.0f / powf(2.0f, (int16_t)i / 4096.0f)` (vp.c:220-226), so the index is interpreted as a signed 16-bit quantity.

Two divergences from upstream:
1. Truncation. `ef_value` is a continuous float in [0,1] and `ps` is int8, so `ps * 32 * ef_value` is fractional; casting to int discards it. The pitch envelope is now quantised to 1/4096-octave steps instead of being continuous — a stair-stepped pitch sweep rather than a smooth one.
2. Wraparound. `p` is int16 (max 32767) and `ps*32*ef_value` reaches +4064, so the sum reaches 36831, which is outside int16. `(uint16_t)36831 == 36831`, and the LUT reinterprets that as `(int16_t)36831 == -28705`, i.e. it returns `1/2^-7.008 == 128.5` where the true value is `1/2^8.99 == 0.00198` — a factor of ~65000 in the resample rate. Symmetrically at the negative end. A voice hitting that corner plays at a completely wrong pitch and drives voice_resample/voice_get_samples at an absurd consumption rate.

Platform-neutral (affects macOS identically), but it is a fork-introduced behaviour change in the audio hot path and cheap to close.
confirmed.proposed_fix: Clamp before the cast: `int pitch_idx = (int)lrintf(fminf(fmaxf(p + ps * 32.0f * ef_value, -32768.0f), 32767.0f));` — that alone removes the sign-flip. To also recover the fractional modulation, interpolate the LUT the same way env_lut_lookup already does (`idx`, `idx+1`, `frac`), which costs one extra load and an FMA and is still far cheaper than the original powf.
confirmed.apple_impact: none for the clamp (in-range indices are untouched); adding LUT interpolation makes macOS marginally *more* faithful to upstream than today, with no measurable cost on the ~20%-utilised APU thread.

confirmed.title: ram_stl / ram_stb bypass invalidate_and_set_dirty, so APU guest-RAM writes no longer set the NV2A / NV2A_TEX / CODE dirty bits
confirmed.description:
The fork replaced `stl_le_phys` / `stb_phys` in the VP with direct writes into `d->ram_ptr`. The QEMU helpers route through `invalidate_and_set_dirty()`, which calls `tb_invalidate_phys_range()` and `cpu_physical_memory_set_dirty_range(..., DIRTY_CLIENTS_NOCODE)`; the direct write does neither. xemu defines extra dirty clients on RAM specifically for the GPU — `DIRTY_MEMORY_NV2A` (3) and `DIRTY_MEMORY_NV2A_TEX` (4) in include/exec/ramlist.h:14-15 — and the Xbox is a UMA machine, so NV2A VRAM *is* system RAM.

Affected writes: voice register updates (voice_set_mask -> ram_stl, vp.c:349), notifier status bytes (set_notify_status -> ram_stb, vp.c:142-147), and the inbuf/outbuf/SSL SGE table entries (vp.c:691, 727, 779). If any of those land in a page the NV2A has cached as a texture or vertex buffer, or in a page TCG has translated code from, the cache/TB is not invalidated.

Realistically low: DirectSound places voice tables and notifier buffers in data heap allocations that do not overlap textures or code, and upstream already writes EP output buffers with a raw `memcpy(&d->ram_ptr[paddr], ...)` in scatter_gather_rw. Recording it because it is a fork-introduced narrowing of a memory-consistency guarantee that is not covered by the existing audit tables A/B.
confirmed.proposed_fix: Either (a) accept it and write the reasoning down as a code comment plus a row in docs/windows-gating-audit.md section B alongside B10, stating that APU write targets are guest data buffers that are never NV2A-cached or TCG-translated; or (b) keep the fast path and add the dirty update explicitly, e.g. call `cpu_physical_memory_set_dirty_range(addr, len, DIRTY_CLIENTS_NOCODE)` after the direct store — the bitmap update is a couple of atomic ORs and would not undo the win of skipping the full address_space dispatch.
confirmed.apple_impact: none — identical code on both platforms; option (b) adds the same small cost to macOS, option (a) adds nothing.
confirmed.verifier_notes: If option (b) is chosen, use the public API `memory_region_set_dirty(d->ram, addr, len)` (include/system/memory.h:2156; already what upstream gp_ep.c:78 does after its raw memcpy, and reachable from vp.c via apu_int.h -> hw/hw.h). Do NOT use `cpu_physical_memory_set_dirty_range` — that name does not exist in this tree (include/exec/ram_addr.h is gone; the function is `physical_memory_set_dirty_range` in include/system/physmem.h and is not the intended device-facing entry point). memory_region_set_dirty is a handful of atomic bitmap ORs and preserves the win of skipping address_space translation; it does not TB-invalidate, which matches upstream's own gp_ep.c behaviour and is adequate for APU data buffers. Option (a) is also acceptable: a comment on ram_stl/ram_stb at vp.c:109 plus an audit-table row stating the targets are never NV2A-cached or TCG-translated. Either way apple_impact is none/identical on both platforms.

confirmed.title: Windows now runs the plain DSP56300 C interpreter: neither JIT engine is on by default
confirmed.description:
Engine selection resolves to "no JIT at all" on Windows x86_64. `dsp_want_external_jit_engine()` short-circuits to the fork's inline JIT only under `#if DSP56K_JIT_SUPPORTED`, which is 0 on x86_64 (`#if defined(__aarch64__) && !defined(_WIN32)`, dsp56k_jit_arm64.h:24); it then returns `g_config.audio.use_dsp_jit`, whose upstream default was flipped to false in fc13b78060 ("apu: Disable DSP JIT by default for first release"). So dsp_init takes the `dsp_c_init` branch and dsp_c_run never calls into a translator.

The upstream dsp56300 Rust engine *is* available on this target — subprojects/dsp56300/meson.build derives `x86_64-pc-windows-gnu` and links `-lbcrypt -lntdll -luserenv -lws2_32` — it is simply off. The recorded Apple-side A/B (docs/optimizations.md, DSP execution engines) puts the upstream engine at 19% APU-thread utilisation vs 22% for the interpreter, so the ceiling is ~3 points of one core on a thread that is off the frame critical path; the archaeology entry on parmove fusion already establishes that APU-thread savings do not convert to fps. Worth an explicit measurement rather than an assumption, and worth documenting so "Windows has no DSP JIT" is a known state rather than a surprise.

confirmed.title: gp_read/ep_read lock-free rationale comment asserts a BQL guarantee that does not hold against the APU thread
confirmed.description:
The fork added a comment justifying lock-free GP/EP MMIO reads on the grounds that "the BQL serializes guest MMIO dispatch". The GP/EP regions are indeed not in the lockless-MMIO set (only `d->vp.mmio` is, apu.c:434-449), so gp_read does run under the BQL — but the thread it needs to be serialised *against* is the APU frame thread, which executes the DSP inside se_frame while holding only `d->lock` and never takes the BQL for that work. The BQL therefore serialises gp_read against other vCPU MMIO and nothing else. gp_write, by contrast, does take `d->lock` (gp_ep.c:318), so writes are correctly serialised and reads are the asymmetric case.

The concrete consequence is not just stale/torn DSP memory reads: `mcpx_apu_update_dsp_preference` (gp_ep.c:45-49) calls `dsp_set_engine` from se_frame whenever `g_config.audio.use_dsp_jit` changes, and dsp_set_engine does `dsp->ops->finalize(dsp)` -> `g_free(dsp->backend); dsp->backend = NULL;` before installing the new engine. A vCPU thread inside gp_read at that moment reaches `dsp_read_memory(d->gp.dsp, ...)` -> `dsp->ops->read_memory` -> `c_core(dsp)` and sees a freed or NULL backend. The "DSP JIT engine" checkbox is unconditional in the UI (ui/xui/main-menu.cc:936), and on Windows it is the *only* DSP engine toggle that does anything, so this is user-reachable there specifically. The switching machinery is upstream's; what the fork added is a comment that says the situation is safe.
confirmed.proposed_fix: Two independent parts. (a) Correct the comment: state that reads are lock-free by design and that the exposure is stale/torn DSP memory values, which the guest tolerates, rather than claiming BQL serialisation. (b) Close the engine-switch window: have mcpx_apu_update_dsp_preference quiesce before switching — the machinery already exists (`mcpx_apu_wait_for_idle` / `mcpx_apu_resume`, apu.c:322-341) — or defer the switch to the vm-state-change path so the backend pointer is never swapped while a vCPU can be inside gp_read/ep_read. A minimal alternative is to require a title restart for the toggle, matching what the fork already does for `audio.dsp_jit.enabled` ("Takes effect on next title launch", main-menu.cc:934).
confirmed.apple_impact: none — on Apple Silicon with `audio.dsp_jit.enabled` set, dsp_set_engine's fork gate forces use_jit=false so the engine never actually switches; the fix only affects the path where a switch really happens.
confirmed.verifier_notes: Two parts, both Apple-neutral. (a) Rewrite the comment at gp_ep.c:267-274 (and the ep_read pointer at :367) to say reads are deliberately lock-free and tolerate stale/torn DSP memory values relative to the APU thread; drop the "BQL serializes" justification since the BQL does not order against the APU frame thread. (b) Make the engine swap safe against in-flight vCPU MMIO reads. Options in ascending cost: (i) require restart for audio.use_dsp_jit — read g_config.audio.use_dsp_jit once at init (dsp_want_external_jit_engine already does this in dsp_init, dsp.c:141) and delete the runtime dsp_set_engine branch from mcpx_apu_update_dsp_preference, updating the main-menu.cc:936 tooltip to "Takes effect on next title launch" like the Apple toggle; (ii) perform the switch under the BQL: in se_frame, when the pref changes, do qemu_mutex_unlock(&d->lock); bql_lock(); qemu_mutex_lock(&d->lock); dsp_set_engine(...); qemu_mutex_unlock(&d->lock); bql_unlock(); qemu_mutex_lock(&d->lock); mirroring the update_irq pattern at apu.c:298-303 — since gp_read/ep_read are BQL-held MMIO this fully excludes them; (iii) alternatively take d->lock in gp_read/ep_read, but the fork's comment says this caused audio dropouts, and it is not needed if (ii) is done. Do not touch the vp.mmio lockless path. On Apple with dsp_jit.enabled the switch is already forced to a no-op, so none of these change macOS behaviour (apple_impact: none).

confirmed.title: wglDXLockObjectsNV is called twice per frame but unlocked once in the DXGI present path
confirmed.description: `Win32DxgiPresenter::EndFrame` calls `m_wgl_dx_lock_objects_nv` inside the `if (!...)` error check and then calls it a *second* time unconditionally on the next line, while only one `wglDXUnlockObjectsNV` follows. WGL_NV_DX_interop specifies that locking an already-locked object is an error (the call returns FALSE and sets ERROR_LOCK_FAILED), so on a conforming NVIDIA driver the second call fails silently every frame — harmless in effect but it means every present sets a Win32 error and the return value is unchecked. If any driver instead ref-counts the lock, the single unlock leaves the object locked: the subsequent `CopyResource` reads a texture still owned by GL (undefined content), and next frame's first lock fails → the code calls `Cleanup()`, which tears the whole presenter down permanently and silently falls back to `SDL_GL_SwapWindow` for the rest of the session. This is upstream-inherited code (identical to upstream/master — `git diff upstream/master...HEAD -- ui/xui/win32-dxgi-present.cc` is empty), but it is on the exact present path this branch now ships on the target machine.
confirmed.proposed_fix: Delete line 585 (the duplicate unconditional lock). One lock, one unlock per frame. If the intent was a retry, it should be written as an explicit retry with its own failure handling rather than an ignored second call.
confirmed.apple_impact: none — the whole translation unit is `#ifdef _WIN32`; the `#else` half is stubs, and ui/xui/meson.build only adds win32-dxgi-present.cc when `host_os == 'windows'`.
confirmed.verifier_notes: Delete the unconditional second `m_wgl_dx_lock_objects_nv(m_wgl_device, 1, &m_wgl_object);` (HEAD line 585 of C:\Users\ms\Documents\xemu-macos\ui\xui\win32-dxgi-present.cc) so EndFrame has one lock (checked) and one unlock. Windows-only translation unit (meson `host_os == 'windows'`, `#ifdef _WIN32`), apple_impact: none. Optional: correct the error-code wording in any commentary to ERROR_BUSY (the spec's code for locking an already-locked interop object). | The proposed fix (delete the unconditional second `m_wgl_dx_lock_objects_nv(...)` at HEAD line 585 of ui/xui/win32-dxgi-present.cc) is correct and sufficient — one lock, one unlock per frame; do not turn it into a retry (a lock failure here means the interop device is broken and Cleanup() is the right response). confirmed.title: UI frame cap and frame_seq dedup exist only in metal_render_frame; the GL/DXGI path free-runs and pays a blocking PFIFO round trip per UI frame
confirmed.description: `XEMU_UI_FRAME_CAP_NS` (a UI-frame-period floor) and the `frame_seq` "don't re-composite unchanged content" dedup both live inside `metal_render_frame`, which is `#ifdef __APPLE__`. `gl_render_frame` — the path Windows uses — has neither. The main loop is `while (!qatomic_read(&qemu_exiting)) { poll_events(scon); render_frame(scon); }` (ui/xemu.c:2016-2019) with no throttle of its own. With `display.window.vsync = false` and DXGI tearing enabled, `Present(0, DXGI_PRESENT_ALLOW_TEARING)` does not block, so the loop free-runs: every iteration calls `nv2a_get_framebuffer_surface()`, which on the Vulkan renderer does `qemu_event_reset` + `qatomic_set(sync_pending)` + `pfifo_kick(d)` + `qemu_event_wait(&d->pgraph.sync_complete)` — a full blocking cross-thread round trip that forces the PFIFO thread to drop `pfifo.lock`, take `pgraph.lock` and run `pgraph_vk_sync`. The fork's own 8 ms `min_sync_interval_ns` gate stops the redundant *composite*, but not the kick/wake/lock churn on the PFIFO thread, nor the full ImGui frame + GL draws + palette upload + DXGI blit/copy/Present the UI thread does each iteration. On 4C/8T this steals cycles directly from the vCPU and PFIFO threads. Note the pull model structurally cannot do the frame_seq dedup (Invariant 8: learning frame_seq *is* the round trip), so the honest portable fix is the frame cap, not the dedup.
confirmed.proposed_fix: Hoist the `XEMU_UI_FRAME_CAP_NS` block out of `metal_render_frame` into `render_frame()` (or the head of `gl_render_frame`) so it applies to both presenters, and give it a non-zero default on the GL path when `g_config.display.window.vsync == false` (e.g. floor the UI period at the guest vblank interval, 16666666 ns) with 0 meaning uncapped. This is a UI-thread present-rate cap only — it does not touch `vblank_interval_ns`, `process_vblank`, or `NV_PCRTC_INTR_0_VBLANK`, so it is unrelated to the reverted 'vblank cadence aligned to host display refresh' experiment (archaeology §3.2). Land it behind the existing env knob first and prove it with an interleaved savestate A/B on the Windows machine (fps + nsprof PRESENT_WAIT) before flipping any default.
confirmed.apple_impact: none if the cap block is hoisted verbatim (metal_render_frame's behaviour and its default of 0 are preserved); the proposed non-zero default must be conditioned on the GL presenter so the Metal path keeps its current uncapped-by-default semantics.
confirmed.verifier_notes: Hoist the XEMU_UI_FRAME_CAP_NS block (ui/xemu.c:1181-1204) verbatim into render_frame() (ui/xemu.c:1400) ahead of the presenter dispatch, or into the head of gl_render_frame after the `rendering` xchg — if placed after the xchg, mirror :1200 `qatomic_set(&rendering, false)` on the early return. confirmed.title: Windows release build silently loses -Doptimization=3 (ships -O2) although the comment claims only LTO was dropped
confirmed.description: The fork added a release-options block that upstream did not have. The `win64*|MINGW*|MSYS*` arm deliberately omits LTO (correctly — see .claude/skills/xemu-build-and-env §6.3), but it also drops `-Doptimization=3` and `-Dstack_protector=disabled`, while the comment on line 504 states "The LTO-independent knobs are kept." `-Doptimization` and `-Dstack_protector` are toolchain-neutral meson options that work identically on mingw GCC and llvm-mingw; they have nothing to do with the ThinLTO / qemu_build_not_reached_always problem the comment cites. Result: on this machine the release build compiles the whole TCG interpreter and NV2A renderer at -O2 while macOS and Linux release builds get -O3 plus thin LTO. This is a pure parity gap, not a platform constraint.
confirmed.evidence: build.sh:496-510 — Windows arm: `opts="$opts -Dqom_cast_debug=false -Dtrace_backends=nop"`; the `*)` arm: `opts="$opts -Doptimization=3 -Dqom_cast_debug=false"` / `opts="$opts -Dtrace_backends=nop -Dstack_protector=disabled"`. confirmed.title: XEMU_PGO on Windows is wired for clang/llvm-profdata but the branch never selects clang; on the MSYS2 GCC toolchain PGO is silently non-functional
confirmed.description: `setup_pgo()` (build.sh:96-135) emits clang-only IR-PGO flags and merges `*.profraw` with `llvm-profdata`. The Windows branch calls it with `profdata_prefix=""` and a comment claiming "MSYS2 clang accepts the same flags" — but the branch never sets `CC`/`CXX`, so the build uses whatever `cc` is, which on a stock MSYS2 MINGW64 install is GCC. GCC accepts `-fprofile-generate=<dir>` and happily produces `.gcda` files, so the generate stage looks like it worked; the use stage then globs `*.profraw`, finds none, and hard-exits `PGO: no profiles found in <dir>` (build.sh:126-129) even though the profile directory is full of real profile data. On this machine `llvm-profdata` is not even installed (only clang is), so if a user did force clang the merge step would abort the script under `set -e`. Net: the documented XEMU_PGO=generate/use flow (.claude/skills/xemu-build-and-env §6.1 says it "works the same two-stage way as macOS") cannot complete on the primary Windows target — which matters because docs/windows-gating-audit.md D7 names Windows PGO as an open item.
confirmed.evidence: build.sh:785-790 `# PGO: same two-stage flow as Darwin/Linux (MSYS2 clang accepts / # the same flags; llvm-profdata without the xcrun prefix). ... profdata_prefix=""; setup_pgo`. build.sh:112-113 `newest_raw=$(ls -t "${pgo_dir}"/*.profraw 2>/dev/null | head -1 || true)`; :126 `if [ ! -f "${pgo_dir}/default.profdata" ]; then echo "PGO: no profiles found in ${pgo_dir}"; exit 1; fi`. Toolchain on the target: build/meson-logs/meson-log.txt:47 `C compiler for the host machine: cc -m64 (gcc 16.2.0 "cc (Rev3, Built by MSYS2 project) 16.2.0")`; `ls /c/msys64/mingw64/bin/llvm-profdata.exe` -> No such file (clang.exe is present).
confirmed.proposed_fix: Either (a) add a GCC arm to `setup_pgo()`: when `$($CC --version)` is GCC, use `-fprofile-generate=$pgo_dir` / `-fprofile-use=$pgo_dir -fprofile-correction -Wno-missing-profile` and skip the llvm-profdata merge entirely (GCC reads .gcda straight from the directory); or (b) have the Windows branch export `CC=clang CXX=clang++` when `$XEMU_PGO` is set and fail early with a clear message if `llvm-profdata` is absent. Either way, make `setup_pgo` refuse to claim success when the compiler family and the profile format disagree.
confirmed.apple_impact: none if the GCC arm is added as a new branch keyed on compiler family — Darwin keeps `profdata_prefix="xcrun "` and the clang path unchanged.
confirmed.verifier_notes: Keep severity medium. Fix description should be corrected: on the default XEMU_PGO_DIR the use stage does not hard-exit; it silently builds without PGO while announcing success (worse). Recommended fix (a): in setup_pgo(), detect compiler family (e.g. `${CC:-cc} --version | grep -q 'Free Software Foundation'` or `-dM -E` for __GNUC__ && !__clang__) and add a GCC arm: generate -> `-fprofile-generate=${pgo_dir} -fprofile-update=atomic` (QEMU is heavily multithreaded), use -> `-fprofile-use=${pgo_dir} -fprofile-correction -Wno-missing-profile` (GCC reads mangled-path .gcda directly from the directory; requires generate and use builds to share the same build/ output paths, which build.sh already does), skip llvm-profdata entirely, and hard-fail if the dir has no *.gcda. Also make check_pgo_staleness() either match GCC's diagnostics ("profile count data file not found", "does not match its profile data") or print "staleness report: clang-only, skipped" under GCC rather than a false 0/0. Alternative (b): export CC=clang CXX=clang++ in the MSYS2 branch when XEMU_PGO is set and `command -v llvm-profdata` early-fail (install mingw-w64-x86_64-llvm-tools / llvm). Either way, refuse to proceed when the committed clang .profdata is the only artefact and the compiler is GCC. confirmed.title: No CI leg builds or tests natively on MSYS2 MINGW64; three native-Windows build breaks had to be found by hand
confirmed.description: build-windows.yml only exercises the win64-cross path (`./build.sh -p win64-cross`) inside a Linux container, and runs no tests on either arch. The fork added an xbox unit suite and wired it into build-macos.yml (arm64 legs) and build-linux.yml (new `test` job, x86_64 + aarch64), but build-windows.yml got neither. The whole `CYGWIN*|MINGW*|MSYS*` arm of build.sh — which is the fork's documented *preferred* Windows path (.claude/skills/xemu-build-and-env §6.1 "Native (MSYS2) — preferred") — has zero automated coverage. The cost is concrete and already paid: scripts/xemu-version.sh needed a hand-written `sanitize_numeric` for windres FILEVERSION, and the working tree right now carries two more uncommitted hand fixes for native-MSYS2-only breakage (the `--prefix=$(cygpath -m /qemu)` workaround for Python >= 3.13 `ntpath.isabs`, and `tar --force-local` in the dsp56300 subproject). None of those three could be caught by the cross legs. Two of the portable test arms (`xbox-mcpx-dsp-corpus-interp`, `xbox-nv2a-swizzle`) would run on Windows unmodified — tests/xbox/dsp/meson.build:57 gates only the aarch64 JIT arms behind `host_os != 'windows'`.
confirmed.evidence: .github/workflows/build-windows.yml:78-79 `- name: Compile\n      run: ./build.sh -p win64-cross ${XEMU_BUILD_OPTIONS}` — the job ends at artifact upload (:82-86) with no `meson test` step, and there is no `windows-latest` build job (only `generate_pdb`, :91-93, which merely runs cv2pdb on the cross artifact). Compare build-linux.yml:171+ (`test:` job, `ninja test-xbox` + `meson test --suite xbox`). docs/windows-gating-audit.md §H already records "`build-windows.yml` (win64-cross) still runs no tests" as an open gap.
confirmed.proposed_fix: Add a `windows-latest` job using `msys2/setup-msys2@v2` (msystem: MINGW64, install the mingw-w64-x86_64 toolchain + glib2/sdl3/libsamplerate/vulkan-headers/glslang deps), running `./build.sh --debug` then `cd build && ninja test-xbox && ./pyvenv/bin/meson test --suite xbox --print-errorlogs --no-rebuild`. Debug avoids the release path's meson options entirely and links fast, matching the rationale already written into build-linux.yml's test job. That single leg would have caught all three of the hand-found breakages plus any future MSYS2 python/tar/windres drift.

confirmed.title: patch_directory overlays a full frozen copy of the pinned imgui repo's meson.build, so a wrap revision bump silently reverts upstream's build file
confirmed.description: To get `add_languages('objcpp')` on darwin, the fork added `patch_directory=imgui` and checked in a complete 137-line copy of the subproject's own meson.build plus its meson_options.txt. meson's patch_directory overwrites files after checkout, so from now on the *fork's snapshot* of imgui's build description wins over whatever revision `imgui.wrap` points at. If xemu-project/imgui bumps imgui (new backend source, new option, changed IMGUI_API handling) and the fork bumps `revision=`, the build will keep using the stale 1.91.8-era file and either miss new sources or fail cryptically — and because the file is a full copy rather than a delta, a reviewer diffing the wrap bump sees nothing wrong. This affects all platforms including the Windows legs (the overlay carries the d3d*/`IMGUI_API=__declspec(dllexport)` logic).
confirmed.evidence:
subprojects/imgui.wrap:1-7 `[wrap-git] url=https://github.com/xemu-project/imgui / revision=b911105fca3ca1b025706dd168e5798070f143a1 / depth=1 / # Overlay: enables Objective-C++ on darwin ... / patch_directory=imgui`. subprojects/packagefiles/imgui/meson.build is a new 137-line file whose only fork-specific content is lines 9-12 `if host_machine.system() == 'darwin'
  # Required for backends/imgui_impl_metal.mm (metal=enabled).
  add_languages('objcpp')
endif`; the rest (including `api = '-DIMGUI_API=@0@'.format(... '__declspec(dllexport)' ...)` at :112-114) is a verbatim snapshot. `.github/workflows/bump-subproject-wraps.yml` bumps wrap revisions with no awareness of the overlay.
confirmed.proposed_fix: Add a cheap drift guard: a CI step (or a `scripts/` check invoked from the Linux test job) that clones the pinned imgui revision to a temp dir and `diff`s its `meson.build`/`meson_options.txt` against `subprojects/packagefiles/imgui/`, failing if they differ by anything other than the four-line darwin `add_languages` block. Alternatively drop the overlay entirely and call `add_languages('objcpp', required: false)` from the *parent* meson.build before `subproject('imgui', ...)` — meson propagates enabled languages into subprojects, which removes the need to shadow the file at all.
confirmed.apple_impact: none — the darwin objcpp enablement is preserved either way; the parent-project variant is strictly equivalent for the Metal backend build.
confirmed.verifier_notes: Keep only the drift-guard variant, extended to cover all three overlay files: a CI/scripts check that clones the wrap's pinned revision and diffs subprojects/packagefiles/imgui/{meson.build,meson_options.txt,backends/imgui_impl_metal.mm} against it, allowing only the known deltas (the 4-line darwin add_languages block; the fork's MRC retain/release patch in the .mm). Better still, convert the two overlays into wrap `diff_files=` patches (meson >= 0.63) so a revision bump that no longer applies fails loudly instead of silently shadowing. Drop the "call add_languages from the parent and delete the overlay" alternative — the parent already calls add_languages('objcpp') at meson.build:92 and it does not satisfy the subproject, and deleting the overlay would lose the imgui_impl_metal.mm leak fixes (macOS regression). apple_impact for the drift guard: none.

confirmed.title: tar --force-local is gated on host_machine.system() but it is a property of the build machine's tar, not the target
confirmed.description: The local (uncommitted) fix that makes the native MSYS2 build work adds `--force-local` so GNU tar does not read `C:/...` as a `host:path` remote archive. The condition used is `host_os == 'windows'`, where `host_os = host_machine.system()` (line 7) — i.e. the *target* platform. The flag's availability and necessity depend on which `tar` binary meson invokes, which is the build machine's. On the win64-cross legs host==windows/build==linux, so GNU tar gets a flag it does not need (harmless); but any build where the target is Windows and the builder is macOS would pass `--force-local` to bsdtar, which does not have it, and `check: true` turns that into a hard configure error — exactly the case the code comment itself calls out ("bsdtar (macOS) lacks the option"). The archive path is only Windows-absolute when meson itself runs on Windows, so the condition is testing the wrong machine.
confirmed.evidence:
subprojects/dsp56300/meson.build:6-7 `host_cpu = host_machine.cpu_family()` / `host_os = host_machine.system()`; :32-35 `if host_os == 'windows'
    # MSYS2/GNU tar parses "C:/path" as host:path (remote archive);
    # --force-local keeps it a file. bsdtar (macOS) lacks the option.
    tar_args += ['--force-local']`. The paths involved come from `meson.current_source_dir()` / `meson.current_build_dir()` (:25, :31), which are build-machine paths. Verified working on the target: build/meson-logs/meson-log.txt:6465 `Running command: C:\msys64\usr\bin/tar.EXE xzf C:/Users/ms/Documents/xemu-macos/subprojects/dsp56300/dsp56300-0.1.3-x86_64-pc-windows-gnu.tar.gz -C C:/Users/ms/Documents/xemu-macos/build/subprojects/dsp56300 --force-local`.
confirmed.proposed_fix: Change the guard to `if build_machine.system() == 'windows'` and, while there, replace the bare `run_command('tar', ...)` with `run_command(find_program('tar'), ...)` so the resolved binary is visible in the meson log and a missing tar fails with a clear message. Also worth upstreaming this whole hunk to xemu-project — the subproject is otherwise verbatim upstream and every native MSYS2 builder will hit it.
confirmed.apple_impact: none — on macOS `build_machine.system()` is 'darwin', so bsdtar never sees the flag; behaviour is identical to today.
confirmed.verifier_notes: In C:\Users\ms\Documents\xemu-macos\subprojects\dsp56300\meson.build:32 change `if host_os == 'windows'` to `if build_machine.system() == 'windows'` (keep `host_os` for the archive-name/target selection and link_args, which correctly depend on the target). Optionally use `tar = find_program('tar')` and `run_command(tar, tar_args, check: true)` so the resolved binary path shows in meson-log.txt and a missing tar fails with a clear message rather than a generic run_command error. The `--force-local` addition itself is a legitimate fix worth offering upstream (xemu-project/xemu's subprojects/dsp56300/meson.build is otherwise identical) once the guard is corrected. Apple impact: none — on a macOS build machine `build_machine.system()` is 'darwin' so bsdtar never receives the flag, identical to today's behaviour. Correct the finding's description: the hunk is committed (ac28e5a5bd), not a local uncommitted change.

confirmed.title: DSP runs fully interpreted on Windows: the inline JIT is aarch64-POSIX-only and the external dsp56300 engine defaults off, despite a Windows prebuilt existing
confirmed.description: On Windows x86_64 `DSP56K_JIT_SUPPORTED` is 0 (hw/xbox/mcpx/apu/dsp/interp/dsp56k_jit_arm64.h:24, `__aarch64__ && !_WIN32`), so `dsp_want_external_jit_engine()` reduces to `g_config.audio.use_dsp_jit`, which upstream set to false for the first release. The MCPX DSP therefore always runs the C interpreter on the target machine, while Apple Silicon gets the fork's inline block JIT. The upstream dsp56300 subproject already ships and links a prebuilt Windows-GNU static library, so the external engine is a build-ready alternative that is simply switched off. This is upstream's conservatism, not a fork regression — flagging it because the FOCUS asks for Apple/aarch64-only optimizations that could be enabled for Windows x86_64, and this is the largest one with no Windows counterpart.
confirmed.evidence:
config_spec.yml:345-349 `# Upstream dsp56300-subproject JIT execution engine.
  use_dsp_jit:
    type: bool
    default: false` (set by upstream commit fc13b78060 "apu: Disable DSP JIT by default for first release"). hw/xbox/mcpx/apu/dsp/dsp.c:120-128 `static bool dsp_want_external_jit_engine(void) { #if DSP56K_JIT_SUPPORTED if (g_config.audio.dsp_jit.enabled) return false; #endif return g_config.audio.use_dsp_jit; }`. subprojects/dsp56300/meson.build:10-12 selects `x86_64-pc-windows-gnu`; :43-44 links it with `['-lbcrypt', '-lntdll', '-luserenv', '-lws2_32']`; the archive `dsp56300-0.1.3-x86_64-pc-windows-gnu.tar.gz` is present and was extracted successfully in this build tree.
confirmed.proposed_fix: Do not change the shipped default (that is upstream's call and the fork's change-control rules require an A/B receipt). Instead: (1) measure it — with `XEMU_APU_PROF` on the target, run a fixed savestate scene with `audio.use_dsp_jit = false` vs `true` and record APU-thread utilisation; (2) if the external engine is both correct and materially cheaper on Windows, propose the flip upstream rather than diverging, or expose it as a documented Windows-side knob in the README knob table. This is blocked on the Windows benchmark harness gap reported above.
confirmed.apple_impact: none — on Apple `dsp_jit.enabled` takes precedence over `use_dsp_jit` (dsp.c:122-124), so the inline JIT selection is unaffected regardless of what `use_dsp_jit` is set to.
confirmed.verifier_notes:
Keep severity low; treat as measurement task plus a doc fix, not a code change:
- Do not flip `use_dsp_jit` in config_spec.yml (upstream's release decision; fork change-control requires an A/B receipt).
- Fix the stale text at docs/optimizations.md:1004 ("default on") and :1008-1009 ("Non-Apple hosts get upstream's dsp56300 engine by default") to reflect that since upstream fc13b78060 every non-Apple host, including Windows x86_64, runs the C interpreter unless `[audio] use_dsp_jit = true` is set.
