- Apple impact: none. `dsp_want_external_jit_engine()` checks `dsp_jit.enabled` first on DSP56K_JIT_SUPPORTED hosts, so changes to `use_dsp_jit` or its docs do not affect the inline JIT selection.

confirmed.title: Fork's new unbound-pad guard is reached through an unbounded array index: device_index >= 4 reads past bound_controllers[4] and then writes through the garbage pointer
confirmed.description: The fork replaced `assert(state)` in `update_output()` (xid.c:48-54) and `update_input()` (xid.c:67-72) with a `if (!state) return;` guard, and the comment explicitly sanctions the new path: "Emulated pad with no host binding (e.g. raw -device for snapshot-topology matching ...)". But `s->device_index` comes from the qdev property `DEFINE_PROP_UINT8("index", USBXIDGamepadState, device_index, 0)` (hw/xbox/xid-gamepad.c:219) which accepts 0..255 with no validation, and `xemu_input_get_bound()` (ui/xemu-input.c:742-745) is `return bound_controllers[index];` with no bounds check against the 4-element array declared at ui/xemu-input.c:90. So `-device usb-xbox-gamepad,port=1.3.1,index=4` (an off-by-one on the `index=<N-1>` formula the fork's own harness docs tell operators to hand-write) makes `xemu_input_get_bound(4)` read whatever global follows `bound_controllers` — most plausibly `bound_drivers[0]`, initialized on the very next line to the string literal `"usb-xbox-gamepad"`. That is a non-NULL pointer, so the fork's new `if (!state)` guard does not catch it; `update_output()` then executes `state->rumble_l = ...` writing into .rodata (access violation on Windows, where the image's read-only section is hard-enforced), and `update_input()` calls `xemu_input_update_controller(state)` on the same bogus pointer. Upstream's `assert(state)` was equally powerless here (it also ran after the OOB read), so this is not a regression the fork introduced — but the fork is the code that now advertises hand-written `-device` as a supported topology-matching path, and this is the exact function where the check belongs.
confirmed.apple_impact: none — pure bounds check on a host-side array whose size is 4 on every platform; on macOS the same -device typo currently produces the same wild pointer, so behaviour for all valid indices (0..3) is bit-identical before and after.
confirmed.verifier_notes: Single-point fix in ui/xemu-input.c:742: `if (index < 0 || index >= (int)ARRAY_SIZE(bound_controllers)) return NULL;` before the array read. This also hardens the other callers (ui/xemu-input.c:416,429; ui/xui/main-menu.cc:165,273), all of which already pass 0..3 so behaviour for valid indices is unchanged. Additionally reject `device_index >= 4` in usb_xbox_gamepad_realize()/usb_xbox_gamepad_s_realize() via `error_setg(errp, "index must be 0..3")` so a bad -device line fails at construction instead of silently producing a dead pad. Drop the ".rodata / bound_drivers" narrative from the write-up — the layout claim is not reliable; the defect is simply an unchecked index into a 4-element array. apple_impact: none (identical array size and valid-index behaviour on all platforms). | Apply the single-point bounds check in ui/xemu-input.c:742 exactly as proposed (`if (index < 0 || index >= (int)ARRAY_SIZE(bound_controllers)) return NULL;`); it is a pure host-array guard, bit-identical for indices 0..3 on every platform (apple_impact: none). Additionally reject the bad line at construction so the operator sees the typo instead of a silently dead pad: in both `usb_xbox_gamepad_realize()` (hw/xbox/xid-gamepad.c:170) and `usb_xbox_gamepad_s_realize()` (:194), which already receive `Error **errp`, add `if (s->device_index >= 4) { error_setg(errp, "usb-xbox-gamepad: index must be 0..3 (got %u)", s->device_index); return; }` before the existing init. Do not add the per-site `>= 4` checks  …[truncated; full text in the session workflow journal]

confirmed.title: LRU free-list rework dropped the lru_is_node_in_use() filter in lru_try_evict_one(), so a node on `global` that is not in a bin is returned as "evicted" and then QTAILQ_REMOVE'd from the wrong list
confirmed.description: The fork split `Lru` into an in-use `global` list and a dedicated `free` list (include/qemu/lru.h:53-54) and, on the strength of the new invariant, deleted the `lru_is_node_in_use(lru, found) &&` term from `lru_try_evict_one()`'s scan (lru.h:145-150). The invariant does hold today, but three pieces of the file are now coupled in a way that fails silently rather than loudly if it ever stops holding: (1) `lru_evict_node()` still opens with `if (!lru_is_node_in_use(lru, node)) { return; }` (lru.h:117-119) — it returns *without* moving the node to `free`; (2) `lru_try_evict_one()` no longer screens such nodes out, so it happily returns one as if it had been evicted; (3) `lru_lookup()`'s miss path then unconditionally does `QTAILQ_REMOVE(&lru->free, found, next_global)` (lru.h:210) on a node that is actually still linked on `global`. That splices the node out of `global` using `free`'s head for the tail fixup, corrupting both lists, and `num_free` goes negative — a heap-corruption-class failure with no assertion anywhere near the cause. The only way to reach a not-in-use node on `global` is re-entrancy into the same `Lru` from `post_node_evict` during the window at lru.h:122-129 where the node has been unlinked from its bin but not yet moved to `free`. I checked every callback (gl/vk shader, shader-module, texture, sampler, pipeline, compute-pipeline caches) and none re-enters its own LRU today — `shader_cache_entry_post_evict` (vk/shaders.c:428) only calls `pgraph_vk_unref_shader_module` on the *module* cache, a different Lru — so this is latent, not live. Related loose end from the same rework: `lru_get_one_free()` (lru.h:166-175) returns a node that is still linked on `free` and has not had `num_free` decremented, i.e. it now has a two-step contract that only `lru_lookup()` honours; nothing in the header states or checks that. This is a shared (non-gated) header so it is identical on Windows and macOS.
confirmed.apple_impact: none — asserts/comments only, no behavioural change on either platform while the invariant holds; the free-list rework itself (which is the real win, turning the once-full O(cache size) tail walk into O(1) for the 50k-entry vk shader-module cache at hw/xbox/nv2a/pgraph/vk/shaders.c:518) is untouched.
confirmed.verifier_notes: Keep as low/hardening. The two proposed asserts are correct and zero-cost in the hot path: `assert(lru_is_node_in_use(lru, found));` at the top of the lru_try_evict_one loop body (lru.h:146) and `assert(!lru_is_node_in_use(lru, found));` after `found = lru_get_one_free(lru);` (lru.h:209). Additionally consider `assert(lru_is_node_in_use(lru, node))` (or at least a comment) at lru_evict_node's early return, since with the split-list design a not-in-use node passed there is always a caller bug. Folding `QTAILQ_REMOVE(&lru->free, ...)` and `num_free -= 1` into lru_get_one_free() would remove the undocumented two-step contract. Also worth noting in the header that post_node_evict must not re-enter the same Lru — this was already an unsupported (and broken) pattern upstream, so documenting it is not a new restriction. apple_impact: none (asserts/comments only; asserts are live on both platforms and never fire while the invariant holds).

confirmed.title: x86_64 hosts never program the host x87 rounding mode, so the 2026-08-09 FIST/FRNDINT directed-rounding fallback is inert under the default hard_fpu=true
confirmed.description: `set_x86_rounding_mode()` mirrors the guest RC into the host FP rounding state only on aarch64 (`#if defined(XBOX) && defined(__aarch64__) ... fesetround(host_round_mode[mode])`). On x86_64 nothing programs the host x87 control word. The 2026-08-09 fix for directed rounding routes the bad cases to `gen_helper_fistl_ST0` / `gen_helper_frndint` (translate.c:2101-2107, 2135-2141, 2159-2166, 2207-2218) with the comment "fall back to the softfloat helper, which honours the guest RC". But translate.c:43-44 rewrites every `gen_helper_f*` through `MAP_GEN_HELPER_SOFT_HARD(name) = (g_use_hard_fpu ? gen_helper_##name##__hard : gen_helper_##name##__soft)`, and `perf.hard_fpu` defaults to `true` (config_spec.yml:402-404). So the fallback lands in the __hard helper, which on x86_64 is `floatx80_to_int32__hard() { return (int32_t)llrintl(a.fval); }` (fpu_helper.c:182-186) and `floatx80_round_to_int__hard() { return (floatx80){ .fval = rintl(a.fval) }; }` (fpu_helper.c:176-180). `llrintl`/`rintl` on x86_64 execute on the host x87 unit and obey the host x87 CW rounding field — which is still round-to-nearest. Net effect on Windows/Linux/macOS x86_64 in the shipped default configuration: FIST/FISTP under guest RC=toward-(-inf)/(+inf) and FRNDINT under ANY non-nearest guest RC (including RC=3 truncate/chop, which Xbox titles commonly set for float->int) still round to nearest. The 'x86_64 FIST/FRNDINT rounding fallback' entry in docs/optimizations.md therefore does not describe the shipped behaviour; the bug is only fixed when the user sets perf.hard_fpu = false.
confirmed.evidence:
fpu_helper.c:1186 `#if defined(XBOX) && defined(__aarch64__)` / `fesetround(host_round_mode[mode]);` / `#endif` — no x86_64 arm.
fpu_helper.c:183-186 `int32_t floatx80_to_int32__hard(floatx80 a, float_status *status) { return (int32_t)llrintl(a.fval); }`
fpu_helper.c:177-180 `floatx80 floatx80_round_to_int__hard(floatx80 a, float_status *status) { return (floatx80){ .fval = rintl(a.fval) }; }`
translate.c:43-44 `#define MAP_GEN_HELPER_SOFT_HARD(name) (g_use_hard_fpu ? gen_helper_##name##__hard : gen_helper_##name##__soft)`
translate.c:2207-2218 gen_frndint: `if (((s->flags >> HF_FPU_RC_SHIFT) & 3) != 0) { gen_helper_frndint(tcg_env); return; }`
config_spec.yml:402-404 `hard_fpu: type: bool default: true`
Empirically verified on this box (MSYS2 mingw64 gcc, /tmp/cwtest.c): default x87 CW = 0x037f (PC=3 extended, RC=0 nearest) and `fesetround(FE_DOWNWARD)` moves it to 0x077f AND MXCSR 0x1f80->0x3f80.
confirmed.apple_impact: none on Apple Silicon — the `defined(__aarch64__)` branch is untouched and still owns the arm64 path. macOS x86_64 (Intel) hosts get the same correctness fix as Windows/Linux x86_64, i.e. a strict improvement, never a regression.
confirmed.verifier_notes:
Two viable fixes; either keeps macOS arm64 untouched.

(A) Minimal blast radius, matches the documented intent: in the four `#if !defined(__aarch64__)` fallback sites in target/i386/tcg/translate.c (gen_fistl_ST0 ~2103, gen_fistll_ST0 ~2114, gen_fist_ST0 ~2137, gen_frndint ~2216) call the un-remapped soft symbol explicitly: `gen_helper_fistl_ST0__soft(arg, tcg_env)`, `gen_helper_fistll_ST0__soft`, `gen_helper_fist_ST0__soft`, `gen_helper_frndint__soft(tcg_env)`. This is safe because floatx80 is a union overlaying `long double fval` on the same {low, high} bits (include/fpu/softfloat-types.h:105-111), so soft and hard helpers share the ST register representation, and the soft path already gets the guest RC via set_x86_rounding_mode -> set_float_rounding_mode. Cost: softfloat speed only in directed-rounding cases.

(B) Root-cause fix: add an x86_64 arm to set_x86_rounding_mode (fpu_helper.c ~1186) that programs ONLY the x87 CW RC field via `fnstcw`/`fldcw` (do not use fesetround — on mingw-w64 it also rewrites MXCSR, which gen_flcr and the SSE hostfp bracket own): `cw = (cw & ~0x0C00) | (mode << 10)`; guest RC encoding matches CW bits 11:10 one-to-one. This makes the __hard rintl/llrintl AND the inline tcg_out_frndint path honour the guest RC (the tcg-target.c.inc:3256 comment could then be updated), and also makes pack()'s (float)/(double) casts (x87 fstps/fstpl) honour RC. confirmed.title: DXGI presenter self-disables on NVIDIA: interop FBO completeness checked while WGL_NV_DX_interop object is unlocked
confirmed.description: In HEAD, CreateSharedResources() attaches the interop texture (registered via wglDXRegisterObjectNV) to m_interop_fbo and calls glCheckFramebufferStatus through the shared create_fbo lambda WITHOUT first locking the object with wglDXLockObjectsNV. Per WGL_NV_DX_interop, a registered object is only usable by GL while locked; NVIDIA returns GL_FRAMEBUFFER_UNSUPPORTED (0x8CDD) for the unlocked texture, create_fbo() fails, Init() returns false, and gl_render_frame() falls back to SDL_GL_SwapWindow with a one-time 'win32_dxgi present failed or unavailable' warning. plausible.title: Pipeline-cache serialize + file write runs synchronously on the PFIFO thread every 30 s; NVIDIA blobs are far larger than MoltenVK's

plausible.title: volkLoadDevice() is never called — every vkCmd* on Windows goes through the vulkan-1.dll loader trampoline
plausible.description:
The renderer initializes volk and calls `volkLoadInstance(r->instance)` but never `volkLoadDevice(r->device)` (or `volkLoadDeviceTable`). volk's instance-level pointers come from `vkGetInstanceProcAddr`, which on Windows returns the *loader's* trampoline for every device-level entry point. Each `vkCmdBindDescriptorSets` / `vkCmdDraw` / `vkCmdBindPipeline` therefore costs an extra indirect call plus the loader's dispatch-table lookup off the VkDevice/VkCommandBuffer handle before reaching the NVIDIA ICD. `volkLoadDevice` replaces those globals with `vkGetDeviceProcAddr` results that enter the ICD directly.

The fork's own measured workload is 408-485 draws per flip with ~14 render passes (architecture contract, Invariant 2 rationale), and each advancing draw issues several vkCmd* calls, so this is on the order of several thousand trampolined calls per frame on the PFIFO thread — exactly the per-draw CPU cost bucket the GPU-frame campaign is trying to shrink. This costs nothing on macOS: MoltenVK is linked as the ICD directly (meson.build `cc.find_library('MoltenVK')`), so there is no loader trampoline to skip there.

Safety: the renderer creates exactly one `VkDevice` (`create_logical_device`, instance.c:471) and one queue, so overwriting volk's global device-level pointers is unambiguous. `volkLoadDevice` only touches device-level entries; instance-level entries (`vkGetPhysicalDevice*`, `vkCreateDebugUtilsMessengerEXT`, `vkDestroyInstance`) keep the pointers from `volkLoadInstance`.

Note that VMA is initialized separately via `vmaImportVulkanFunctionsFromVolk` (instance.c:707) *after* device creation, so it picks up the device-level pointers automatically. Measure with the standard savestate A/B protocol on the Windows box before claiming a number — this is a per-call overhead reduction, so the win scales with draws/flip and may be small in GPU-bound scenes.
plausible.apple_impact: none — MoltenVK is linked directly as the ICD (no loader trampoline), so `volkLoadDevice` resolves to the same function addresses `volkLoadInstance` already produced. Neutral on macOS, not gated.

plausible.title: Physical-device preference matches by name only: two identical GPUs make the Vulkan device diverge from the GL adapter after the first run
plausible.description:
(Upstream-inherited selection logic — flagged because the FOCUS asks for it and because the fork made Vulkan the live Windows default, per docs/windows-gating-audit.md §K.)

`select_physical_device` matches the saved preference against `VkPhysicalDeviceProperties::deviceName` and, because the match loop has no `break`, `preferred_device_index` ends up holding the *last* index whose name matches. It then writes the chosen device's name back into the config (instance.c:459). On a machine with two identical GPUs (e.g. two "NVIDIA TITAN Xp"), the first run has an empty preference and picks index 0; the config is saved as the shared name; every subsequent run matches both entries and lands on index 1.

On the Windows display path this is not cosmetic. The composited frame is shared out of Vulkan by `vkGetMemoryWin32HandleKHR` and imported into GL by `glImportMemoryWin32HandleEXT` (display.c:1269-1279). An OPAQUE_WIN32 handle is only importable by a GL context on the *same* physical device; the WGL context comes from `glo_context_create()` and lands on whichever adapter Windows gives it (normally the primary/index 0). Cross-device import fails, and the guarding `assert(glGetError() == GL_NO_ERROR)` at display.c:1279 aborts (QEMU never defines NDEBUG) — or, if the driver reports success and produces garbage, the game area is black with audio running, i.e. the exact field symptom §Q was chasing. Nothing in the selection path consults `VkPhysicalDeviceIDProperties::deviceUUID`/`deviceLUID` against `GL_DEVICE_UUID_EXT`/`GL_DEVICE_LUID_EXT`, which is what EXT_external_objects provides for precisely this.
plausible.proposed_fix: Two independent hardenings. (1) Disambiguate the preference: query `VkPhysicalDeviceIDProperties` via `vkGetPhysicalDeviceProperties2` and store/compare `deviceUUID` (hex) alongside the human-readable name, and add `break;` once a match is found so the first match wins deterministically. (2) On `HAVE_EXTERNAL_MEMORY`, prefer the physical device whose `deviceUUID`/`deviceLUID` equals the GL context's `GL_DEVICE_UUID_EXT`/`GL_DEVICE_LUID_EXT` (EXT_memory_object / EXT_memory_object_win32), and if no device matches, log it loudly and fail over to the OpenGL renderer rather than aborting inside an assert.
plausible.apple_impact: none — gate the GL-adapter matching under `#if HAVE_EXTERNAL_MEMORY` (0 on Apple). The UUID disambiguation is inert on Apple, which enumerates a single MoltenVK device.

plausible.title: PVIDEO YUV->RGBA compute dispatch consumes a flight-partitioned compute descriptor set with no capacity guard
plausible.description:
The fork's new compute-based PVIDEO conversion calls `pgraph_vk_dispatch_yuv_to_rgba`, which routes through `update_descriptor_sets` (surface-compute.c:463) and consumes one entry of the per-flight-slot compute descriptor-set partition. Every other consumer of that partition checks `pgraph_vk_compute_needs_finish(r)` and forces a `pgraph_vk_finish` first (surface.c:281, texture.c:885, texture.c:1196). The display call site does not.

Because the checking consumers legitimately leave `compute.descriptor_set_index == compute_descriptor_set_limit` after their last allocation (they check *before* consuming, then consume), the display dispatch can arrive with the partition already exhausted. `update_descriptor_sets`'s only protection is `assert(r->compute.descriptor_set_index < r->flight[r->current_flight].compute_descriptor_set_limit)` — which aborts the process (QEMU never defines NDEBUG). Were that assert ever compiled out, the write would target the *other* flight slot's first descriptor set, which the in-flight submission may still be bound to — VUID-vkUpdateDescriptorSets-None-03047 (a descriptor set must not be updated while bound to a command buffer that is pending execution) — or, from the last slot, read past `r->compute.descriptor_sets[8192]`.

This is a new consumer of a partitioned resource added without the guard the architecture contract's Invariant 2 requires ("any new per-something allocation whose cadence can change at runtime needs a capacity guard that degrades gracefully"). It is adjacent to, but distinct from, the "surface-upload compute-descriptor partition guard" already listed as latent in docs/windows-gating-audit.md §R.

Optionally upgrade `update_descriptor_sets`' assert to a graceful degrade consistent with the `begin_draw` REPORTS_FULL pattern.
plausible.apple_impact: none — the guard is platform-neutral and inert whenever the partition has room, which is the steady state on both platforms; it fires only in the exhausted case that today aborts on macOS too.

plausible.title: The fork's new AArch64 FP backend gives INDEX_op_cvt{32,64}f_i{32,64} truncate semantics (FCVTZS) while the pre-existing i386 backend gives them MXCSR-rounded semantics (CVTSD2SI) — same TCG opcode, two different rounding contracts
plausible.description:
The whole AArch64 FP backend is fork divergence (`git show upstream/master:tcg/aarch64/tcg-target.c.inc | grep -c FCVTZS` -> 0; upstream also has no TCG_TARGET_HAS_fpu in tcg/aarch64/tcg-target-has.h). The fork implemented `cvt32f_i32`/`cvt32f_i64`/`cvt64f_i32`/`cvt64f_i64` as FCVTZS — round-toward-zero, ignoring FPCR.RMode. The i386 backend, which predates it, implements the same four opcodes as CVTSS2SI/CVTSD2SI (opcode 0x2d, NOT the truncating 0x2c CVTTSD2SI) — i.e. round per the current MXCSR RC. include/tcg/tcg-opc.h:184-193 documents the intended contract as truncate ("The existing cvtNf_iM opcodes already cover truncate (RZ) mode via FCVTZS"), so the i386 implementation silently violates the fork's own stated contract.

Nothing is currently broken because all five frontend users were patched one by one with `#if !defined(__aarch64__)` escape hatches (gen_fistt_ST0 / gen_fisttl_ST0 / gen_fisttll_ST0 at target/i386/tcg/translate.c:2156-2184, plus gen_fistl_ST0 / gen_fistll_ST0). It also costs Windows x86_64 the inline FISTTP: all three FISTTP widths unconditionally take `gen_helper_fistt*_ST0` there.

plausible.title: Voice-worker count defaults to logical CPU count — 8 threads and ~96 MB/s of fixed reduction traffic on the 4C/8T target
plausible.description:
`voice_work_init` spawns one worker per logical core when `audio.vp.num_workers == 0` (the default). On the target i7-4770K that is 8 worker threads, competing with the TCG vCPU thread, the PFIFO thread and the UI thread for 4 physical cores.

The per-worker cost is *not* proportional to the number of voices it was given: every worker that receives at least one voice pays a fixed `memset(self->mixbins, 0, sizeof(self->mixbins))` (32 bins x 32 floats = 4 KiB) plus a fixed `float_accumulate` reduction of the same 4 KiB into `vwd->mixbins` under `vwd->lock` — the fork's own float_accumulate change sits exactly here. mcpx_apu_vp_frame runs at 1500 Hz (32 samples @ 48 kHz), so with 8 active workers that is 8 x 8 KiB x 1500 = ~96 MB/s of memset+add that exists purely because of the worker count, plus 12000 condvar wakeups/s from `qemu_cond_broadcast(&vwd->work_pending)` (vp.c:2196) and the serialised `vwd->lock` reduction. With 2-4 workers the same voice work is done with a quarter of that overhead.

Windows condvar wake + context switch is materially more expensive than Darwin's, and on 4 physical cores the extra threads cannot actually run in parallel anyway — they just displace the vCPU/PFIFO threads.

If the expected shape holds, change the auto default to something bounded, e.g. `int auto_workers = SDL_GetNumLogicalCPUCores(); #ifdef _WIN32 auto_workers = MIN(auto_workers / 2, 4); #endif` — or, better because it is platform-neutral, scale by the observed active-voice count rather than core count. Keep `audio.vp.num_workers` as the explicit override it already is. Note this line is upstream code; the fork owns the float_accumulate reduction inside the loop.
plausible.apple_impact: gated — put the cap under `#ifdef _WIN32` (or leave the existing auto path for darwin) so the Apple worker count and the measured macOS APU utilisation are untouched.
plausible.verifier_notes: Keep as a low-confidence perf-opportunity, reframed: the actionable overhead is the per-frame broadcast that wakes idle workers and the 8-way SRWLOCK convoy, not memory traffic. Before any default change, A/B with XEMU_APU_PROF=1 (apu.c:244-256 prints utilization/frames per second) at audio.vp.num_workers = 1, 2, 4, 8 on the Windows target using the F-key savestate; g_dbg.vp.total_worker_time_us / workers[i].time_us are available via the debug UI. plausible.title: APU frame thread runs at default priority on Windows with no equivalent of the fork's Apple QoS bumps
plausible.description:
The fork raises scheduling priority on its other latency-critical threads on macOS — `pthread_set_qos_class_self_np(QOS_CLASS_USER_INTERACTIVE, 0)` in pfifo_thread (hw/xbox/nv2a/pfifo.c:502-504) and in the vblank thread — and the Windows gating audit records those as "compiled out; no scheduling change" (table row A6). The APU frame thread has no priority statement on any platform, but it is the one thread in the emulator with a hard 5.33 ms deadline: it must produce an EP frame every EP_FRAME_US or SDL's audio queue underruns (audible crackle).

On the target machine that thread shares 4 physical cores with the TCG vCPU thread, the PFIFO thread (which on Windows is *also* at default priority, unlike macOS), the UI thread and up to 8 voice workers. Windows' scheduler gives none of them any hint about which is deadline-sensitive.

Windows offers two mechanisms this codebase does not currently use anywhere: `SetThreadPriority(GetCurrentThread(), THREAD_PRIORITY_ABOVE_NORMAL)` (cheap, no dependencies) and MMCSS `AvSetMmThreadCharacteristicsW(L"Pro Audio", &idx)` (avrt.lib, the mechanism WASAPI-based audio apps use).

plausible.title: glFinish() downgraded to glFlush() before nv2a_release_framebuffer_surface() — UI reads are no longer complete when the renderer is told the frame is free
plausible.description: The fork replaced upstream's `glFinish()` with `glFlush()` immediately before `nv2a_release_framebuffer_surface()`. That handshake is the *only* thing telling the PFIFO thread it may reuse or destroy the display image. `glFlush` guarantees submission, not completion, so on Windows the PFIFO thread can re-run `pgraph_vk_render_display` into `r->display.image` (the VkDeviceMemory that `gl_texture_id` aliases via `glImportMemoryWin32HandleEXT`) while the UI context's sampling draws are still in flight. Worse, on this path everything that actually *reads* the frame runs after the release: line 1022 releases, then line 1026 `win32_dxgi_present_end_frame()` does the FBO→interop `glBlitFramebuffer` and the D3D11 `CopyResource`/`Present`. The same hazard exists for the GL renderer: `gl_display_buffer` is created in the `g_nv2a_context_display` glo context on the PFIFO thread and consumed in the main-window context (share group via `SDL_GL_SHARE_WITH_CURRENT_CONTEXT`, gloffscreen/sdl.c:52) — OpenGL 4.6 spec Appendix D.3 requires explicit completion (glFinish / sync object) around cross-context object handoff, which `glFlush` does not provide. It is also the release gate the renderer-switch path waits on: `pgraph.c:3681` `while (pg->framebuffer_in_use) qemu_cond_wait(...)` then calls `ops.finalize`, which on Windows runs `glDeleteMemoryObjectsEXT` and closes the imported Win32 memory handle (`vk/display.c:1005-1018`) — doing that while GL commands referencing the memory object are merely flushed is undefined. Either way the barrier must precede `nv2a_release_framebuffer_surface()`; moving the release after `win32_dxgi_present_end_frame()` alone is not sufficient because the blit is still only queued.

plausible.title: Vblank thread priority bump is Apple-only; no Windows equivalent (Invariant 12 has no non-Apple arm)
plausible.description: `vblank_timer_thread` raises itself to `QOS_CLASS_USER_INTERACTIVE` under `#ifdef __APPLE__` only (matching pfifo.c:503). On Windows the thread that owns the fixed 60 Hz guest-vblank deadline runs at THREAD_PRIORITY_NORMAL and competes with the vCPU thread, the PFIFO thread, the APU thread and the UI thread on a 4C/8T Haswell. Missing the deadline is not just a smoothness issue: `process_vblank` → `graphic_hw_update` → `nv2a_vga_gfx_update` raises `NV_PCRTC_INTR_0_VBLANK`, i.e. a *guest* interrupt titles gate simulation on, so late wakeups jitter guest timing. `SDL_DelayPrecise` will busy-spin the tail of the wait to hit the deadline, so under contention the thread also burns a core doing so without ever being scheduled preferentially. This is the direct Windows analogue of the fork's own Invariant 12 and it is currently empty. (This is NOT the reverted 'vblank cadence aligned to host display refresh' experiment — `vblank_interval_ns` stays at the fixed 16666666 ns; only the OS scheduling class changes.)
plausible.proposed_fix: Add an `#elif defined(_WIN32)` arm: `SetThreadPriority(GetCurrentThread(), THREAD_PRIORITY_ABOVE_NORMAL);` (cheap, no dependency). Important semantic difference from a FIFO: every `echo "down 26" > \\.\pipe\xemu` from PowerShell opens and closes a client, which surfaces as ERROR_BROKEN_PIPE/ERROR_NO_DATA on the server; on that, `DisconnectNamedPipe()` and go back to the connect step so successive one-shot writers keep working (a FIFO tolerates writer churn implicitly; a named pipe does not).
