Alternatively the smaller regular-file-tail backend (poll file size via GetFileSizeEx, read appended bytes) is driven trivially by `Add-Content` and avoids the connect/disconnect state machine. Note that this alone does not give Windows the movement-probe class: scripts/movement-probe.sh (zsh, dist/xemu.app, ~/Library toml, MVK_CONFIG exports) and scripts/bench-screenshot.py (Quartz + screencapture) also need a  …[truncated; full text in the session workflow journal]

refuted.title: Aux single-time command buffers are submitted while the pipelined main CB is still executing (upstream's finish drained; the fork's does not)
refuted.why:
The factual premise about control flow is correct: the fork's pgraph_vk_finish (hw/xbox/nv2a/pgraph/vk/draw.c:2020-2023) waits only the *other* slot via pgraph_vk_wait_for_previous_flight (command.c:224-234 waits r->flight[current_flight].fence after the rotation), and pgraph_vk_end_single_time_commands (command.c:110-114) waits only r->aux_fence where upstream did vkQueueWaitIdle. So the just-submitted main CB can indeed still be executing when the aux CB is submitted.

The central technical claim, however, is false: "Vulkan gives same-queue batches submission order but NOT an execution dependency ... so no ordering exists between the two batches." That would only be true if the aux CB contained no synchronization commands. It does. The upload path records, in the aux CB, before any copy into the surface image:

  surface.c:2149-2153
    pgraph_vk_transition_image_layout(pg, cmd, surface->image, ...,
        surface->color ? VK_IMAGE_LAYOUT_COLOR_ATTACHMENT_OPTIMAL : VK_IMAGE_LAYOUT_DEPTH_STENCIL_ATTACHMENT_OPTIMAL,
        VK_IMAGE_LAYOUT_TRANSFER_DST_OPTIMAL);

which is a vkCmdPipelineBarrier (image.c:210-211) with, for color (image.c:147-152):
    srcAccessMask = COLOR_ATTACHMENT_READ|WRITE, dstAccessMask = TRANSFER_WRITE,
    sourceStage = VK_PIPELINE_STAGE_COLOR_ATTACHMENT_OUTPUT_BIT, destinationStage = TRANSFER
and for depth (image.c:171-176):
    sourceStage = EARLY_FRAGMENT_TESTS|LATE_FRAGMENT_TESTS, srcAccess = DS_ATTACHMENT_READ|WRITE.

Per the Vulkan spec (§7.6 vkCmdPipelineBarrier): "If vkCmdPipelineBarrier was recorded outside a render pass instance, the first synchronization scope includes all commands that occur earlier in submission order", and submission order (§7.2) explicitly spans earlier vkQueueSubmit calls on the same queue. Further (§7.1.2), a source stage mask includes "any logically earlier stages", so COLOR_ATTACHMENT_OUTPUT covers every graphics stage of the in-flight main CB (vertex fetch, fragment-shader sampling of this surface as a texture, depth tests, attachment writes/loads/stores/clears). This is exactly the mechanism that orders work across batches on one queue without semaphores; it does not depend on MoltenVK/Metal hazard tracking, and NVIDIA's ICD honours it. The finder's cited spec sentence ("submission order alone does not guarantee...") is true but irrelevant, since the ordering here is not from submission order alone but from the barrier.

I checked whether any earlier-submitted CB touches surface images at stages outside that scope: (a) compute — all vkCmdDispatch sites are in surface-compute.c and there are zero VK_DESCRIPTOR_TYPE_STORAGE_IMAGE uses in vk/*.c, so compute only touches buffers; (b) TRANSFER — texture.c:1442 vkCmdCopyImage(surface->image ...) and surface.c:1662 vkCmdCopyImage(zeta->image ...) are recorded into the main CB via pgraph_vk_begin_nondraw_commands, but each is followed in the same CB by a Src->Color / Src->Depth transition (image.c: sourceStage TRANSFER -> destinationStage COLOR_ATTACHMENT_OUTPUT / fragment tests), which chains with the aux CB's Color->Dst barrier. On Windows the compositor is not async (HAVE_IOSURFACE_SHARING is Apple-only, display.c:1626-1630), so render_display's own CB is a fence-waited single-time CB.

Consequently the claimed failure mode (aux upload racing the in-flight main CB's reads/writes of the same image on a native ICD, "renders wrong on the main path") is not supported: the aux CB's own barriers already establish the execution+memory dependency, exactly as upstream also relied on them inside a single CB. The "high" severity and the proposed full-pipeline drain before every aux CB (which fires on every present under WHPX and on every surface upload/download) are not justified, and the drain would be a significant Windows perf regression for no correctness gain.

Residual, much narrower point (separate from this finding's thesis): the fork changed image.c Color->Dst sourceStage from upstream's VK_PIPELINE_STAGE_ALL_COMMANDS_BIT to COLOR_ATTACHMENT_OUTPUT_BIT (git diff upstream/master...HEAD -- image.c). With upstream's draining finish that narrowing was harmless; in the pipelined fork, cross-submission ordering of any *TRANSFER*-stage access to a surface image in a prior batch now relies on the intervening Src->Color barrier forming a dependency chain rather than on ALL_COMMANDS directly. In the current tree every such access is bracketed by that transition, so it holds, but it is fragile. That is a low-severity hardening nit anchored at image.c:151, not the high-severity race described. || The finding's core premise -- that the aux CB's copies/layout transitions into a SurfaceBinding image have "no ordering" against the still-executing main CB because "submission order alone does not guarantee that commands complete in order" -- is wrong as applied to this code. Submission order alone is indeed not an execution dependency, but the aux CB does not rely on submission order alone: every aux upload begins with a layout-transition pipeline barrier, and core Vulkan (spec 7.6, vkCmdPipelineBarrier) defines that barrier's first synchronization scope as "commands that were submitted to the same queue before it", i.e. it spans earlier vkQueueSubmit batches, not just the current command buffer. The decisive code is hw/xbox/nv2a/pgraph/vk/surface.c:2148-2152, which transitions surface->image from COLOR_ATTACHMENT_OPTIMAL / DEPTH_STENCIL_ATTACHMENT_OPTIMAL to TRANSFER_DST_OPTIMAL before the vkCmdCopyBufferToImage, and hw/xbox/nv2a/pgraph/vk/image.c:143-149 / 164-170 which implement that as `sourceStage = VK_PIPELINE_STAGE_COLOR_ATTACHMENT_OUTPUT_BIT` (srcAccess COLOR_ATTACHMENT_READ|WRITE) and `sourceStage = EARLY_FRAGMENT_TESTS|LATE_FRAGMENT_TESTS` (srcAccess DEPTH_STENCIL_ATTACHMENT_READ|WRITE), dstStage TRANSFER. Per spec 7.1.2 the first scope also includes all logically earlier stages, so the in-flight main CB's fragment-shader samples of the same surface (texture-as-surface reads) are covered too; its TRANSFER-stage touches of the surface (texture.c:1442 vkCmdCopyImage) are bracketed by Src->Color transitions (TRANSFER -> COLOR_ATTACHMENT_OUTPUT, image.c:172-178) that chain into the aux barrier. This is the same core-Vulkan guarantee the fork already relies on for surface reuse (architecture contract Invariant 1 item 3: "ordered against all earlier same-queue submissions by the ... explicit VK_SUBPASS_EXTERNAL dependency -- a core Vulkan guarantee, not a MoltenVK one"). So the image race the finding describes does not exist on a native ICD; MoltenVK is not hiding anything here. Corroborating history: `target_is_active = true` for non-Apple (surface.c:1861-1867) was added in c0d7bb5412 on 2026-07-03, three months AFTER flight-slot pipelining landed (86a2e2bb3e, 2026-04-14) -- the fork's own WHPX repro was fixed by a submit-only (non-draining) finish, which is exactly what you expect if the real hazard was aux-before-recording-CB ordering inversion, not aux-vs-in-flight overlap. The fork's surface.c comment ("Core Vulkan only orders same-queue submissions at execution start") overstates the risk by ignoring the barriers it records. The proposed fix (drain both slots before every aux CB on non-Apple) would serialise the 2-slot pipeline on every surface upload, every texture-as-surface bind, and every present on Windows for a hazard that is not present. Impact-novelty: not new either -- docs/windows-gating-audit.md section Q already parks "pipelined pgraph_vk_finish" as a known, deliberately-not-fixed divergence.

refuted.title: vk_wait_for_fence_or_die's diagnostic is lost on Windows: stderr is a freopen'd buffered file and MSVCRT abort() does not flush
refuted.why:
Both premises of the finding are false for the actual MSYS2 MINGW64 (msvcrt.dll) build.

1. "nothing in the tree calls setvbuf on stderr" is wrong. QEMU's `os-win32.c:58-62`:
```
void os_set_line_buffering(void)
{
    setbuf(stdout, NULL);
    setbuf(stderr, NULL);
}
```
(`setbuf(f, NULL)` == `setvbuf(f, NULL, _IONBF, BUFSIZ)`). It is called from `system/runstate.c:930` in `qemu_init_subsystems()`, which `system/vl.c:3166` calls unconditionally inside `qemu_init()`. xemu's `main()` does the `freopen("xemu.log", "a", stderr)` at `ui/xemu.c:1945-1946` first, then spawns `qemu_main` -> `qemu_init` (ui/xemu.c:1818-1820), so stderr is switched to unbuffered long before the NV2A device / Vulkan renderer (created during machine init later in qemu_init) can ever call `vk_wait_for_fence_or_die` or `VK_CHECK`. Every fprintf from those paths is therefore an immediate write to xemu.log.

2. Even ignoring (1), msvcrt.dll's `abort()` DOES flush stdio buffers, so the cited `command.c:53 abort()` path never loses its message. Verified with a test program built by the exact toolchain (`/c/msys64/mingw64/bin/gcc.exe` 16.2.0, `-O2 -std=gnu11 -D__USE_MINGW_ANSI_STDIO=1`, links msvcrt.dll like dist/xemu.exe) that mirrors ui/xemu.c (CreateFileA + freopen "a" + `_set_error_mode(_OUT_TO_STDERR)` + fprintf):
   - no setbuf, `abort()`            -> xemu.log = 73 bytes, both lines present
   - no setbuf, `TerminateProcess()` -> xemu.log = 0 bytes (proves the stream *was* fully buffered and that abort itself flushed it)
   - no setbuf, `__builtin_trap()`   -> xemu.log = 0 bytes (message lost)
   - with `setbuf(stderr, NULL)` after prior I/O on the freopen'd stream (as QEMU does): abort, `__builtin_trap`, and TerminateProcess all -> 52 bytes, both lines present.

So the only sub-case where the description had a grain of truth (the `VK_CHECK` `__builtin_trap()` at debug.h:59, which is fork code replacing upstream's `assert`) is already neutralised in the real process by QEMU's `os_set_line_buffering()`. The Vulkan diagnostic is not lost on Windows in either the timeout or the VK_ERROR_DEVICE_LOST branch; the severity-medium claim that "the user gets an xemu.log that ends before the diagnostic" does not hold. The docs §M `Application Error` field report was a debug build of the *OpenGL* renderer crashing in a VM and is unrelated to stdio buffering.

Minor: the TDR-2s / VK_ERROR_DEVICE_LOST remark is plausible but irrelevant once the buffering premise falls. || Refuted on two independent grounds, one empirical and one from the tree's own init path.

(1) The tree already unbuffers stderr on Windows before any NV2A Vulkan code runs. os-win32.c:58-62 defines `void os_set_line_buffering(void) { setbuf(stdout, NULL); setbuf(stderr, NULL); }`. system/runstate.c:925-930 calls it unconditionally from `qemu_init_subsystems()` (no XBOX/_WIN32 bypass), and system/vl.c:3166 invokes `qemu_init_subsystems()` early in `qemu_init()` — long before `qemu_create_machine` (vl.c:4037) and `qmp_x_exit_preconfig` -> `qemu_init_board` -> `machine_run_board_init` (vl.c:2773), which is where NV2A realize -> `pgraph_init` (hw/xbox/nv2a/nv2a.c:243) -> `pg->renderer->ops.init` = `pgraph_vk_init` (pgraph.c:597-598, vk/renderer.c:405) happens. The `freopen("xemu.log","a",stderr)` at ui/xemu.c:1945-1947 runs in `main()` before the `qemu_main` thread calls `qemu_init` (xemu.c:1818-1820), so `setbuf(stderr, NULL)` is applied to the freopen'd log stream and stderr is `_IONBF` by the time any `VK_CHECK` (`debug.h:54-61`, `__builtin_trap()`) or `vk_wait_for_fence_or_die` (`command.c:53`, `abort()`) can fire. The finding's statement "nothing in the tree calls setvbuf on stderr" is wrong — `setbuf(stderr, NULL)` is the `setvbuf(_IONBF)` it asks for.

(2) Empirical test with the actual target toolchain (/c/msys64/mingw64/bin/gcc, -O2 -std=gnu11, links msvcrt.dll; run both with plain MSVCRT fprintf and with -D__USE_MINGW_ANSI_STDIO=1): `freopen(log,"a",stderr); fprintf(...); abort();` -> GetFileSize before exit = 0 (stderr IS fully buffered, as the finding says) but the final log holds the full 65-byte diagnostic. Identical result for `_exit(3)` and even raw `ExitProcess(3)`: msvcrt.dll's DLL_PROCESS_DETACH flushes stdio on any orderly exit, so "MSVCRT abort() does not flush stdio buffers" is false in practice — the `abort()` branch the finding targets was never lossy. Only `__builtin_trap()` (ud2 -> unhandled exception, no DLL detach) lost the bytes (0-byte log) — and that case is exactly what `setbuf(stderr, NULL)` from (1) fixes: tested `setbuf(stderr,NULL)` before or after the fprintf then `__builtin_trap()` -> 65 bytes already on disk before the trap, in both stdio flavours.

The docs §M field report cited as corroboration does not support the finding either: that xemu.log did contain `pfifo heartbeat iters=1`, i.e. stderr logging into xemu.log was working; what was missing there was a usable WER dump, not a stderr line. Practical effect of the proposed change on this machine: nil (already handled).

refuted.title: Byte-exact vertex-conflict refinement memcmps a mapped Vulkan buffer with no HOST_CACHED check
refuted.why:
The code quoted in the finding is accurate (hw/xbox/nv2a/pgraph/vk/vertex.c:128 `const uint8_t *mirror = r->storage_buffers[BUFFER_VERTEX_RAM].mapped;` and :143-144 `memcmp(mirror + lo, data + (lo - offset), hi - lo)`; hw/xbox/nv2a/pgraph/vk/buffer.c:43-44 records only `is_coherent`), and it is fork divergence (git diff upstream/master...HEAD shows +269 lines in vertex.c including this function). But the claim that this is a Windows perf hazard does not hold for the stated target, and the finding itself concedes the point ("On the target NVIDIA/Windows configuration a HOST_CACHED|HOST_COHERENT type exists so the default is fine").

I positively verified that concession on the actual target machine. `C:\Windows\System32\vulkaninfo.exe` (TITAN Xp, driver 561.9, Vulkan 1.3.280) lists memoryTypes[9] = `HOST_VISIBLE_BIT | HOST_COHERENT_BIT | HOST_CACHED_BIT` (heap 1, system RAM), alongside [8] = HOST_VISIBLE|HOST_COHERENT and [10] = DEVICE_LOCAL|HOST_VISIBLE|HOST_COHERENT (BAR heap 2). The in-tree VMA (subprojects/VulkanMemoryAllocator/include/vk_mem_alloc.h:4271-4290) for `VMA_MEMORY_USAGE_AUTO_PREFER_HOST` + `HOST_ACCESS_RANDOM_BIT` (buffer.c:63-67) does `outPreferredFlags |= VK_MEMORY_PROPERTY_HOST_CACHED_BIT;` and `outRequiredFlags |= VK_MEMORY_PROPERTY_HOST_VISIBLE_BIT;` ("Always CPU memory"), and the type selector at :14311-14321 picks the type minimising `VMA_COUNT_BITS_SET(preferredFlags & ~currFlags) + VMA_COUNT_BITS_SET(currFlags & notPreferredFlags)`, early-exiting at cost 0. Type 9 has cost 0; types 8 and 10 cost 1. So on this NVIDIA/Windows build BUFFER_VERTEX_RAM is deterministically placed in write-back-cached host memory and the memcmp runs at full cached speed. The GPU never writes this buffer (usage is VERTEX_BUFFER_BIT only, buffer.c:119), so no invalidate is needed either; the CPU is comparing bytes it wrote itself at vertex.c:244.

What remains is a hypothetical "any Windows ICD without a HOST_CACHED type". No shipping Windows desktop ICD (NVIDIA, AMD, Intel) lacks one; the VMA comment's example of a platform without HOST_CACHED is Raspberry Pi (#362), not Windows. Even on such a device the code stays correct (Invariant 4 is not at risk; it only affects speed), and the "large per-write regression" magnitude is unsubstantiated: the memcmp is bounded to the recorded span intersection per page (<=4 KiB), terminates at the first differing byte, and its alternative is `pgraph_vk_finish` + `pgraph_vk_wait_slot_fence` (vertex.c:215-216) - a submit plus GPU drain costing hundreds of microseconds to milliseconds - so a WC-memory read of a few KiB would still very plausibly be the cheaper branch. The finding therefore describes a non-reproducible hazard on the target configuration, with an overstated consequence on a configuration that does not exist among Windows ICDs. || The finding is technically accurate that no code checks VK_MEMORY_PROPERTY_HOST_CACHED_BIT (grep of hw/, ui/ finds zero hits; buffer.c:43-44 records only `is_coherent`), but it fails on both impact and novelty.

Impact on the target machine: none, by the finder's own admission. NVIDIA (and AMD, and Intel iGPU) Windows ICDs all expose a HOST_VISIBLE|HOST_COHERENT|HOST_CACHED type, and VMA selects it: vk_mem_alloc.h:4272-4275 `if(hostAccessRandom) { // Prefer cached. Cannot require it, because some platforms don't have it (e.g. Raspberry Pi - see #362)! outPreferredFlags |= VK_MEMORY_PROPERTY_HOST_CACHED_BIT; }`. The only known platform lacking it is Raspberry Pi/V3DV, which is out of scope for this audit. The failure scenario ("any Windows ICD without one") is hypothetical with no concrete Windows driver named.

Novelty/premise: the claim "Upstream only ever *wrote* through this mapping; the fork added reads" is false for the relevant memory class. BUFFER_VERTEX_RAM (buffer.c:117-121) uses the identical `host_alloc_create_info` (buffer.c:63-67, AUTO_PREFER_HOST | HOST_ACCESS_RANDOM_BIT) as BUFFER_STAGING_DST, and upstream already reads whole surfaces back through that class every download: upstream/master surface.c:449-458 `vmaMapMemory(...)` then `memcpy_image(gl_read_buf, mapped_memory_ptr, surface->pitch, ...)`; the fork does the same at surface.c:578 (`memcpy_image(gl_read_buf, r->storage_buffers[BUFFER_STAGING_DST].mapped, ...)`), plus texture.c:1571 and display.c:555 read/write STAGING_SRC. If a Windows ICD ever landed these allocations in write-combining memory, surface downloads (hundreds of KiB to MiB per download) would be the catastrophic regression, and the vertex memcmp (bounded to the intersection of a <=4 KiB page span with the incoming write, only on pages already tracked in the current flight slot) would be a rounding error on top of it. Guarding only the vertex path would not fix the real problem in that hypothetical.

Already covered: docs/windows-gating-audit.md:45 row B3 explicitly evaluates the byte-exact refinement for Windows and concludes "memcmp semantics are host-neutral" with the XEMU_VTX_EXACT=0 hatch as the escape. The finding adds no new hazard beyond that assessment.

Correctness is not in question: the mirror is host-written/GPU-read only, so host reads see host writes without any invalidate regardless of coherence; the refinement's safe direction (Invariant 4) is preserved.

refuted.title: Non-Apple surface upload pays a full submit per upload that is no longer even a full finish; recording into the main CB is spec-legal and removes the stall
refuted.why:
The finding's core claim -- that the non-Apple `target_is_active = true` (hw/xbox/nv2a/pgraph/vk/surface.c:1865-1867) makes every upload pay a forced submit, "at least one extra submit per flip plus one per guest CPU write" -- is false for a Windows build.

(1) `pgraph_vk_finish` (hw/xbox/nv2a/pgraph/vk/draw.c:1915-1921) only ends/submits a command buffer inside `if (r->in_command_buffer) { ... }`. When no main CB is open it performs only `pgraph_vk_compute_finish_complete(r)` (a single index reset, surface-compute.c:497-501) and staging buffer_offset/limit resets -- no vkQueueSubmit, no fence wait.

(2) The Apple gate is `(surface == r->color_binding) || (surface == r->zeta_binding) || r->in_command_buffer`. Whenever `in_command_buffer` is true (the only case a finish can submit), the Apple expression is also true, so Apple and non-Apple finish identically. Whenever it is false, the non-Apple finish is the no-op above. Hence the `#else true` branch never produces a submit that the Apple branch does not also produce; the submit-count difference is exactly zero.

(3) On the per-flip path (hw/xbox/nv2a/pgraph/vk/display.c:1613-1618), `render_display` runs `pgraph_vk_finish(pg, VK_FINISH_REASON_PRESENTING)` when the open CB touched the surface, leaving `in_command_buffer == false`, so the SURFACE_CREATE finish inside the upload does not submit. Also the "force-uploads on every present" is `pgraph_vk_upload_surface_data(d, surface, !tcg_enabled())` -- only under a hardware accelerator, not under TCG.

(4) The "no longer delivers the GPU-idle guarantee" claim mischaracterises the path: every upload ends in `pgraph_vk_end_single_time_commands` (hw/xbox/nv2a/pgraph/vk/command.c:95-118) which does `vkQueueSubmit(..., r->aux_fence)` followed by `vk_wait_for_fence_or_die(r->device, r->aux_fence, ...)`. Per the Vulkan spec (Fences: fence signal operations defined by vkQueueSubmit include in their first synchronization scope all commands earlier in submission order), that wait implies every earlier main-CB submission on the single queue has completed. The aux CB's Color/Depth->Dst barriers (image.c:150/174) additionally order GPU-side against in-flight draws by submission order. So the ordering guarantee is delivered on both platforms, independent of the finish.

(5) Upstream baseline (upstream/master surface.c:958) calls `pgraph_vk_finish(pg, VK_FINISH_REASON_SURFACE_CREATE)` unconditionally and upstream's finish did `vkWaitForFences(command_buffer_fence)`; the fork's non-Apple branch is strictly cheaper than upstream.

What survives is only a platform-neutral observation: the synchronous aux_fence wait per upload is a full GPU drain on both macOS and Windows. Recording the upload into the main CB is a plausible future optimisation, but it (a) is not the defect claimed, (b) affects macOS equally so a Windows-only gate would leave the primary target unchanged for no reason, (c) depends on staging sub-allocation the finder defers to another finding (memcpy_image writes BUFFER_STAGING_SRC at offset 0 every upload), and (d) on the render_display path the upload would still need to be submitted before the separate compositor/aux CB reads the image, so the submit would move rather than vanish. The only concrete residue is that the non-Apple comment's phrase "Keep the upstream full-finish semantics" is slightly stale since the fork's finish no longer waits on its own CB. || The finding's core claim ("every pgraph_vk_upload_surface_data on non-Apple buys a forced submit + partial fence wait; at least one extra submit per flip") is false on inspection. hw/xbox/nv2a/pgraph/vk/draw.c:1915-1922: `void pgraph_vk_finish(...) { ... if (r->in_command_buffer) { ... vkEndCommandBuffer ... vkQueueSubmit ... } ... }` — with no CB recording, finish submits nothing and only runs `pgraph_vk_compute_finish_complete(r)` (surface-compute.c:497-501, resets a descriptor index) and re-bases the staging offsets. In the render_display path the finder cites as the per-flip cost, hw/xbox/nv2a/pgraph/vk/display.c:1611-1618 runs `pgraph_vk_finish(pg, VK_FINISH_REASON_PRESENTING)` when a CB with newer draws is open and then `pgraph_vk_upload_surface_data(d, surface, !tcg_enabled())`, so `in_command_buffer == false` and the non-Apple SURFACE_CREATE finish is a no-op. For every other caller — update_surface_part (surface.c:2646/2655) passing r->color_binding/r->zeta_binding, and bind_textures (texture.c:1754) mid-frame with a CB open — the Apple gate `target_is_active = (surface == r->color_binding) || (surface == r->zeta_binding) || r->in_command_buffer` (surface.c:1860-1863) is also true, so Apple finishes identically. The `#else target_is_active = true` branch never yields observably different GPU work vs macOS; this is exactly what docs/windows-gating-audit.md row A1 already records, and upstream itself finishes unconditionally here (upstream surface.c:958 `pgraph_vk_finish(pg, VK_FINISH_REASON_SURFACE_CREATE)`). The real per-upload stall is the aux-CB submit + `vk_wait_for_fence_or_die(r->device, r->aux_fence, ...)` in pgraph_vk_end_single_time_commands (command.c:95-118), which is platform-neutral and already documented (docs/optimizations.md:640-643) — not a Windows-specific perf opportunity. The proposed fix is also unsound for the very path it cites: render_display immediately records the compositor into a separately submitted single-time CB (display.c:1627-1629 `pgraph_vk_begin_single_time_commands(pg)`) that samples surface->image, so an upload recorded into the unsubmitted main CB would not have executed before the compositor reads the image (stale/garbage frame) unless a finish is inserted — reintroducing the submit. It further requires per-flight partitioning of BUFFER_COMPUTE_DST/SRC (texture.c:1004: "single, shared") and sub-allocating the offset-0 `memcpy_image(copy_buffer->mapped, ...)` write (surface.c:1937), i.e. a general renderer refactor, not a Windows gating fix. Nothing here matters differently on the TITAN Xp than on macOS.

refuted.title: Inline DSP JIT UI toggle is gated on __APPLE__ but the engine is gated on POSIX aarch64, hiding it from Linux arm64
refuted.why:
The code facts in the finding are accurate, but the finding has no bearing on the audit target and is refuted on scope grounds (it depends on a code path that cannot execute on Windows).

Verified code:
- ui/xui/main-menu.cc:926: `#if defined(__APPLE__) && defined(__aarch64__)` wraps `Toggle("DSP JIT (Apple Silicon)", &g_config.audio.dsp_jit.enabled, ...)`.
- hw/xbox/mcpx/apu/dsp/interp/dsp56k_jit_arm64.h:24-27: `#if defined(__aarch64__) && !defined(_WIN32)` / `#define DSP56K_JIT_SUPPORTED 1` else `0`.
- hw/xbox/mcpx/apu/dsp/dsp.c:120-127: `dsp_want_external_jit_engine()` honours `g_config.audio.dsp_jit.enabled` only under `#if DSP56K_JIT_SUPPORTED`.
- interp/meson.build:3-6 confirms the widening intent ("Linux arm64 runs it too, and CI tests it there"); commit 2f6c6d691c "dsp: admit POSIX aarch64 hosts to the DSP56K JIT (Linux arm64)".

So the two gates do disagree exactly on Linux aarch64 (toggle hidden, engine present). However, for the audit's target — MSYS2 MINGW64 x86_64 on Windows 10, and the secondary Windows ARM64 llvm-mingw build — both preprocessor conditions evaluate to false (`__aarch64__` undefined on x86_64; `_WIN32` defined on Windows ARM64), so the toggle is hidden and the engine compiles out identically. There is no Windows behaviour difference, no compile/link issue, and no perf opportunity here. The finder itself concedes "Correct and harmless on Windows". Under the verifier rule "depends on a code path that cannot execute on Windows, refute it", this is refuted as out of scope; it is a Linux-arm64 UI nit, not a Windows finding. Note also that docs/windows-gating-audit.md row A10 still states the old `__APPLE__ && __aarch64__` gate while row F3 states the new one — the finding's cited docs are internally stale, though that does not change the conclusion.

refuted.title: QEMU monitor is driven over an AF_UNIX socket; Windows CPython has no socket.AF_UNIX so loadvm can never be issued
refuted.why:
The narrow technical fact is true (native CPython 3.14.7 MSC on this machine reports `hasattr(socket,'AF_UNIX') == False`; I re-ran the probe), but the finding's central claim — that the AF_UNIX monitor transport is what makes the savestate A/B / probe / soak protocols "dead on Windows", and that a transport shim would fix it "rather than forking the scripts" — is false. These four scripts are macOS-only end to end and fail long before line 245/252/277 is ever reached:

- `scripts/bench-savestate-ab.sh:1` `#!/bin/zsh`, `:82` `ROOT=${0:a:h:h}` (zsh modifiers), `:136` `: ${CONFIG_SRC:=$HOME/Library/Application Support/xemu/xemu/xemu.toml}` (macOS config path; Windows is %APPDATA%\xemu\xemu), `:156-157` `cp -Rc $APP_SRC $APP ... APPBIN=$APP/Contents/MacOS/xemu` (clones `dist/xemu.app`, a bundle that a Windows build never produces; APPBIN does not exist so `set -e` aborts or the launch at :252 is a dead run regardless of transport), `:177` `cp -c` APFS clonefile, `:229` `strings $MVK_DYLIB` MoltenVK version, `:296` `ps -o %cpu= -p $pid`, and the mid-run screenshot `scripts/bench-screenshot.py:33-35,108` uses `import Quartz` / `CGWindowListCopyWindowInfo` / `screencapture -l`.
- `probe-run.sh:10,19`, `soak-cycles.sh:11,23`, `movement-probe.sh:56-60` likewise hardcode `$HOME/Library/Application Support/...`, `cp -Rc ... .app`, `Contents/MacOS/xemu`, plus `mkfifo` for the XEMU_INPUT_PIPE input path.

So the socket family is one of roughly ten macOS-native dependencies, not the gating one; the proposed `unix:`->`tcp:` shim plus a Python `create_connection` probe would leave every script still non-functional on Windows. The "blocker" severity is also misapplied by the task's own definition (won't compile/link, crash/hang/render wrong on Windows) — this is a developer benchmark harness that was written for the dev Mac, and docs/windows-gating-audit.md item 6 already records that "Windows needs its own savestate A/B baseline" as open work. Side note: the finding's secondary claim that `-monitor unix:` cannot work on a native xemu.exe is also weak — util/qemu-sockets.c has no `_WIN32` exclusion around `unix_listen_saddr` (`:1012 un.sun_family = AF_UNIX`) and Windows 10 1803+ supports AF_UNIX sockets; the real problems are the `/tmp` pseudo-path and the CPython client, both moot given the above.

The one accurate, non-duplicated residue is documentation drift: `.claude/skills/xemu-frontier-and-positioning/SKILL.md:380-382` asserts `scripts/bench-savestate-ab.sh` is "portable, none macOS-gated ... applies unmodified once a build reaches real hardware", which the code above contradicts. That is a low-severity docs finding, not the blocker claimed. || The cited code is accurate (scripts/bench-savestate-ab.sh:277 `s = socket.socket(socket.AF_UNIX)`; native CPython 3.14.7 on this box reports AF_UNIX=False), but the finding mischaracterizes a macOS-only dev harness as a Windows blocker with a single point of failure. The script is `#!/bin/zsh` (zsh is MISSING on this MSYS2 install, so it never gets to line 277), clones `dist/xemu.app` and runs `$APP/Contents/MacOS/xemu` (:135,:157), reads `$HOME/Library/Application Support/xemu/xemu/xemu.toml` (:136), uses APFS `cp -c` (:177,:183), exports MVK_CONFIG_* (:219-223), scrapes `libMoltenVK.dylib` (:228), calls `screencapture -l` via bench-screenshot.py:108 (MISSING here), and samples with `ps -o %cpu=` (:302). probe-run.sh, soak-cycles.sh and movement-probe.sh share the identical `#!/bin/zsh` + `.app/Contents/MacOS/xemu` + `cp -c` + MVK scaffolding. The harness is documented as macOS-only (`.claude/skills/xemu-testing/SKILL.md:15` "benchmarking and debugging this fork on macOS"), and the already-accepted Windows policy for POSIX automation facilities is "absent by design" (docs/windows-gating-audit.md A12 for XEMU_INPUT_PIPE; archaeology 8.2: "every POSIX-flavored automation facility needs a Windows story, even if the story is 'absent'"). On the emulator side there is no defect at all: QEMU's util/qemu-sockets.c supports `unix:` sockets on win32, so xemu.exe would serve `-monitor unix:` fine — only the client and the surrounding macOS scaffolding are non-portable. The proposed tcp: shim would remove one of ~8 hard blockers and leave the harness equally dead, so it does not deliver the claimed value; it is out of the audit's scope (fork runtime/build behaviour on Windows), affects no Windows user or receipt, and is not a new observation relative to the documented macOS-only status. Practical impact on the target machine: none.

refuted.title: `ps -o %cpu=` is unsupported by MSYS ps, and the `|| break` silently truncates every bench run to 5 seconds
refuted.why:
The isolated facts in the finding check out: on this MSYS2 box `ps -o %cpu= -p $$` prints `ps: unknown option -- o` (ps is cygwin 3.4.10), and `scripts/bench-savestate-ab.sh:300-302` does read `for j in $(seq 1 $n); do / sleep 5 / ps -o %cpu= -p $pid >> $cpul 2>/dev/null || break`. But the claimed failure scenario ("every bench run silently truncated to 5 s, scene gate reports INVALID for every arm") cannot execute on Windows because the script never reaches line 302 there:

- Line 1: `#!/bin/zsh`. zsh is not installed in this MSYS2 environment (`which zsh` -> not found) and is not part of a default MSYS2 install. The script also uses zsh-only syntax (`ROOT=${0:a:h:h}` line 84, `typeset -a pos` line 90, `${BIN_SHA[1,16]}` line 230), so it does not run under MSYS bash either.
- Line 135: `: ${APP_SRC:=$ROOT/dist/xemu.app}` and line 139: `[[ -d $APP_SRC ]] || { echo "no app bundle at $APP_SRC (build first, or --app)" >&2; exit 1; }` — a Windows build produces `build/qemu-system-i386.exe`/`dist/xemu.exe`, not an `.app` directory, so this hard-exits.
- Line 136: `: ${CONFIG_SRC:=$HOME/Library/Application Support/xemu/xemu/xemu.toml}` followed by line 140 `[[ -f $CONFIG_SRC ]] || exit 1` — macOS path.
- Lines 154-156: `cp -Rc $APP_SRC $APP ...; APPBIN=$APP/Contents/MacOS/xemu; [[ -x $APPBIN ]] || exit 1` — requires bundle layout even if `--app` is passed.
- Lines 228-229: `shasum -a 256`, `strings $MVK_DYLIB` on `Contents/Libraries/*/libMoltenVK.dylib`; lines 220-224 export MVK_CONFIG_*; `scripts/bench-screenshot.py` uses the Quartz window list and `screencapture -l`.

So the harness is a macOS-only tool end to end; the `ps -o` line is one of a dozen macOS-only dependencies, not a Windows defect that "silently" produces wrong benchmark numbers. No Windows benchmark can be produced by this script at all, so nothing is being silently truncated or misreported. The "blocker" severity (crash/hang/wrong output on Windows) is unfounded, and the proposed `cpu_sample()` dispatch would be dead code without a full Windows port of the launcher/bundle/screenshot/sha plumbing.

The only accurate residual is a documentation inconsistency: `.claude/skills/xemu-frontier-and-positioning/SKILL.md:381` states "`build.sh`, `XEMU_NV2A_NSPROF`, and `scripts/bench-savestate-ab.sh` are all portable, none macOS-gated ... the exact protocol used on this Mac applies unmodified once a build reaches real hardware", which is false for the bench script. That is a separate low-severity docs/test-harness finding, not the finding as stated. || The technical premise is accurate (MSYS2 `ps` prints `Usage: ps [-aefls] [-u UID] [-p PID]` — no `-o`; and `$!` is the MSYS pid), but line 302 is unreachable on Windows, so the claimed consequence ("every bench run silently truncated to 5 s, scene gate reports INVALID") cannot occur on this machine.

`scripts/bench-savestate-ab.sh` is an Apple-only harness end to end, not a portable script with one bad line:
- Line 1: `#!/bin/zsh` — zsh is not installed in this MSYS2 environment (`which zsh` -> not found); `${0:a:h:h}` at line 84 is zsh-only syntax.
- Line 135-136: `: ${APP_SRC:=$ROOT/dist/xemu.app}` / `: ${CONFIG_SRC:=$HOME/Library/Application Support/xemu/xemu/xemu.toml}`.
- Line 141: `[[ -d $APP_SRC ]] || { echo "no app bundle at $APP_SRC (build first, or --app)" >&2; exit 1; }` — the Windows build produces `dist/xemu.exe` + DLLs (verified: `ls dist` shows SDL3.dll, libepoxy-0.dll, ...), no `.app` directory, so the script exits here, ~160 lines before the sampling loop.
- Lines 156-158: `cp -Rc` APFS clone, `APPBIN=$APP/Contents/MacOS/xemu`, `[[ -x $APPBIN ]] || exit 1`.
- Lines 222-226: exports canonical `MVK_CONFIG_*` (MoltenVK-only); line 230-232: `shasum`, `libMoltenVK.dylib` version sniff.
- Line 265: `-monitor unix:$sock,server,nowait` with the Python side using `socket.AF_UNIX`.
- `scripts/bench-screenshot.py` (called at line 307) does `import Quartz` / `CGWindowListCopyWindowInfo` and shells out to `screencapture -l` — macOS-only.

So even with `|| true` and a Windows `cpu_sample()` helper, the harness still would not run on Windows; the proposed two-line fix delivers nothing on the target machine, and the "blocker" severity (implies broken Windows runs) is unfounded because there are no Windows runs of this script. A real Windows bench harness would be a separate port (different launcher, config path under %APPDATA%, TCP monitor socket, Windows screenshot/CPU sampling), which is a new feature rather than a bug fix and is out of scope for "fork divergence that misbehaves on Windows". The finding is also not new in spirit: docs/windows-gating-audit.md A12 already records the input-pipe harness facility as absent on Windows by design, and the xemu-testing skill documents the harness's Quartz/screencapture dependencies as macOS-specific.

refuted.title: movement-probe.sh depends on mkfifo + zsh `print >` into a FIFO; an MSYS FIFO is invisible to a native xemu.exe
refuted.why:
The narrow factual claim (an MSYS/Cygwin `mkfifo` FIFO is not a Windows named pipe a native mingw xemu.exe could open) is plausible, but it is moot and the finding as framed is both already-baselined and exaggerated:

1. The load-bearing dependency is already in the do-not-re-report baseline. `docs/windows-gating-audit.md` row A12: "`ui/xemu-input.c:522` | `XEMU_INPUT_PIPE` FIFO harness | `#ifdef _WIN32` stub — facility absent by design". The code confirms it (`C:\Users\ms\Documents\xemu-macos\ui\xemu-input.c:547-552`):
```c
#ifdef _WIN32
/* POSIX FIFOs (and O_NONBLOCK reads) don't exist on Windows; the
 * test-input channel is a macOS/Linux automation facility. */
static void test_input_poll(void)
{
}
#else
```
On Windows xemu.exe never even calls `getenv("XEMU_INPUT_PIPE")`, so what kind of object `$FIFO` is cannot matter. The finding concedes this ("even if XEMU_INPUT_PIPE were implemented") and its proposed fix is conditional on an unlanded "previous finding".

2. `mkfifo` is not the decisive blocker; the script is wholesale macOS-only and cannot execute on this MSYS2 host regardless of transport (`C:\Users\ms\Documents\xemu-macos\scripts\movement-probe.sh`):
   - `:1 #!/bin/zsh` and `:28 ROOT=${0:a:h:h}` (zsh modifiers) — `which zsh` on this MSYS2 install: "no zsh in (...)".
   - `:55 APP_SRC=$ROOT/dist/xemu.app`, `:59 APPBIN=$APP/Contents/MacOS/xemu` — .app bundle layout; the Windows build produces `xemu.exe`.
   - `:56 CONFIG_SRC=$HOME/Library/Application\ Support/xemu/xemu/xemu.toml` — macOS config location (Windows uses %APPDATA%).
   - `:58/:64 cp -Rc` / `cp -c` — APFS clonefile flags.
   - `:89-93 export MVK_CONFIG_*` — MoltenVK-only.
   - `:100 -monitor unix:$SOCK` + `:114 socket.socket(socket.AF_UNIX)` in the embedded Python — verified `python3 -c "import socket; print(hasattr(socket,'AF_UNIX'))"` prints `False` on this Windows CPython, so `mon()`/`flushes()`/`loadvm` all fail before any FIFO write.
   - `:148 bench-screenshot.py` uses `import Quartz` + `screencapture -l` (`scripts/bench-screenshot.py:33-34,108`).
   The proposed "two-line transport abstraction" would leave every one of these in place; it would not make the probe operable on Windows.

3. Severity "high" is unjustified under the stated rubric (high = wrong behaviour in a common path or large perf win). Nothing in the Windows build or runtime is wrong; this is a portability wish for a macOS validation harness whose non-portability is documented (xemu-testing SKILL.md describes it as an isolation-cloned bundle harness). The "sub-page dirty default differs on Windows" argument actually cuts the other way: Windows keeps the upstream page-granular default (the conservative one), so the TB-flush instrument is less urgently needed there, not more.

Net: no Windows defect, core premise already recorded in the baseline audit (A12), and the cited line is one of ~8 independent macOS-only dependencies — fixing it alone changes nothing. Refuted as a distinct actionable finding. || The cited code is exactly as quoted (scripts/movement-probe.sh:43-45 `FIFO=/tmp/xmp-$$.fifo` / `mkfifo $FIFO`; :135-136 `print "clear" > $FIFO` / `print "$1 $2" > $FIFO`; :99 `XEMU_INPUT_PIPE=$FIFO`), and it is true that an MSYS FIFO is not openable by a native mingw exe. But the finding fails the impact/novelty bar on several independent grounds:

1. Already recorded as absent-by-design. docs/windows-gating-audit.md table A row A12: "`ui/xemu-input.c:522` | `XEMU_INPUT_PIPE` FIFO harness | `#ifdef _WIN32` stub — facility absent by design". ui/xemu-input.c:546-551 confirms: `#ifdef _WIN32 /* POSIX FIFOs (and O_NONBLOCK reads) don't exist on Windows; the test-input channel is a macOS/Linux automation facility. */ static void test_input_poll(void) { }`. xemu-failure-archaeology 8.2 records the decision and its reopen condition: "Reopen if: someone wants Windows input injection — that's a named-pipe port, not an unguard." The finding itself concedes it is contingent on "the named-pipe/file-tail input channel lands (previous finding)" — so it is not a standalone defect, it is a follow-on to a feature request that has not been accepted.

2. The FIFO is not the operative blocker; the script is a macOS app-bundle harness end to end. Line 1 `#!/bin/zsh` (zsh-only `${0:a:h:h}`, `typeset -a`, `print`); :51 `APP_SRC=$ROOT/dist/xemu.app`; :52 `CONFIG_SRC=$HOME/Library/Application\ Support/xemu/xemu/xemu.toml`; :54 `cp -Rc` (APFS clonefile); :55 `APPBIN=$APP/Contents/MacOS/xemu`; :86-93 six `export MVK_CONFIG_*` lines; :63 `cp -c`. Even with a Windows input channel, none of the isolation/launch section runs under MSYS2. Fixing the two FIFO lines as proposed would leave the probe exactly as inoperable on Windows as it is now — the proposed fix does not achieve the claimed outcome.

3. The "this matters on Windows because the sub-page dirty default differs" argument inverts. Commit 0aeb1998c3 gates the fork's sub-page dirty tracking default to Apple, meaning Windows runs the upstream page-granular path — i.e. the code the probe was built to police (fork TB-lifetime/invalidation changes, the v0.11 139-flush bug) is not enabled on Windows. The probe's marginal value there is correspondingly low, not high.

Net: technically true, already documented (A12 / archaeology 8.2), dependent on an unlanded prerequisite, and the proposed fix is insufficient on its own. Not a high-severity Windows defect; at most a low "harness is macOS-only" cleanup note, which is already the documented status.

refuted.title: Scratch-config rewriter writes the harness's own (POSIX/MSYS) paths into hdd_path/eeprom_path, which a native xemu.exe cannot resolve
refuted.why:
The finding treats the TOML path rewriter at scripts/bench-savestate-ab.sh:192-195 as an isolated Windows bug, but that line is unreachable in any native-Windows invocation of this harness, and the failure mode it describes ("surfaces as a DEAD or gate-INVALID run") cannot occur because the script aborts long before the rewriter runs.

Decisive code (all in the fork's diff; the whole file is fork-added, +376 lines):

- Line 1: `#!/bin/zsh` — a zsh script using zsh-only constructs (`${0:a:h:h}`, `typeset -a`, `${(j:,:)INTERLEAVE}`, `${BIN_SHA[1,16]}`). MSYS2 does not ship zsh by default; running it under bash fails at line 84.
- Line 135/139: `: ${APP_SRC:=$ROOT/dist/xemu.app}` / `[[ -d $APP_SRC ]] || { echo "no app bundle at $APP_SRC (build first, or --app)" >&2; exit 1; }` — a Windows build produces `dist/xemu.exe`, not a `.app` directory; hard exit 1.
- Line 136/140: default config is `$HOME/Library/Application Support/xemu/xemu/xemu.toml`; `[[ -f $CONFIG_SRC ]] || exit 1`.
- Lines 156-158: `cp -Rc $APP_SRC $APP ...; APPBIN=$APP/Contents/MacOS/xemu; [[ -x $APPBIN ]] || { echo "clone failed: no executable at $APPBIN" >&2; exit 1; }` — even with `--app`, it requires a macOS bundle layout with an executable at `Contents/MacOS/xemu`. Exit 1 before line 187.
- Only after all of that does the rewriter at 187-200 run. So on Windows the script dies at line 139 or 158 with an explicit error, never at "after boot begins".

Even hypothetically past that point, the launch/measurement path is Apple-only end to end: `-monitor unix:$sock` + Python `socket.AF_UNIX` (line 245-277; an MSYS2/Cygwin Python AF_UNIX socket is a TCP-emulated Cygwin socket and is not interoperable with a native xemu.exe's Winsock AF_UNIX; `[[ -S $sock ]]` would also never see a native socket file as a socket), `ps -o %cpu= -p $pid` (line 302), `shasum -a 256` (227), `strings $APP/Contents/Libraries/*/libMoltenVK.dylib` (228-229), the MVK_CONFIG exports (219-223), and scripts/bench-screenshot.py which imports `Quartz` and shells out to `screencapture -l` (lines 33-47, 108). The sibling scripts named in the fix (probe-run.sh, soak-cycles.sh, movement-probe.sh) are likewise `#!/bin/zsh`, default to `$HOME/Library/Application Support/...`, and launch `$APP/Contents/MacOS/xemu`.

The project already acknowledges this: docs/windows-gating-audit.md:81/88 says "no macOS number transfers; Windows needs its own savestate ... training run of the bench corpus on real Windows hardware." The harness is a macOS-only tool by design, not a portable one with a single path-form bug. A `hostpath()` helper alone would not produce a working Windows harness; the proposed fix addresses roughly one of a dozen macOS-only assumptions, so the finding's severity ("medium", DEAD-run misdiagnosis) is not supported. If a Windows harness is ever wanted, it needs a separate port (or a PowerShell/bash rewrite), at which point path form is one item on a much longer list. || The cited rewriter (scripts/bench-savestate-ab.sh:190-199, `line = "hdd_path = '%s'\n" % hdd`) is unreachable on Windows, so the path-form question never arises. The script is `#!/bin/zsh` and hard-exits long before line 193 on this machine:

- `: ${APP_SRC:=$ROOT/dist/xemu.app}` (line 135) then `[[ -d $APP_SRC ]] || { echo "no app bundle at $APP_SRC ..."; exit 1; }` (line 139). On the Windows tree `dist/` holds `xemu.exe` + DLLs (SDL3.dll, libepoxy-0.dll, ...) and no `.app` directory, so the script exits here.
- `: ${CONFIG_SRC:=$HOME/Library/Application Support/xemu/xemu/xemu.toml}` (line 136) and `[[ -f $CONFIG_SRC ]] || exit 1` — the macOS config location, not %APPDATA%.
- `APPBIN=$APP/Contents/MacOS/xemu; [[ -x $APPBIN ]] || exit 1` (lines 157-158), `cp -Rc`/`cp -c` APFS clones, `shasum -a 256`, `strings .../libMoltenVK.dylib` for the receipt, exported `MVK_CONFIG_*`, and `/tmp/xemu-bench.$$.*.sock` unix monitor sockets.
- The mandatory visual gate `scripts/bench-screenshot.py` does `import Quartz` / `Quartz.CGWindowListCopyWindowInfo` and shells out to `screencapture -l` (lines 33-35, 108).
- zsh is not present in this MSYS2 environment (`which zsh` returns nothing; only cygpath exists).

The same applies to probe-run.sh, soak-cycles.sh and movement-probe.sh: all are `#!/bin/zsh` and launch `$APP/Contents/MacOS/xemu` (probe-run.sh:40, soak-cycles.sh:44, movement-probe.sh:59). These four scripts are fork-only macOS test tooling (687 added lines vs upstream, no Windows branch anywhere), and the audit brief's Windows-runtime scope is about xemu.exe itself. Adding a `hostpath()`/cygpath shim to the TOML rewriter would fix one line of a script that cannot start on Windows for at least six independent reasons; the practical effect on this machine is nil and the "DEAD/gate-INVALID run" failure mode described cannot occur because no run is ever launched. Even in the hypothetical where the bundle checks were removed, the default `OUT=./bench-out` yields relative forward-slash paths that a native process resolves fine (as the finding itself concedes), so the only failing case is an operator-supplied absolute MSYS outdir.

Not a correctness or perf issue in the emulator, not a new observation about Windows behaviour, and not actionable in isolation. Refuted on impact/novelty grounds.

refuted.title: Binary-identity block depends on `shasum`, `strings` and a MoltenVK dylib; degrades to unknown provenance on Windows
refuted.why:
The finding's premise is that on Windows the harness runs, reaches the binary-identity block at scripts/bench-savestate-ab.sh:227-229, "does not hard-fail", and merely emits a meaningless MoltenVK field. That code path cannot execute on the MSYS2 build. Before line 227 the script does:

  : ${APP_SRC:=$ROOT/dist/xemu.app}                       (line 135)
  [[ -d $APP_SRC ]] || { echo "no app bundle at $APP_SRC (build first, or --app)" >&2; exit 1; }   (line 139)
  ...
  APP=$WORK/xemu-bench.app
  cp -Rc $APP_SRC $APP 2>/dev/null || cp -R $APP_SRC $APP
  APPBIN=$APP/Contents/MacOS/xemu                          (line 155)
  [[ -x $APPBIN ]] || { echo "clone failed: no executable at $APPBIN" >&2; exit 1; }   (line 156)

build.sh on Windows produces dist/xemu.exe + DLLs (build.sh:14 `cp build/qemu-system-i386w.exe dist/xemu.exe`; `ls dist` on this checkout shows SDL3.dll, libglib-2.0-0.dll, ... and no xemu.app). So the script exits 1 at line 139, or — if someone passes `--app <dir>` — at line 156 because `Contents/MacOS/xemu` does not exist. Line 227 (`shasum`), 228 (the libMoltenVK.dylib glob) and 229 (`strings`) are never evaluated, and no receipt.json is written at all. There is no "unknown provenance" receipt to degrade to.

Even setting the bundle check aside, the script is macOS-only end to end, not a portable harness with one Apple-specific block: `#!/bin/zsh` with zsh-only `${0:a:h:h}` (line 84); default CONFIG_SRC `$HOME/Library/Application Support/xemu/xemu/xemu.toml` (line 136); APFS `cp -c` clones (lines 154, 170, 176); `-monitor unix:$sock` driven by an embedded Python client using `socket.AF_UNIX` (line 277), which CPython on Windows does not expose; `ps -o %cpu= -p $pid` (line 302, MSYS2 lacks procps ps -o %cpu); `uptime` in the meta block (line 349); and the mid-run visual check in scripts/bench-screenshot.py imports `Quartz` and shells out to `screencapture -l` (lines 33-34, 108). The identity block is one of the smaller obstacles, so the proposed fix (sha256sum fallback + renaming moltenvk_version to driver_version + a Win32_VideoController probe) would not produce a runnable Windows harness and would not change any observable behaviour on the target.

The finding also cites "shasum /usr/bin/core_perl/shasum" as if the block would run; it does not. The only kernel of truth is that the harness has not been ported to Windows at all — a different, larger work item than the one-block low-severity fix described — and the xemu-frontier-and-positioning skill's statement (SKILL.md:381) that the script is "portable, none macOS-gated" is inaccurate documentation, which is not this finding. On macOS, `shasum -a 256` and `strings` are in the base system and the MoltenVK dylib glob matches the bundle layout, so there is no correctness defect in the block on its own platform either.

clean_areas: vk-cmd: command.c flight-slot allocation/teardown: NUM_FLIGHT_SLOTS*2 CBs from one pool, per-slot fence created SIGNALED + reset before each submit, vkDeviceWaitIdle before destroying fences/semaphores/CBs in pgraph_vk_finalize_command_buffers — no leak, no destroy-while-in-flight.

vk-cmd: command.c retirement watermark: note_slot_retired() takes a monotonic max and is called from both fence-observation sites (pgraph_vk_wait_slot_fence, pgraph_vk_wait_for_previous_flight); reports.c's non-blocking poll routes through pgraph_vk_wait_slot_fence so it also updates the watermark. Matches Invariant 1 clause 3.

vk-cmd: command.c compositor CB ring + VkTimelineSemaphoreSubmitInfo: compiles on MinGW (Vulkan 1.2 headers) but is unreachable on Windows — the only producer, display.c:1626-1628, gates `async_compositor` on `#if HAVE_IOSURFACE_SHARING && xemu_present_is_metal()`, so Windows always takes pgraph_vk_begin_single_time_commands. The 2 idle CBs + 2 fences allocated on Windows are harmless.

vk-cmd: command.c pgraph_vk_init_flight_partitions: descriptor-set, UBO-set, compute-set and all four staging ranges partitioned N ways with base/limit pairs; the current slot's offsets/limits are seeded at init and re-seeded at the tail of pgraph_vk_finish. No cross-slot overlap; integer division truncation only wastes the remainder.

vk-cmd: draw.c aux→main semaphore wait stage (VK_PIPELINE_STAGE_VERTEX_INPUT_BIT | VK_PIPELINE_STAGE_TRANSFER_BIT): correct per Vulkan §7.4 — a semaphore wait blocks the named stages and all logically later ones, so VERTEX_INPUT covers VERTEX_SHADER (the UBO copy's consumer) and FRAGMENT. The main CB issues no compute dispatch that reads the aux-synced buffers.

vk-cmd: draw.c sync_staging_buffer per-slot copy region: srcOffset==dstOffset==slot base, size = offset-base, guarded by `offset > base` so size is never 0 (VUID-VkBufferCopy-size-01988); the following VkBufferMemoryBarrier uses the same offset/size and the correct dst access/stage per destination buffer.

Only NaN diverges (SSE yields -0x800000 via MAXPS's NaN-returns-src2 rule vs the scalar's lrint(NaN)), which is unreachable from mixbin data.

apu: vp.c SSE2 mixbin kernel (vp.c:1897-1919) — de-interleave verified: _MM_SHUFFLE(2,0,2,0) over (L0 R0 L1 R1),(L2 R2 L3 R3) yields L0..L3 and (3,1,3,1) yields R0..R3, matching vDSP_vsma's `&samples[0][b % channels]` with stride 2. NUM_SAMPLES_PER_FRAME == 32 is a multiple of 4 so there is no scalar tail; the widest access (i == 28 reading samples[30][0..3], writing dst[28..31]) is in bounds; loadu/storeu need no alignment guarantee. `b % channels` collapses to 0 for mono, matching the vDSP branch.

apu: float_accumulate (vp.c:50-84) — the vDSP / NEON / SSE2 / scalar arms are numerically identical (plain elementwise add, no reassociation). Both call sites pass multiples of 4 (NUM_SAMPLES_PER_FRAME = 32 for mixbins, NUM_SAMPLES_PER_FRAME*2 = 64 for the flattened sample_buf), so the scalar tails never execute, and the (float*)d->vp.sample_buf flattening is valid for a [32][2] array.

apu: HRTF FIR linearization (vp/hrtf.h:100-170) — index bounds proved: itd_tar is clamped to +/-HRTF_MAX_DELAY_SAMPLES (42) at hrtf.h:62 and itd_cur is a convex smoothing of it, so di <= 42; the deepest read is lin[HRTF_BUFLEN + n - di - HRTF_NUM_TAPS] = 73 + n - 42 - 31 >= 0. The k==0, di==0 tap still reads the current input sample, matching the old push-then-convolve order. The writeback of lin[32..104] with buf_pos = 0 reproduces the circular invariant the next call's two-span copy expects. in == out aliasing is safe because all inputs are prefilled before the first output store. The 840-byte stack array is not a concern for QEMU's 1 MB default Windows thread stacks.

apu: Envelope / attenuation / LPF LUTs — decay LUT algebra verified: (decay_rate*16 - count)*4096/decay_rate == 65536*(1 - count/(decay_rate*16)) exactly, and the LUT form additionally removes the original's int32 overflow for large decay_rate. Endpoint behaviour matches (s == 1 gives exactly 255.0f, so the `value > 255.0f` branch is taken identically). attenuate() and the LPF fc LUT reproduce their powf expressions including the clamp bounds. env_lut_lookup's idx/next/frac arithmetic cannot read past ENV_LUT_SIZE-1. apu_init_luts is called from mcpx_apu_vp_init (vp.c:2317) before voice_work_init spawns any worker, and mcpx_apu_realize calls mcpx_apu_vp_init before creating the frame thread, so there is no initialization race.

apu: setup_svf coefficient cache (vp/svf.h:48-89) — sound: sv->op is compared by pointer identity into the same struct, filters[] is a fixed array that never moves, run_svf mutates only l/b/h/n/p and never f/q/op, and a zero-initialized filter has op == NULL so the first call always takes the full path. The double->float sqrt change is a precision detail well below the 8-bit voice quantization.

apu: Engine-aware mixbuffer bulk handoff (dsp.c:197-207, gp_ep.c:451-472) — address mapping confirmed: GP_DSP_MIXBUF_BASE (apu_regs.h:322) == DSP_MIXBUFFER_BASE (dsp_cpu_regs.h:117) == 0x1400, and NUM_MIXBINS * NUM_SAMPLES_PER_FRAME == 32*32 == 1024 == DSP_MIXBUFFER_SIZE, so the memcpy exactly fills core->mixbuffer[] with the same words write_memory_raw would have stored. Bypassing write_memory_raw's `assert((value & 0xFF000000) == 0)` is safe because float_to_24b/float_to_24b_bulk mask to 0xffffff. The `dsp->ops == &c_dsp_ops` test correctly falls back to the per-sample dsp_write_memory loop for the upstream jit_dsp_ops engine, preserving contract Invariant 5.

apu: Reset-hold runstate gate (apu.c:357-378) — correctly paired: the only path that leaves the frame thread paused is a reset taken while the VM is not running, and mcpx_apu_vm_state_change's running branch (apu.c:400-409) performs dsp_sync_from_vm on both cores and then mcpx_apu_resume. Machine-creation-time reset (PRELAUNCH) is covered by the same handler at vm_start. No Windows-specific behaviour: runstate_is_running() reads a plain global.

apu: DSP engine precedence on Windows — traced end to end. dsp_init -> dsp_want_external_jit_engine returns g_config.audio.use_dsp_jit (false by default) -> dsp_c_init. First se_frame calls mcpx_apu_update_dsp_preference (gp_ep.c:45-49) with last_known_jit_pref == -1, which calls dsp_set_engine(dsp, false); currently_jit is already false so it returns without touching the backend. No spurious engine swap at startup on Windows, and the DSP56K gate in dsp_set_engine correctly compiles out.

apu: dsp_dma.c scratch buffer (dsp_dma.c:211-221) — the g_realloc conversion fixes a genuine leak, and the `(ssize_t)` cast fixes the signed/unsigned comparison that made the old `-1` sentinel work by accident. The function-local static is not raced: dsp_dma_run is reachable only from dsp_dma_write(DMA_CONTROL) -> write_peripheral, and peripheral writes originate only from DSP instruction execution on the APU frame thread (the GPXMEM/GPPMEM MMIO ranges decode to addresses below DSP_PERIPH_BASE).

apu: d->lock coverage of the new vp_write critical section — every one of the ~45 fe_method-dispatching cases in vp_write (vp.c:858-907) is inside the single `qemu_mutex_lock(&d->lock)` / `unlock` pair, and voice_lock's inlined replacement voice_lock_locked has no remaining caller outside fe_method. The frame thread holds d->lock across the whole of se_frame including voice_work_dispatch's wait for workers, so guest MMIO cannot race the workers' voice_buf snapshots. No lock-order inversion introduced: gp_write/ep_write take BQL->d->lock, and the VP region's lockless-MMIO opt-in means vp_write holds no BQL when it takes d->lock.

apu: Windows timer resolution for the APU pacing loop — os-win32.c:50-56 already calls timeGetDevCaps + timeBeginPeriod(wPeriodMin) from os_setup_early_signal_handling, which runs unconditionally from qemu_init_subsystems (system/runstate.c:961). The throttle() loop's qemu_cond_timedwait sleeps (EP_FRAME_US/1000 = 5 ms at apu.c:191, and remaining_ms in 1..5 at apu.c:209) therefore get ~1 ms granularity rather than the 15.6 ms default. No timeBeginPeriod work is owed.

apu: POSIX-API scan of the slice — grep for getenv/setenv/mmap/open/fopen/usleep/nanosleep/gettimeofday over apu.c, apu_int.h, vp/*.c,*.h, dsp/*.c,*.h and dsp_cpu.c returns only the XEMU_APU_PROF getenv (apu.c:249). No file paths, signals, W^X, page-size or fork/exec assumptions anywhere outside the Apple-only JIT. `__builtin_expect`, `ctz32`, powf/expf/logf/fminf/fmaxf/sqrtf/lrint are all available on MinGW-w64; the only `#pragma push_macro`/Accelerate block is under `#if defined(__APPLE__)` (vp.c:35-44).

apu: Memory-ordering audit of the qatomic conversions — every one is a single naturally-aligned 32-bit or 64-bit slot (d->regs[], d->pause_requested, d->vp.voice_locked[]). QEMU's qatomic_read/set are relaxed, so they buy tear-freedom, not ordering; no code in the slice depends on the acquire/release that the comments loosely imply, and nothing is correct only because of x86-TSO or only because of ARM barriers. The SE2FE_IDLE_VOICE collapse of four RMWs into one qatomic_set (vp.c:804-822) is a strict improvement for the lock-free reader.

apu: ram_ldl/ram_ldw/ram_ldb bounds arithmetic (apu_int.h:127-134, vp.c:92-124) — `addr + N <= d->ram_size` cannot wrap for any reachable address: all inputs derive from 32-bit guest register values plus small constants, and the one subtraction (set_notify_status's `notify_offset - 1`) is preceded by a `+= 15` so it can never underflow past zero. d->ram_size is zero until mcpx_apu_init runs, which merely forces the address_space fallback while the frame thread is still parked at pause_requested = true.

apu: tests/xbox/dsp harness portability — test-dsp-jit-diff.c includes only qemu/osdep.h, glib/gstdio.h and project headers; the cross-process arm uses g_spawn_sync (portable) rather than fork/exec, and all four JIT arms are correctly gated on `host_machine.cpu_family() == 'aarch64' and host_os != 'windows'` in tests/xbox/dsp/meson.build:57. The always-on /corpus interpreter arm builds and runs on MinGW. tests/xbox/meson.build is unconditional and only appends to xbox_test_exes.

Confirmed b_ndebug == false in the local build config, so the plain asserts guarding voice indices in voice_process/is_voice_locked are live in this build.

apu: Vulkan spec validity — no surface in this slice. The APU touches no VkDevice, descriptor, barrier, query, render pass, dynamic state, external-memory import, or host-visible mapping; nothing here can contribute to the MoltenVK-lenient-vs-native-driver bug class.

misc: hw/xbox/xid.c GET_REPORT length handling — the fork's `memcpy(data, &s->in_state, length)` (line 140, was `s->in_state.bLength`) is strictly more correct than upstream: it is guarded by `length <= s->in_state.bLength` on the line above, so it can only shrink the copy, and `p->actual_length = length` already agreed with the short length. No over-read of the 20-byte in_state and no reliance on data_buf being 4096.

misc: hw/xbox/xid.c stale-input concern for the new unbound early-return — traced ui/xemu-input.c:747-777: `xemu_input_bind()` calls `qdev_unplug()` on the XID device *before* clearing `bound_controllers[index]`, and USB unplug is synchronous, so a pad can never be polled after losing its binding. The comment's claim that in_state "stays at its initialized defaults" is therefore accurate: the only reachable no-binding cases (savestate topology, raw -device) are ones where the device was never bound and in_state is still the zeroed realize() state with bLength=20. No stuck-button hazard.

misc: hw/xbox/xid.h struct packing / MSVC-vs-GCC ABI on MinGW-w64 — QEMU_PACKED is plain `__attribute__((packed))` (include/qemu/compiler.h:25) with no `gcc_struct`, but none of XIDDesc / XIDGamepadReport / XIDGamepadOutputReport uses bitfields, and MinGW's default ms_struct layout differs from gcc_struct only for bitfields. Hand-computed sizes match the wire protocol on both ABIs: XIDDesc = 16 (== the hardcoded bLength 0x10 at xid-gamepad.c:108), XIDGamepadReport = 20 (== bMaxInputReportSize 20), XIDGamepadOutputReport = 6 (== bMaxOutputReportSize 6). `s->in_state.bLength = sizeof(s->in_state)` is therefore correct on Windows.

misc: util/ and include/qemu/ (other than lru.h) — `git diff upstream/master...HEAD --stat -- util include/qemu` returns lru.h only; the fork has zero divergence under util/ and adds no files there. include/ divergence is entirely in the TCG/subpage slice (translation-block.h, xemu-subpage-fast.h, physmem.h, tcg-op-common.h, tcg-opc.h, tcg.h).

misc: include/qemu/lru.h — list-invariant walkthrough of every state transition (lru_add_free -> free; lookup-hit: global+bin -> re-head both; lookup-miss: free -> off-both-lists during init_node -> global+bin; evict: bin+global -> free; flush: bin-iteration evict). num_used/num_free bookkeeping balances on every path. Confirmed QEMU's QTAILQ_REMOVE (include/qemu/queue.h:451-462) clears tqe_circ.tql_prev, which is what makes lru_is_node_in_use() correct after the bin removal at lru.h:122. Confirmed the rework actually *fixes* a latent upstream double-hand-out: upstream left the node linked on `global` and not-in-use across the init_node() call, so a nested lru_get_one_free() could return the same node twice; the fork's version has it on neither list.

misc: include/qemu/lru.h callers — audited all 8 Lru instances (gl shader/shader-module/texture/element, vk shader/shader-module/texture/sampler/pipeline/compute-pipeline). Every one calls lru_init() before lru_add_free(). Nothing outside lru.h touches `lru->global`, `lru->free`, or lru_get_one_free(); the only external num_free reader is `ensure_cache_headroom()` (vk/texture.c:1676, `if (lru->num_free > 0) return;`) whose semantics are unchanged. `pgraph_vk_trim_texture_cache()` (vk/texture.c:2586) calls lru_try_evict_one() directly and gets the same victim as upstream (oldest pre_evict-approved in-use node), just without walking the free nodes first.

misc: include/qemu/lru.h re-entrancy audit of every callback — read shader_cache_entry_post_evict (vk/shaders.c:428), shader_module_cache_entry_post_evict (vk/shaders.c:485), and the gl/texture/sampler/pipeline equivalents; none re-enters lru_lookup/lru_evict_* on its own Lru (the shader cache's init_node crosses into the *module* cache, a different Lru, which is safe). This is what makes the finding-2 hazard latent rather than live.

misc: include/qemu/lru.h mid-run lru_flush() call site — gl/shaders.c:302 (disk-cache writeback) flushes the shader cache while the renderer keeps running. Verified the new code path is equivalent: after flush every node is on `free`, and the next lru_lookup() pulls from the free head instead of upstream's global-tail scan. Only the reuse *order* of interchangeable pool slots changes. The adjacent file I/O uses qemu_fopen(path, "wb") — binary mode, correct on Windows.

misc: include/qemu/lru.h Windows/ABI specifics — struct member named `free` is legal C and does not shadow stdlib free; the header is included only from four nv2a C translation units (no C++ TU, so no `free`-as-identifier or QTAILQ-in-C++ issues); `hash % LRU_NUM_BINS` with a power-of-two constant compiles to an AND on x86-64; no `long`, no size_t/pointer punning, no atomics or memory-ordering assumptions (the LRUs are all BQL/PFIFO-thread-confined, unchanged by the fork).

misc: include/qemu/lru.h Vulkan-spec-validity lens — the rework is pure host-side bookkeeping. It does not change *when* post_node_evict destroys VkImage/VkShaderModule/VkPipeline relative to submission, and the texture/sampler pre_node_evict in-flight guards (vk/texture.c:2493/2566) are still consulted on exactly the same set of candidate nodes. No new path can destroy an object referenced by an unretired command buffer on a native NVIDIA driver.

misc: hw/usb/hcd-ohci.c (adjacent to the slice's USB focus, not in my FILES/PATHS — checked opportunistically, found clean). The fork's five hardening hunks: (a) MPS==0 -> ohci_die at line 966 is confined to `len && dir != OHCI_TD_DIR_IN`, matching upstream QEMU's fix; (b) `trace_usb_ohci_td_too_many_pending(ep ? ep->nr : -1)` is dead defensiveness (usb_ep_get() cannot return NULL for ED_EN's 4-bit value <= USB_MAX_ENDPOINTS=15) and the trace event is declared `(int ep) "ep=%d"` so -1 is type-correct; (c) `head &= OHCI_DPTR_MASK` at ohci_service_ed_list entry is redundant-but-harmless for ctrl/bulk_head and genuinely useful for hcca.intr[n]; (d) the `hcca == 0 || !QEMU_IS_ALIGNED(ohci->hcca, 256)` check can never fire from MMIO since HcHCCA writes are already masked with OHCI_HCCA_MASK 0xffffff00 (line 1736); (e) the new `(ctl & OHCI_CTL_HCFS) != OHCI_USB_OPERATIONAL -> return` at line 1248 skips ohci_sof() and therefore does NOT rearm the EOF timer — I traced this specifically as a hang risk and it is safe: the only transitions out of OPERATIONAL that skip ohci_bus_stop() are ->RESUME and ->RESET (ohci_set_ctl, lines 1382-1397), and re-entering OPERATIONAL from either is a state change that calls ohci_bus_start() -> ohci_eof_timer(). The FNO condition `frame_number == 0x8000 || frame_number == 0` correctly implements OHCI 1.0a bit-15-toggle semantics and is masked by HcInterruptEnable in ohci_intr_update().

perf-windows: QEMU_CLOCK_REALTIME on Windows: include/qemu/timer.h:826-831 get_clock() uses QueryPerformanceCounter, so every fork site that paces on it (surface expiry throttle, reports idle budget reports.c:325, the 8 ms min_sync_interval renderer.c:152, MFX resize settle) gets a monotonic sub-microsecond clock.
