merge-review: hw/xbox/nv2a/pgraph/gl/shaders.c: upstream's pgraph_clear_dirty_reg_map(pg) at bind time (line 836) is orthogonal to the fork's shader_uniform_inputs_dirty skip (lines 843-853); the only regs_dirty consumer is vk/draw.c:1090 (not active in the GL renderer), and both clear and set happen under pg->lock, so no lost-update race.

merge-review: win32-dxgi-present.cc vs fork-specific state: SDL window flags are identical to upstream (SDL_WINDOW_OPENGL|RESIZABLE|HIGH_PIXEL_DENSITY, ui/xemu.c:1577-1579); exclusive-fullscreen mode selection (SDL_SetWindowFullscreenMode, 429-431) is also upstream code; Init() is called with the SDL GL context current on the main thread; Resize() only stores an atomic pending size and GL/D3D work is deferred to BeginFrame on the rendering thread; gl_render_frame is serialized by the `rendering` atomic. The vblank thread (ui/xemu.c:887-921) never touches the presenter.

batches.name: Unblock the Windows present path and clean the non-Apple compile
batches.rationale: The headline feature of this merge (DXGI flip-model present) is inert on the target GPU: CreateSharedResources checks interop-FBO completeness on an unlocked WGL_NV_DX_interop object, NVIDIA returns GL_FRAMEBUFFER_UNSUPPORTED, Init() fails and every frame silently falls back to SDL_GL_SwapWindow. Nothing downstream (present pacing, vsync, any perf measurement of the present path) is meaningful until this is fixed. The fix already exists uncommitted in the working tree and only needs committing. Two -Wunused-variable/-Wmissing-prototypes diagnostics on the non-Apple legs ride along because they are in the same ui/ area, are one-line each, and would become hard failures the moment anyone adds --werror to the Windows legs.
finding_titles: DXGI presenter self-disables on NVIDIA: interop FBO completeness checked while WGL_NV_DX_interop object is unlocked
wglDXLockObjectsNV is called twice per frame but unlocked once in the DXGI present path
g_framebuffer_rect_shader is declared on every platform but only ever referenced under __APPLE__ (-Wunused-variable on MinGW/Linux)
xemu_present_is_metal() is defined with external linkage and no visible prototype on non-Apple builds (-Wmissing-prototypes)
batches.approach: Commit the existing working-tree hunk in win32-dxgi-present.cc verbatim (lock the interop object around glGenFramebuffers/glFramebufferTexture2D/glCheckFramebufferStatus, unlock, ReleaseSharedResources+false on incomplete; delete the duplicate unconditional m_wgl_dx_lock_objects_nv in EndFrame so lock/unlock is 1:1). Optionally drain glGetError() once after the completeness check so a stale error does not leak into gl_drain_errors on frame 1. Split g_framebuffer_rect_shader out of the shared declarator list into its own #ifdef __APPLE__ block (optionally gate ShaderType::BlitGammaRect, its case arm and image_gamma_rect_frag_src too). Move #include "xemu-present.h" out of the #ifdef __APPLE__ include block in ui/xemu.c. Escape hatch: this restores the intended path rather than changing behaviour, but add XEMU_WIN32_DXGI=0 to force the SDL_GL_SwapWindow fallback so a DXGI-specific regression stays bisectable; add the row to the README knob table.
batches.validation: Boot to the xemu menu on the TITAN Xp; stderr must show "DXGI Presentation Helper successfully initialized (mode=flip, tearing=...)" and must not show "win32_dxgi present failed or unavailable". Resize the window once to exercise PerformResize -> CreateSharedResources under the same lock. Rebuild the affected TUs with -Werror locally and confirm the two diagnostics are gone. Confirm XEMU_WIN32_DXGI=0 still presents.
batches.macos_risk: none - win32-dxgi-present.cc is only compiled when host_os == 'windows' and is #ifdef _WIN32 internally; the gl-helpers declaration stays byte-identical under __APPLE__; the xemu-present.h include was already unconditional on Apple.

batches.name: Display/PVIDEO path correctness (nested finish abort, frozen overlay, stale composite)
batches.rationale: This is the only remaining hard-abort class on the Windows default path: upload_pvideo_to_cmd calls pgraph_vk_finish() while the display aux command buffer is open, which either trips assert(!r->in_aux_command_buffer) or silently ends the half-recorded CB and then keeps recording into it. It only survives on macOS because the Metal compositor path uses a different CB. Fixing it requires touching the same function that carries the PVIDEO upload cache and the pvideo image recreate bug, so the whole display.c cluster lands together. Second on the list because a crash/black-overlay on any FMV is a worse user outcome than the subtler draw-state bugs, and because it is self-contained in one file.
finding_titles: PVIDEO upload calls pgraph_vk_finish() while the display aux command buffer is open — assert abort / recording-state corruption on Windows
PVIDEO overlay freezes: the upload cache keys on the register state only, never on the VRAM contents
draw_time early-out in pgraph_vk_render_display skips PVIDEO/register-only display changes entirely on non-Apple
create_pvideo_image never records pvideo.width/height, so the overlay image, view and sampler are destroyed and recreated on every upload
PVIDEO YUV->RGBA compute dispatch consumes a flight-partitioned compute descriptor set with no capacity guard
batches.approach: (1) In render_display, before the aux/compositor CB is opened, compute need_pvideo_upload = state.enabled && memcmp(state, last_uploaded_state) != 0 and issue ONE pre-CB finish covering both reclaims: if (need_pvideo_upload && r->in_command_buffer && (STAGING_SRC.buffer_offset > flight[cur].staging_buffer_base || pgraph_vk_compute_needs_finish(r))) pgraph_vk_finish(NEED_BUFFER_SPACE). Delete display.c:547-550 entirely (including the cross-slot `buffer_offset = staging_base` write) and re-read staging_base after any finish. (2) Add nv2a_vk_assert(!r->in_aux_command_buffer) as the first statement of pgraph_vk_finish and delete the now-dead `if (r->in_aux_command_buffer) { vkEndCommandBuffer... }` branch that masked this. (3) Restore upstream semantics for the overlay: upload unconditionally while state.enabled (preferred), or keep the memcmp as a fast reject plus a fast_hash over exactly the bytes upload_pvideo_to_cmd copies, stored in a new last_uploaded_hash reset on savestate load. Do NOT use memory_region_test_and_clear_dirty(DIRTY_MEMORY_NV2A_TEX) - that bitmap is consumed by texture dirty tracking. (4) Widen the pgraph_vk_render_display early-out: hoist get_resolution/interlace/scaling and get_pvideo_state above the guard and require draw_time, width, height and PvideoState all unchanged. On Apple, keep the existing interpolation-stepping branch whenever interp_remaining > 0 || pending_real_texture so a register-only change cannot pre-empt an in-flight interp cycle. (5) create_pvideo_image: early-return when image && width == w && height == h, otherwise destroy/create and THEN assign d->pvideo.width/height; zero them in destroy_pvideo_image. Escape hatch: XEMU_PVIDEO_CACHE=1 restores the register-only skip, XEMU_DISPLAY_SKIP_STRICT=0 restores the draw_time-only early-out; README rows for both.
batches.validation: Needs a title that drives the PVIDEO overlay (in-game FMV or DVD playback): overlay must animate rather than freeze on the first frame, and must appear/disappear when the guest toggles it while the 3D layer is static. Menu boot smoke for no regression. Run once with VK_LAYER_KHRONOS_validation enabled (plus synchronization validation) to confirm no unbalanced/aborted command buffer and no descriptor-update-while-pending VUID. Confirm no new VK_FINISH_REASON_NEED_BUFFER_SPACE storm via XEMU_NV2A_NSPROF / the finish-reason counters.
batches.macos_risk: gated - the Metal/compositor path never took the aborting branch and its finish now simply happens a few lines earlier (which also removes a latent macOS race where the compositor CB was opened and then the flight slot rotated underneath it). The Apple interpolation stepping block is preserved verbatim and is kept dominant when interp work is pending. The PVIDEO upload fix and the pvideo image reuse are platform-neutral improvements macOS also needs today.

batches.name: draw.c pipeline / dynamic-state / query-capacity correctness
batches.rationale: Three high-severity fork-introduced state-tracking bugs that MoltenVK tolerates and native drivers do not: a clear pipeline can stay bound for a following real draw (the fork replaced upstream's accidental attribute-memcmp guard with a dirty flag); the dynamic-state skip caches are not invalidated when a pipeline specifies that state statically (blend constants after any full clear, line width, depth bias); and the REPORTS_FULL capacity guard finishes AFTER begin_pre_draw has already built the framebuffer and descriptor sets, producing framebuffers[-1] (a VkSemaphore handle handed to vkCmdBeginRenderPass) and descriptor_sets[base-1]. All three live in one file and share a validation-layer run, so they land together. The primitiveRestart revert rides along because it is a one-line revert to upstream in the same pipeline-creation function.
finding_titles: create_pipeline() early-return can leave the CLEAR pipeline bound for a subsequent real draw (fork replaced upstream's vertex-description memcmp with a dirty flag)
Dynamic-state skip caches are invalidated at CB begin but not when a pipeline that specifies the same state STATICALLY is bound
REPORTS_FULL capacity guard in begin_draw() submits after begin_pre_draw() already built the frame → framebuffers[-1] and descriptor_sets[base-1]
primitiveRestartEnable=VK_TRUE for strip/fan topologies is a fork-only divergence with no NV2A basis and no GL-renderer counterpart
batches.approach: (1) check_pipeline_dirty(): add r->pipeline_binding->key.clear to the fast-exit condition (key is populated on both LRU hit and miss). Do not introduce a separate clear_pipeline_binding field. (2) begin_draw(), immediately after vkCmdBindPipeline and before the line-width compare: poison every cache whose state the newly bound pipeline specifies statically - cached_line_width when !has_dynamic_line_width, cached_depth_bias_* when !has_dynamic_depth_bias, and cached_blend_constants[0..3] when !has_dynamic_blend_constants (new PipelineBinding field: true in create_pipeline, partial_color_clear in create_clear_pipeline, false in pipeline_cache_entry_init). NaN poisoning survives until the next dynamic-pipeline draw re-issues vkCmdSet*. (3) Move the query capacity guard (draw.c:2259-2274) to the very top of begin_pre_draw(), dropping its trailing pgraph_vk_ensure_command_buffer (begin_pre_draw ends with one). This also fixes the cross-slot inline-vertex/index staging hazard. Keep the `- 1` reserve for the primer query. (4) Turn the two dead nv2a_vk_asserts (framebuffer_index > 0 in begin_render_pass, descriptor_set_index >= 1 in bind_descriptor_sets) into real asserts. (5) Revert .primitiveRestartEnable to VK_FALSE and delete the unverifiable NV2A comment plus the docs bullet. (6) Update architecture-contract Invariant 2 (it cites begin_draw as the guard's home and a no-crash validation) and windows-gating-audit row B1. Escape hatches: XEMU_VK_CLEAR_PIPELINE_RECHECK=0, XEMU_VK_DYNSTATE_POISON=0, XEMU_PRIM_RESTART=1; README rows.
batches.validation: Run under VK_LAYER_KHRONOS_validation on the TITAN Xp before and after: pre-fix a same-state clear->draw sequence should raise the blend-constant/depth-bias VUIDs and the clear-layout descriptor mismatch; post-fix clean. Re-run XEMU_MAX_QUERIES=64 on Windows AND macOS to re-validate the contract's guard-fire claim after moving it, and add a distinct profile counter for the begin_pre_draw guard so future validation can attribute which guard fired. Interleaved savestate A/B expecting zero fps delta (the extra work is one bool read per draw plus a few stores per pipeline change).
batches.macos_risk: none - all four are platform-neutral and macOS is exposed to the identical defects today (MoltenVK also applies statically specified pipeline state at bind, and also currently receives a semaphore handle as a framebuffer when the guard fires). No macOS fast path is removed: the per-draw dynamic-state skip still fires for consecutive draws on the same pipeline. Invariant 2 documentation must be updated in the same commit.

batches.name: Surface/texture upload correctness (flight-slot staging, swizzled zeta, compute-set reservation)
batches.rationale: pgraph_vk_upload_surface_data still assumes it owns all of BUFFER_STAGING_SRC and writes at absolute offset 0, but the fork partitions that buffer per flight slot and its pgraph_vk_finish no longer waits for the CB it submits - so on every other finish the host memcpy overwrites bytes an in-flight vkCmdCopyBufferToImage is still reading (garbled textures). In the same function, a swizzled Z24S8 zeta runs the GPU unswizzle and then throws the result away, uploading depth from Morton-ordered garbage. And the compute descriptor-set partition is checked once before a loop that consumes up to 96 sets, which aborts in release builds. Correctness cluster in two files, one validation-layer run.
finding_titles: Surface upload writes BUFFER_STAGING_SRC at absolute offset 0, ignoring the flight-slot partition, and races the still-in-flight command buffer left by the pipelined pgraph_vk_finish
GPU surface unswizzle is silently discarded (and its output overwritten) for swizzled Z24S8 zeta uploads — depth uploaded from still-swizzled bytes
Compute descriptor-set partition guard checked once before a loop that consumes num_layers * levels sets
batches.approach: (1) In pgraph_vk_upload_surface_data, after the existing finish, take staging_base = r->flight[r->current_flight].staging_buffer_base (defensively finish if buffer_offset > base, as display.c does) and thread it through EVERY use of offset 0: memcpy_image destination, vmaFlushAllocation offset, the host_barrier .offset, swz_copy.srcOffset, buffer_copy_region.srcOffset, and regions[].bufferOffset ONLY on the path where upload_src_buffer is still copy_buffer->buffer (when GPU-unswizzle or the depth unpack ran, the image copy reads BUFFER_COMPUTE_SRC and its offset must stay 0). Replace the bounds check against copy_buffer->buffer_size with one against staging_buffer_limit - staging_base. Slot bases are 256 MiB multiples so texel-block alignment is preserved. Do not permanently advance buffer_offset (the aux CB is fence-waited before return). (2) Hoist the use_compute_to_convert_depth_stencil_format computation above use_gpu_unswizzle and add `&& !use_compute_to_convert_depth_stencil_format` to the use_gpu_unswizzle predicate so swizzled D24S8/D32S8 zeta takes the existing CPU unswizzle_rect branch exactly as upstream; add nv2a_vk_assert that the two are mutually exclusive, and collapse the redundant else-if/else at surface.c:1919-1923. (3) Add pgraph_vk_compute_needs_finish_for(r, n) (index + n > limit) in surface-compute.c, declare it in renderer.h, make the existing 1-arg form call it, and use it at texture.c:885 with num_layers * state->levels; add a QEMU_BUILD_BUG_ON that 96 <= sets-per-slot so a single upload always fits an empty partition. Add the missing plain pgraph_vk_compute_needs_finish check in pgraph_vk_upload_surface_data before pgraph_vk_begin_single_time_commands (never after the CB is begun). Leave the plain assert in update_descriptor_sets as the backstop. Escape hatch: XEMU_SURFACE_STAGING_SLOT=0 restores the offset-0 behaviour for bisecting.
batches.validation: Run with VK_LAYER_KHRONOS_validation + VK_VALIDATION_FEATURE_ENABLE_SYNCHRONIZATION_VALIDATION_EXT: the host-write hazard on the mapped staging range must be flagged before and clean after. Texture-streaming-heavy in-game route on the TITAN Xp looking for garbled textures before/after. For (2), a title with a swizzled RTT depth pass (shadow/env map) with XEMU_ZETA_SHAPE_READBACK=1; trace nv2a_pgraph_surface_upload for ZETA/sz uploads. For (3), exercise a mipmapped cubemap upload and confirm no abort; optionally add an env override of the compute partition size (analogous to XEMU_MAX_QUERIES) to force the guard deterministically. Watch finish counts via XEMU_SURFACE_CB_STATS / nsprof so the defensive finish never fires in steady state.
batches.macos_risk: none - all three defects exist identically on macOS today (there the Apple fast path can skip the finish entirely and clobber the recording CB's texture staging, so the staging fix is if anything more valuable there). The changes add one add per upload, remove one wasted dispatch, and fire the new guard only where the partition would actually overflow (which currently aborts on macOS too).

batches.name: Vulkan hygiene: defensive bounds, barrier ranges, pool ordering, volk device dispatch
batches.rationale: A batch of small, independently safe corrections that convert silent-UB-under-optimization into diagnosable failures and remove two pool/ordering inversions. Deliberately kept separate from the correctness batches so a bisect can distinguish 'behaviour changed' from 'assert added'. Cheap enough for one sitting, and the reclassification of nv2a_vk_bounds_check must land before any further work in surface.c/texture.c so future guest-boundary violations abort instead of licensing the optimizer.
finding_titles: nv2a_vk_bounds_check compiles to __builtin_unreachable() in every build, converting guest-driven bounds guards into optimization licences
copy_zeta_surface_to_texture's narrowed barrier sizes under-count the alignment padding before the stencil plane
prune_invalid_surfaces destroys the newest quarantined surfaces first (inverted relative to upstream)
LRU free-list rework dropped the lru_is_node_in_use() filter in lru_try_evict_one(), so a node on `global` that is not in a bin is returned as "evicted" and then QTAILQ_REMOVE'd from the wrong list
Inline jump-cache probe hardcodes a 16-byte CPUJumpCache entry stride with no build-time assert
is_coherent flush coverage is incomplete: the three host-mapped staging buffers are copied to the device with no vmaFlushAllocation
volkLoadDevice() is never called — every vkCmd* on Windows goes through the vulkan-1.dll loader trampoline
batches.approach: (1) Revert the guest-boundary sites to plain assert() as upstream had them (surface.c:408, surface.c:1929, surface.c:2318-2322, texture.c:1255); keep nv2a_vk_bounds_check only for table-index sites whose index is already masked. Optionally make NV2A_VK_PERF_BUILD follow a meson option defaulting to 1. (2) In copy_zeta_surface_to_texture, derive the covered range from the actual layout (stencil_buffer_size ? stencil_buffer_offset + stencil_buffer_size : w*h*hbpp) and use it for the bounds check and the four barrier .size fields, mirroring surface.c's download path. (3) prune_invalid_surfaces: iterate QTAILQ_FOREACH_REVERSE_SAFE so destruction proceeds oldest-first while the head stays available for get_any_compatible_invalid_surface; keep both existing continue gates. (4) lru.h: assert(lru_is_node_in_use(found)) in the lru_try_evict_one scan and assert(!lru_is_node_in_use(found)) after lru_get_one_free in lru_lookup; fold the QTAILQ_REMOVE + num_free decrement into lru_get_one_free (or document the two-step contract) and note that post_node_evict must not re-enter the same Lru. (5) xemu-inline-jc.c: QEMU_BUILD_BUG_ON(sizeof(array[0]) != 16) and sizeof(vaddr) != 8, or derive the shift from ctz32(sizeof(...)). (6) sync_staging_buffer: add the `if (!b_src->is_coherent) vmaFlushAllocation(...)` one-liner before vkCmdCopyBuffer (dead on every desktop ICD and on MoltenVK; hygiene only, no extra barrier). (7) Add volkLoadDevice(r->device) after vkCreateDevice succeeds and before vkGetDeviceQueue - hygiene, NOT a perf claim; note that device-level entry points for non-enabled extensions become NULL and that vkGetMemoryWin32HandleKHR is covered because its extension is enabled. Items (6) and (7) are also upstream defects and are good upstream PR candidates.
batches.validation: Full boot + in-game route with the new asserts live; none may fire. Sync validation on an odd clip-size D24S8 surface (e.g. 641x480) for (2). For (3), watch the quarantine hit rate (create_surface_image / vmaCreateImage counters) before and after on a title that ping-pongs zeta shapes. For (7), confirm the renderer still initialises and that vkGetMemoryWin32HandleKHR resolves (the VK->GL import path must still work).
batches.macos_risk: none - every item is platform-neutral. (1) restores upstream's assert cost (one predictable branch off the per-draw path), (2) narrows an over-covering barrier to the exact written range on Apple (still valid), (3) can only improve quarantine hit rate, (6)/(7) are dead/no-op on MoltenVK.

batches.name: Shader-key and uniform dirty-tracking correctness
batches.rationale: Two shared-path correctness bugs that only bite on the Windows default renderer or on any guest that updates a light between draws. use_hw_depth is set from !need_geometry_shader rather than !supports_geometry_shaders, so on a GS-capable native driver every POINTS primitive silently takes the MoltenVK dFdx/dFdy depth approximation instead of the exact barycentric path - wrong in z_perspective (w-buffer) mode and divergent from the GL renderer on the same machine. Separately, the fork's new shader_uniform_inputs_dirty gate has an incomplete writer enumeration: seven method handlers write live VSH uniform inputs without marking dirty, so a stale UBO is served whenever a guest moves a light or fades material alpha without touching any other register. Grouped because both are 'shader inputs the gate believes are clean', both need the same in-game validation, and both want the same adversarial refuter.
finding_titles: use_hw_depth is derived from need_geometry_shader, silently changing native-driver fragment depth for POINTS primitives
MoltenVK hardware-depth fallback (use_hw_depth) also fires on native Vulkan drivers for point primitives, replacing an exact depth with a dFdx/dFdy approximation
shader_uniform_inputs_dirty enumeration is incomplete: 7 direct writers of VSH uniform inputs never mark dirty, so the new skip-gate serves stale uniforms
batches.approach: (1) shaders.c:419 -> key.psh.state.use_hw_depth = !r->supports_geometry_shaders, and reword the comment to 'device has no geometry shaders (MoltenVK/Metal)'. This is byte-identical GLSL on macOS (supports_geometry_shaders is always false there) and restores upstream's exact vtxPos/triMZ path on every GS-capable driver, matching draw.c's existing use of the same predicate for topology emulation. Do NOT bundle the separate, macOS-affecting variant (also giving Apple the barycentric path for point lists). (2) Add pgraph_mark_uniforms_dirty(pg) to the seven handlers: SET_MATERIAL_ALPHA, SET_SPECULAR_PARAMS (inside the slot==5 branch only), SET_POINT_PARAMS, SET_LIGHT_INFINITE_HALF_VECTOR, SET_LIGHT_INFINITE_DIRECTION, SET_LIGHT_LOCAL_POSITION, SET_LIGHT_LOCAL_ATTENUATION. For surface_binding_dim, compare-then-mark at the four write sites (gl/surface.c and vk/surface.c) rather than marking unconditionally, so the gate is not defeated on every surface re-evaluation; surfaceSize feeds both the VSH and PSH uniform value setters. (3) Rewrite the enumeration comments (pgraph.h, gl/shaders.c, vk/shaders.c, docs/optimizations.md) as the invariant 'every PGRAPHState field read by pgraph_glsl_set_{vsh,psh}_uniform_values', and record the awk/grep re-verification recipe in docs/windows-gating-audit.md. (4) Add XEMU_UNIFORM_REFUTE=1: when the gate would skip, recompute VshUniformValues/PshUniformValues and memcmp against the last applied values, one-shot fprintf on mismatch. Escape hatches: XEMU_PSH_HW_DEPTH=0|1 forces the flag, XEMU_UNIFORM_DIRTY=0 restores the unconditional pull.
batches.validation: XEMU_UNIFORM_REFUTE=1 soak on the Azurik savestate plus a menu route: zero violations required. Visual check on a title with particle/HUD point sprites (and ideally a w-buffered one) that point depth matches the OpenGL renderer on the same machine before/after. Interleaved A/B to confirm the extra dirty marks do not measurably reduce the skip hit rate (the counters for uniform-gate hits are in the nv2a profile channel; note those are stripped today until the diagnostics batch lands).
batches.macos_risk: none - (1) is byte-identical on Apple Silicon (supports_geometry_shaders is false, so use_hw_depth stays true for every shader, same shader-cache keys). (2) is strictly additive: worst case it turns a wrongly skipped uniform pull back into the pre-optimization unconditional pull, which is exactly when the pull is required. Note the separate macOS-only issue that the use_hw_depth branch itself ignores z_perspective - track it, do not fix it here.

batches.name: SPIR-V disk cache: UTF-8 paths, atomic writes, blob validation, complete key
batches.rationale: The fork's shader cache is the mechanism that removes first-run compile stutter, and on Windows it has three independent failure modes: bare fopen() means it silently never works under a non-ASCII profile path (the sibling pipeline cache already uses qemu_fopen); a non-atomic, unchecked write plus an unvalidated read turns any torn file into a permanent __builtin_trap via VK_CHECK on vkCreateShaderModule, with no self-heal and no diagnostic; and the key omits display.vulkan.debug_shaders, so toggling that option no-ops against a warm cache and, worse, a run made with it on poisons every later run with unoptimized debug-info SPIR-V - which silently corrupts any Windows A/B baseline. Small, self-contained, and it must land before the benchmark harness batch so measurements are not taken against a poisoned cache.
finding_titles: SPIR-V disk cache uses bare fopen() instead of qemu_fopen() — silently never works under a non-ASCII Windows profile path
SPIR-V cache is written non-atomically and read back unvalidated — a torn file is a permanent hard crash via VK_CHECK's __builtin_trap
SPIR-V cache key omits display.vulkan.debug_shaders, so the debug-shader option silently no-ops against a warm cache
batches.approach: Replace both fopen calls with qemu_fopen (osdep.h already reachable via renderer.h; static inline fopen on non-_WIN32 so macOS codegen is byte-identical). Mirror draw.c's save_pipeline_cache_to_disk: write to a per-process-unique temp name ("%s.%u.tmp" with GetCurrentProcessId/getpid), require fwrite == spv->len and fclose == 0, g_rename to the final path, g_unlink the temp on any failure. In load_spirv_from_cache, reject unless size >= 5*4 && (size % 4) == 0 && first word == 0x07230203, and on rejection g_unlink(path) (move the g_free(path) below the check) plus one stderr line naming the file, so the next compile self-heals the entry. Append a variant suffix to the cache directory name in get_spirv_cache_dir ("...-dbg" when g_config.display.vulkan.debug_shaders) so the two variants do not evict each other and existing normal-mode caches stay warm on both platforms. Optionally reflect the blob with SPIRV-Reflect before vkCreateShaderModule and treat reflect failure as a cache miss.
batches.validation: Cold-start timing with the cache dir deleted, then warm-start; confirm the directory repopulates. Truncate one .spv by a few bytes and confirm the next launch logs the rejection, deletes it, recompiles and does not trap. Flip display.vulkan.debug_shaders and confirm a separate directory appears and that RenderDoc/validation actually sees debug info. If a non-ASCII profile path is available, confirm the cache populates (today it silently does not).
batches.macos_risk: none - qemu_fopen is fopen on non-_WIN32; the atomic-write and validation paths are platform-neutral robustness; the directory-suffix key change leaves existing macOS default-config caches warm (only debug_shaders runs get a fresh directory).

batches.name: x87/FP correctness on x86_64 (no codegen change)
batches.rationale: Two independent defects make the shipped Windows build compute wrong float->int and rounding results in the DEFAULT configuration. First, the 2026-08-09 'FIST/FRNDINT rounding fallback' is inert: it routes to gen_helper_* which the soft/hard macro remaps to the __hard variant under perf.hard_fpu=true, and the x86_64 __hard converters are rintl/llrintl, which obey a host x87 control word nothing ever programs - so directed rounding still rounds to nearest, i.e. the MSVCRT floor()/ceil() idiom is silently wrong. Second, gen_flcr's cached_fpuc_rc cache is not invalidated on the Windows longjmp path (Win64 setjmp/longjmp save and restore MXCSR), so after any cpu_loop_exit the cache claims the guest RC is programmed while MXCSR has reverted - all subsequent inline x87 runs in the wrong mode for the rest of the RC epoch. Third, the __hard int converters never raise float_flag_invalid, so FIST's integer-indefinite substitution is dead code and out-of-range conversions wrap (1e10 -> 1410065408) instead of yielding 0x80000000. Deliberately scoped to no new instruction encodings so it can land and be validated independently of the SSE lowering batch.
finding_titles: Windows longjmp restores MXCSR, leaving gen_flcr's cached_fpuc_rc stale: inline x87 silently runs with the wrong rounding mode
The 2026-08-09 x86_64 FIST/FRNDINT directed-rounding fallback is a no-op: it calls the *hard* helper, which is itself RC-blind on x86_64
x86_64 hosts never program the host x87 rounding mode, so the 2026-08-09 FIST/FRNDINT directed-rounding fallback is inert under the default hard_fpu=true
hard floatx80_to_int32/int64 never raise float_flag_invalid, so FIST's integer-indefinite substitution is dead code and out-of-range conversions wrap
x86_64 SSE host-FP bracket omits the cached_fpuc_rc invalidation its aarch64 twin has, but on x86_64 the inline x87 path is MXCSR-based too
batches.approach: (1) cpu_exec_longjmp_cleanup() - the single shared landing routine for both sigsetjmp sites - gets an unconditional (XBOX && TARGET_I386) `cpu_env(cpu)->cached_fpuc_rc = 0xFFFF;` with a comment naming the invariant 'anything that changes host MXCSR/FPCR outside tcg_gen_flcr must reset cached_fpuc_rc'. Do not hang it off cpu_handle_exception (cpu_loop_exit_noexc bypasses it). One 16-bit store per longjmp. (2) Make the directed-rounding fallbacks call the un-remapped soft symbols explicitly: gen_helper_frndint__soft, gen_helper_fist{,l,ll}_ST0__soft, guarded so hosts without the __soft symbols are unaffected. This is the minimal change that makes the shipped behaviour match the documented intent; the faster CVT/ROUNDSD lowering is the next batch. (3) Range-check inside the x86_64 and aarch64 __hard int converters: on overflow/NaN float_raise(float_flag_invalid) and return INT32_MIN/INT64_MIN, so helper_fist*'s indefinite substitution works. Gate on !defined(__APPLE__) only if a zero-Apple-delta landing is required - do NOT gate on !__aarch64__, because Windows ARM64 routes every FIST through the aarch64 __hard helper. (4) Add `env->cached_fpuc_rc = 0xFFFF;` inside the `if (want != csr)` block of the x86_64 xemu_hostfp_enter, mirroring the aarch64 twin, and correct windows-gating-audit row F2 (on x86_64 the inline x87 is SSE2 and shares MXCSR with the SSE bracket - they are NOT independent registers). (5) Correct the 2026-08-09 entry in docs/optimizations.md. Escape hatch: perf.hard_fpu=false already exists as the coarse fallback; add XEMU_X87_RC_STRICT=0 to restore the old (broken) fast paths for bisecting.
batches.validation: Guest snippet regression: FLDCW RC=down (0x077F) then FLD 2.7; FRNDINT must yield 2.0 and FISTP must yield 2; RC=up (0x0B7F) on 2.2 must yield 3. Out-of-range: FISTL of 1e10/1e30/NaN must store 0x80000000 under all four RCs with FPUS_IE consistent. XEMU_X87_REFUTE=1 differential (run alone, never stacked with the subpage or DSP refuters per the archaeology wedge) under the default perf.hard_fpu=true. XEMU_X87_CENSUS to size the FRNDINT/FIST RC!=0 population before quoting any perf effect. Cheap optional refuter: on x86_64, stmxcsr at the top of cpu_exec_longjmp_cleanup and count RC mismatches against cached_fpuc_rc - expect non-zero before, zero after.
batches.macos_risk: none on Apple Silicon - (1) costs one redundant msr fpcr per longjmp; (2) and (5) are inside !__aarch64__/x86_64-only blocks; (4) is in the #else /* __x86_64__ */ arm; (3) is the only shared edit and only changes results for inputs whose current answer is already wrong (out of int range or NaN), with in-range conversions byte-identical. Intel macOS gets the same fixes.

batches.name: APU and host-array bounds (guest-controlled indices, pitch clamp, engine-switch race)
batches.rationale: One guest-reachable arbitrary 4-byte host write: the fork turned a 16-bit guest voice handle into an index into filters[256] and then dereferences and stores through whatever pointer it finds, reachable from plain MMIO (SET_CURRENT_VOICE takes any 32-bit value, and unlike VOICE_ON there is no assert). Two smaller fork-introduced audio behaviour changes ride along (a pitch LUT that wraps at the int16 boundary for a ~65000x wrong resample rate, and lock-free GP/EP reads whose justifying comment cites a BQL guarantee that does not hold against the APU thread, with a real use-after-free window when the DSP engine is switched from the UI). The xid/xemu-input pad index is the same class of unchecked host-array index and is one line, so it lands here too.
finding_titles: Guest-controlled voice handle indexes the host filters[] array out of bounds (wild read, then wild write)
Pitch LUT truncates the envelope-modulated pitch and wraps at the int16 boundary, giving a ~2^16 wrong resample rate
ram_stl / ram_stb bypass invalidate_and_set_dirty, so APU guest-RAM writes no longer set the NV2A / NV2A_TEX / CODE dirty bits
gp_read/ep_read lock-free rationale comment asserts a BQL guarantee that does not hold against the APU thread
Fork's new unbound-pad guard is reached through an unbounded array index: device_index >= 4 reads past bound_controllers[4] and then writes through the garbage pointer
batches.approach: (1) Add `static inline uint32_t *voice_snapshot(MCPXAPUState *d, uint16_t h) { return likely(h < MCPX_HW_MAX_VOICES) ? d->vp.filters[h].voice_buf : NULL; }` and use it in voice_get_mask, voice_get_word and voice_set_mask; out-of-range handles then fall through to the existing bounds-checked ram_ldl/ram_stl path, exactly upstream's semantics. Optionally treat v >= MCPX_HW_MAX_VOICES as an invalid entry in the voice-list walk (log + break) so an active bad handle cannot reach the assert in voice_process. Do not mask FECV. (2) Clamp before the pitch LUT index: pitch_f = fminf(fmaxf(p + ps*32.0f*ef_value, -32768.0f), 32767.0f) then cast; skip LUT interpolation (0.29-cent steps are inaudible) but note the saturation as an intentional divergence from upstream's SRC_ERR_BAD_SRC_RATIO silence. (3) ram_stl/ram_stb: either add memory_region_set_dirty(d->ram, addr, len) after the direct store (the public API, and what upstream's gp_ep.c already does after its raw memcpy) or accept it and write the reasoning as a code comment plus an audit row - pick one and record it. (4) Rewrite the gp_read/ep_read comment to say reads are deliberately lock-free and tolerate stale/torn DSP memory relative to the APU thread; close the engine-switch use-after-free by making audio.use_dsp_jit read-once-at-init (drop the runtime dsp_set_engine from mcpx_apu_update_dsp_preference and change the menu tooltip to 'Takes effect on next title launch', matching the Apple toggle) or by performing the swap under the BQL. (5) ui/xemu-input.c: bounds-check index in xemu_input_get_bound; additionally error_setg on device_index >= 4 in both usb_xbox_gamepad realize functions so a bad -device line fails loudly.
batches.validation: Audio smoke on a music/voice-heavy title before and after, with XEMU_APU_PROF=1 utilisation unchanged. Reproduce the OOB deliberately: NV1BA0_PIO_SET_CURRENT_VOICE with 0x1234 followed by SET_VOICE_CFG_FMT (via monitor/MMIO or a debug hook) must no longer fault. Launch with -device usb-xbox-gamepad,index=4 and confirm a clean error instead of a wild pointer. Toggle the DSP JIT checkbox repeatedly during play and confirm no crash (or that it is now restart-only).
batches.macos_risk: none - all of these are on shared paths; for every in-range voice handle and pad index the generated code and values are identical, only the out-of-range paths change (from UB to upstream semantics). The pitch clamp only affects indices that today produce a ~65000x wrong rate. The engine-switch change is inert on Apple, where dsp_jit.enabled already forces use_jit=false.

batches.name: Make the diagnostics actually report on Windows
batches.rationale: Hard prerequisite for every perf batch: today three of the four measurement channels the fork's methodology depends on are dead or lying on this target. nsprof never prints under the OpenGL renderer because nsprof_flip_tick has a single call site in the Vulkan flip path; xemu_inv_ticks returns a constant 0 on x86_64 so XEMU_INV_TIMING prints an all-zero notdirty_write report (exactly the measurement needed to decide whether to port sub-page arm (b)); the NV2A profile counters are stripped unconditionally so the in-app HUD plots fabricated zeros even in --debug builds; and XEMU_SUBPAGE_FAST=1 silently does nothing on a host with no store-prefilter emitter. All are diagnostic-only paths, none change shipped behaviour.
finding_titles: nsprof never prints under the OpenGL renderer: nsprof_flip_tick() is only wired into the Vulkan flip path
xemu_inv_ticks() returns a constant 0 on x86_64 hosts, so XEMU_INV_TIMING prints an all-zero notdirty_write timing report on Windows
NV2A_STRIP_PROFILE_COUNTERS defaults to 1 unconditionally, so the in-app NV2A profiling HUD reads zero in every build including debug
Sub-page arm (b) inline NOTDIRTY store-skip has no i386 emitter, so Windows x86_64 forfeits the whole measured +12% draws/s win (the arm-(a) bitmap it needs is already default-on there)
batches.approach: (1) Move nsprof_flip_tick() into DEF_METHOD(NV097, FLIP_STALL) immediately after ops.flip_stall(d) and delete the call in vk/renderer.c - same PFIFO-thread instant for Vulkan, so macOS per-flip denominators are byte-identical; do NOT add a second call in gl/renderer.c (double counting). Update the stale file:line in the diagnostics SKILL and note that under OpenGL only flips + flip_idle are populated. (2) Add an x86 arm to xemu_inv_ticks returning __builtin_ia32_rdtsc() (optionally with an lfence to mirror the isb intent), keeping __aarch64__ first, and give xemu_inv_tick_ns a matching arm that calibrates ns/tick once against g_get_monotonic_time and caches it; fix the stale fallback comment. (3) Make NV2A_STRIP_PROFILE_COUNTERS default to 0 under XEMU_DEBUG_BUILD and 1 otherwise, and replace the function-like no-op macro with a typed `static inline void nv2a_profile_inc_counter(enum ...) { (void)cnt; }` so arguments stay type-checked and evaluated (compiles to nothing at -O2). (4) In the host-agnostic latch that DOES run on x86_64 (xemu_subpage_dirty_on in tb-maint.c), warn_report once if XEMU_SUBPAGE_FAST=1 or XEMU_SUBPAGE_FAST_REFUTE=1 is set on a host with no emitter, and fix the docs/optimizations.md knob row to say 'aarch64 hosts only; no-op on x86_64'.
batches.validation: XEMU_NV2A_NSPROF=1 must print the 5 s summary under BOTH renderers on Windows (with only flips/flip_idle populated under GL). XEMU_INV_TIMING=1 must print non-zero total/inval/rest and a sane ns/call. A --debug build must show moving counters in the ImGui NV2A panel; a release build must show the panel gated off or unchanged-zero by design. XEMU_SUBPAGE_FAST=1 must print the one-time warning. Confirm release-build codegen for the counter no-op is unchanged (spot-check one hot TU's assembly or object size).
batches.macos_risk: none - (1) is the identical PFIFO-thread instant on the Vulkan path; (2) keeps the __aarch64__ arm first so Apple Silicon still uses cntvct_el0; (3) only restores the per-draw counter store in macOS --debug builds (its intended cost), release unchanged; (4) fires only on hosts with no emitter, never on aarch64.

batches.name: Windows benchmark fixture, harness and testing protocol
batches.rationale: Gate for every perf batch below. Today there is no way to produce a receipt-backed number on this machine: the qcow2 has 0 snapshots and xemu.toml has no [general.snapshots.shortcuts], so the golden fixture does not exist; and every harness script is #!/bin/zsh, hard-wired to dist/xemu.app, uses cp -Rc APFS clones, an AF_UNIX monitor socket, pgrep for the quiet-machine check (absent here), and screencapture/Quartz for the artifact oracle. Without this batch no perf claim in batches 13-21 can meet the fork's own evidence bar, and the leftover-harness-loop incident class has no Windows detector.
finding_titles: The testing protocol is macOS-only end to end (pgrep quiet-check, ~/Library toml, APFS clones, screencapture, System Events) with no Windows variant or recipe
Every benchmark / soak / probe harness script is hard-wired to dist/xemu.app, so the fork's own Windows acceptance gate cannot be executed
Every fork bench/probe driver is #!/bin/zsh with zsh-only syntax; zsh is not installed on the Windows target
meta.json generator calls `uptime` unguarded; the binary is absent on MSYS2 so no receipt is ever produced
Visual artifact gate is Quartz + screencapture only; on Windows it always SKIPs, so the ARTIFACT exit-3 net silently never fires
XEMU_INPUT_PIPE is a no-op stub on _WIN32, so no live-movement / streaming-lag benchmark class exists on Windows
batches.approach: Step 0 (user, manual): launch xemu, boot Azurik, reach the target scene, F7/F8-save; recover the real vm-* tag with .claude/skills/xemu-diagnostics-and-tooling/scripts/list_snapshots.py on the live image (block/file-win32.c opens with FILE_SHARE_READ so a read-only open alongside a running xemu is safe); record the tag, title, scene and date in a Windows fixture table in xemu-validation-and-qa. Do NOT port the zsh scripts - write a new stdlib-Python scripts/bench-savestate-ab-win.py that: copies dist/ and clones xbox_hdd.qcow2 + eeprom.bin to a scratch dir (never runs the user's live dist/qcow2), writes a scratch xemu.toml with Windows paths, fullscreen_on_startup=false and a pinned surface_scale, launches xemu.exe with -config_path and -monitor tcp:127.0.0.1:<unique port>,server,nowait, waits for the port, sleeps the warmup, sends loadvm <tag> over the socket, dwells N s in 5 s ticks sampling CPU via psutil/Get-Process TotalProcessorTime deltas over >= 5 s windows, then quits; it reuses scripts/bench-receipt.py and nsprof_summarize.py unmodified (both are stdlib and already run here). Keep the same gates (draws/flip band, CV <= 0.10, cross-arm identity) so receipts are structurally comparable to macOS ones, and never compare absolute fps across platforms. Quiet-machine check: tasklist /FI "IMAGENAME eq xemu.exe" plus a Get-CimInstance Win32_Process CommandLine filter for ninja|cc1|lto|bench|soak|probe|abx (catches the between-cycles soak that owns no xemu process), plus nvidia-smi utilization ~0%. Artifact oracle: prefer triggering xemu's own SaveScreenshot GPU-readback path and scoring the PNG with the existing pure-Pillow score(), rather than PrintWindow (flip-model swapchains often return black). Guard the unguarded `uptime` shell-out in the macOS harness with try/except OSError while there. Document that XEMU_INPUT_PIPE is a POSIX-FIFO facility with no Windows transport, so the movement-probe/live-route class is out of scope until a named-pipe or file-tail backend is added - and add a clear early guard to the zsh scripts so an accidental bash/Windows invocation fails with a message instead of a parse error.
batches.validation: Run a null A/B (identical binary in both arms) and require: receipt.json produced, CV <= 0.10 per arm, cross-arm draws/flip identity, and a delta inside the noise band. Then a sanity A/B with a knob known to matter (e.g. surface_scale 1 vs 2) to prove the harness can detect a real difference. Confirm the quiet-machine check flags a deliberately started background ninja.
batches.macos_risk: none - new Windows-only script plus documentation; existing zsh harness, its defaults and the bundle-clone isolation rule stay byte-identical (the only edit is a try/except around uptime and an explicit 'requires zsh' guard).

batches.name: Build-system and CI enablement for native Windows
batches.rationale: Three build-side gaps that block later work and hide native-only breakage. XEMU_PGO on Windows emits clang IR-PGO flags and merges with llvm-profdata, but the branch never selects clang and llvm-profdata is not installed here - so on the stock MSYS2 GCC toolchain PGO silently produces .gcda that the use stage never finds, and the documented two-stage flow cannot complete (docs D7 names Windows PGO as an open item). No CI leg builds natively on MSYS2 MINGW64 - the fork's own preferred Windows path - which is why three native-only breakages had to be found by hand. And two subproject build hunks are guarded on the wrong machine or shadow upstream files silently.
finding_titles: XEMU_PGO on Windows is wired for clang/llvm-profdata but the branch never selects clang; on the MSYS2 GCC toolchain PGO is silently non-functional
No CI leg builds or tests natively on MSYS2 MINGW64; three native-Windows build breaks had to be found by hand
tar --force-local is gated on host_machine.system() but it is a property of the build machine's tar, not the target
patch_directory overlays a full frozen copy of the pinned imgui repo's meson.build, so a wrap revision bump silently reverts upstream's build file
XEMU_HARDENING opt-out for -fzero-call-used-regs is inside the Darwin case arm only; Windows has no A/B knob for it
batches.approach: (1) setup_pgo(): detect compiler family (`${CC:-cc} -dM -E - </dev/null | grep -q __clang__`) and add a GCC arm - generate uses -fprofile-generate=$pgo_dir -fprofile-update=atomic (QEMU is heavily multithreaded; without atomic the profile is noise), use uses -fprofile-use=$pgo_dir -fprofile-correction -fprofile-partial-training -Wno-missing-profile -Wno-coverage-mismatch, no llvm-profdata merge, and the existence check becomes 'any *.gcda in the dir'. Make check_pgo_staleness either recognise GCC's diagnostics or print an explicit 'GCC profile - report not implemented' so a 0/0 is not misread as clean. Refuse to proceed when compiler family and profile format disagree. Fix the misleading comment and the three doc claims. (2) Add a windows-latest `test-native` job (fail-fast: false, NOT a needs: of packaging) using msys2/setup-msys2@v2 with msystem MINGW64, shell: msys2 {0}, installing base-devel git zstd and the mingw-w64-x86_64 toolchain/ccache/ninja/pkgconf/python/glib2/pixman/libepoxy/SDL3/libsamplerate/libslirp/vulkan-headers/vulkan-loader; build ./build.sh --debug with a ccache cache, then ninja test-xbox and meson test --suite xbox --print-errorlogs --no-rebuild resolving the venv path (pyvenv/bin or pyvenv/Scripts). Expect xbox-mcpx-dsp, xbox-mcpx-dsp-corpus-interp and xbox-nv2a-swizzle to select. Optionally upload dist/ so get_deps.py (another native-only path) is exercised. Update the change-control class-5 gate text and close the docs §H line. (3) dsp56300/meson.build: change the --force-local guard to build_machine.system() == 'windows' (it is a property of the tar meson invokes) and use find_program('tar') so the resolved binary appears in the log; offer this hunk upstream. (4) imgui overlay: add a CI/scripts drift guard that clones the pinned revision and diffs meson.build/meson_options.txt/backends/imgui_impl_metal.mm against subprojects/packagefiles/imgui/, allowing only the known deltas - or better, convert the overlays to wrap diff_files= so a revision bump that no longer applies fails loudly. Do NOT delete the overlay (the .mm carries the fork's MRC leak fixes). (5) Hoist the XEMU_HARDENING block (and its zero_call_regs_override/check_zero_call_regs_order pairing) out of the Darwin case arm to just before the configure invocation so the knob is reachable on Windows/Linux; default stays 1 everywhere; fix check_zero_call_regs_order's token parsing for the quoted Windows compile database and treat '0 matched compile lines' as a warning, not success.
batches.validation: Both existing Windows CI legs (x86_64 GCC cross and arm64 llvm-mingw) must stay green, plus the new native leg green with the xbox suite passing. Locally: XEMU_PGO=generate then XEMU_PGO=use must complete on MSYS2 GCC and produce a binary; the staleness report must say something honest. Confirm the imgui drift guard fails when the pinned revision is bumped without refreshing the overlay. Confirm the dsp56300 extraction still works on both native MSYS2 and the Linux-hosted cross build.
batches.macos_risk: none - the Darwin case arm keeps profdata_prefix="xcrun " and the clang PGO path unchanged, build-macos.yml is untouched, and the tar guard is false on a Darwin build machine (bsdtar never sees --force-local, identical to today). The XEMU_HARDENING hoist keeps the default at 1 on every platform.

batches.name: perf: restore -O3 build parity on the Windows arm
batches.rationale: Highest payoff-per-line perf item and the cheapest to try now that a harness exists. The fork's release-options block drops -Doptimization=3 and -Dstack_protector=disabled on the win64*|MINGW*|MSYS* arm while its comment claims only LTO was dropped; confirmed empirically on this tree (optimization = 2, no -O3 in the compile line for accel/tcg/cpu-exec.c) while Darwin/Linux release builds get -O3. Neither option has anything to do with the ThinLTO/qemu_build_not_reached_always problem the comment cites. Whole-binary effect on the TCG interpreter and the NV2A renderer.
finding_titles: Windows release build silently loses -Doptimization=3 (ships -O2) although the comment claims only LTO was dropped
batches.approach: Add -Doptimization=3 (and -Dstack_protector=disabled for arm parity; a no-op today on mingw but keeps the arms honest) to the win64*|MINGW*|MSYS* arm and reword the comment to 'only LTO is CI's call (per-toolchain)'. Note -fno-strict-aliasing stays, so no new aliasing hazard at -O3. Keep -Db_lto* out of this arm. Optional, separate, opt-in follow-up for the NATIVE MSYS2 GCC branch only: XEMU_LTO=1 adds plain -Db_lto=true (never -Db_lto_mode=thin, which is a meson setup error on GCC); CI's x86_64 wincross leg already proves mingw-GCC LTO links this tree. Add a README knob row if XEMU_LTO is adopted.
batches.validation: Both Windows CI legs green first (the only theoretical risk is the arm64 llvm-mingw release leg's qemu_build_not_reached_always elision, which more optimization normally helps). Then an interleaved savestate A/B on the Azurik fixture using the new Windows harness, with a predicted number and kill threshold stated before the run; if the delta is inside noise, land it anyway as build parity and record the null result rather than claiming a win.
batches.macos_risk: none - the *) arm that Darwin and Linux take is untouched.

batches.name: perf: x86_64 FIST/FRNDINT via MXCSR-honouring SSE instead of the x87 round-trip
batches.rationale: FIST/FISTP is one of the hottest x87 opcodes in Xbox title code (float->int for every index, coordinate and loop bound), and on this host every RC=0 FIST emits MOVQ [rsp-0x10] / FLD m64 / FRNDINT (microcoded, ~11 uops on Haswell) / FSTP m64 / MOVQ and only then CVTSD2SI - two store-forwarding round trips plus a microcoded x87 op where one SSE instruction suffices, because gen_flcr has already programmed MXCSR with the guest RC. RC 1/2 and every non-nearest FRNDINT additionally pay a full helper call after the previous batch's soft-helper fix. Highest-confidence codegen win available, and it deletes the fallbacks that batch 8 had to add.
finding_titles: i386 backend lowers rint_f32/f64 to x87 FRNDINT, forcing FRNDINT (RC!=0) and FIST (RC 1/2) onto the softfloat helper on Windows x86_64; SSE4.1 ROUNDSS/ROUNDSD would be one instruction and correct for all four RCs
perf: every RC=0 FIST/FISTP emits an x87 FRNDINT memory round-trip on x86_64 where a single CVTSD2SI would do
i386 backend lowers rint_f32/f64 to x87 FRNDINT (perf-opportunity companion): SSE4.1 cpuinfo bit and ROUNDSD lowering

The fork's new AArch64 FP backend gives INDEX_op_cvt{32,64}f_i{32,64} truncate semantics (FCVTZS) while the pre-existing i386 backend gives them MXCSR-rounded semantics (CVTSD2SI) — same TCG opcode, two different rounding contracts
batches.approach: (1) FIST first (bigger, needs only SSE2): in ops_fpu.h gen_fistl_ST0/gen_fistll_ST0, wrap the RC switch so that under #if defined(__x86_64__) the plain tcg_gen_cvt<PRECf>_i32/_i64 is emitted for ALL four RCs - that is byte-for-byte upstream's ops_fpu.h and is correct because CVTSD2SI/CVTSS2SI round per MXCSR and produce the same integer indefinite on overflow. Keep get_st0() so gen_flcr still fires. Then delete the RC 1/2 helper fallbacks in translate.c gen_fistl_ST0/gen_fistll_ST0/gen_fist_ST0 (they become redundant). (2) FRNDINT: add CPUINFO_SSE41 (free bit 8; CPUID.1:ECX bit 19) plus have_sse41, define OPC_ROUNDSS/OPC_ROUNDSD (0x0a/0x0b | P_EXT3A | P_DATA16), and in OP_f32_f64(rint) emit the legacy 2-operand tcg_out_modrm form with imm8 = 0x04 (use MXCSR.RC) when have_sse41, keeping the FLD/FRNDINT/FSTP block as the pre-SSE4.1 fallback; make the translate.c gen_frndint fallback a runtime predicate (soft helper when !have_sse41) rather than a compile-time delete. (3) Leave the FISTTP wrappers on the helper path (FISTTP must truncate regardless of MXCSR and the guest's Coppermine has no SSE3). (4) Document the cvtNf_iM rounding contract at the DEF() and at both backend switch cases rather than silently diverging (optionally switch the i386 lowering to CVTTSS2SI/CVTTSD2SI to match the documented truncate contract and drop the three FISTTP hatches - verified safe against all current callers, but it buys nothing on this guest, so treat as optional cleanup). (5) Correct docs/optimizations.md and windows-gating-audit's 2026-08-09 claims. Escape hatch: XEMU_X87_SSE_CVT=0 restores the x87 round-trip lowering.
batches.validation: Predict first: add/extend an XEMU_X87_CENSUS counter for FIST by RC and FRNDINT by RC to size the population before quoting fps. Correctness: XEMU_X87_REFUTE=1 differential (alone, never stacked) must be clean for RC 0/3 (bit-identical to today) and must now pass RC 1/2 cases; plus the guest snippet regressions from batch 8. Then an interleaved savestate A/B on a floor()/ceil()-heavy title and on the Azurik fixture.
batches.macos_risk: none - tcg/i386/tcg-target.c.inc, host/include/i386 and util/cpuinfo-i386.c are not compiled on Apple Silicon, and every translate.c/ops_fpu.h edit is inside #if defined(__x86_64__) or an existing !defined(__aarch64__) block, so the AArch64 FCVT{N,M,P,Z}S/FRINTI lowering is byte-identical.

batches.name: perf: evaluate and possibly enable the host-SSE fast path on x86_64
batches.rationale: xemu_sse_neon_mode defaults to 1 only on __aarch64__; every other host ships dark. The fork's own comment argues the x86_64 case is stronger than the ARM one - host and guest share the ISA, so _mm_{add,sub,mul,div,min,max}_ps ARE the guest instructions, bit-perfect including NaN payload selection and (-0,+0) ordering, and the MXCSR bracket matches FTZ/DAZ independently. The helpers it replaces measured ~6% of the vCPU thread on the fork's bench scene, and each currently runs 4 softfloat calls per packed op. Sequenced after batch 8 because enabling it without the x86_64 cached_fpuc_rc invalidation would corrupt inline x87 rounding and denormal handling.
finding_titles: perf: the host-SSE fast path is bit-exact by construction on x86_64 yet ships dark, leaving the packed-SSE helpers on softfloat on the Windows box
batches.approach: Prerequisite: the x86_64 xemu_hostfp_enter cached_fpuc_rc invalidation from batch 8 must already be in. Step 1: run XEMU_SSE_HOST=2 (strict-bracket differential) over a live route long enough to accumulate a few 1e9 checks; the harness aborts on any non-NaN-class divergence, so a clean run is the receipt. Note the =2 mode uses strict brackets and therefore does NOT exercise the sticky-leave composition, so the x87 side must be validated separately with XEMU_X87_CENSUS/REFUTE under mode 1. If it diverges, stop and record - do not flip. Step 2: interleaved savestate A/B, XEMU_SSE_HOST=1 vs unset. Step 3 only if it clears the fork's bar: change the non-aarch64 arm from `mode = 0` to `mode = g_config.perf.hard_fpu ? 1 : 0`, keep XEMU_SSE_HOST=0 as the escape hatch, and update the comment plus the docs table. Record in the perf note that the MSYS2 build is non-PGO GCC so the number is not directly comparable to the Apple PGO figure.
batches.validation: XEMU_SSE_HOST=2 clean soak (documented check count), an x87-side check under mode 1 (guest ftol/denormal probe or census/refute run), then 3/3 interleaved A/B pairs clearing the fps bar before any default flip.
batches.macos_risk: none - only the non-aarch64 arm of the existing #if changes; Apple Silicon keeps `mode = g_config.perf.hard_fpu ? 1 : 0` verbatim and its measured numbers.

batches.name: perf: port the sub-page store pre-filter (arm b) to the i386 backend
batches.rationale: The largest single measured optimization in the fork (+12% draws/s, 6/6 interleaved pairs, ~2M eligible stores/s completed inline) exists only as an AArch64 emitter, while the host-agnostic arm-(a) bitmap it depends on is already default-ON on Windows. The win comes from renderer-watched guest pages - a property of the guest workload and the NV2A dirty-tracking design, not the host ISA - so a comparable win should be available here. Ranked below the cheaper items because it is a real TCG backend change with substantial implementation and soak cost, and because the XEMU_INV_TIMING measurement enabled in batch 10 should size the prize before the work is done.
finding_titles: Sub-page arm (b) inline NOTDIRTY store-skip has no i386 emitter, so Windows x86_64 forfeits the whole measured +12% draws/s win (the arm-(a) bitmap it needs is already default-on there)
batches.approach: Measure first with the now-working XEMU_INV_TIMING to size notdirty_write cost on this box. Then add sf_out_store_prefilter to tcg_out_qemu_st_slow_path under #if defined(XBOX) && defined(__x86_64__), called after the label patches and before tcg_out_st_helper_args, with the same eligibility filter as aarch64 (!is_ld, size <= MO_64, !MO_BSWAP). Register state differs from AArch64: on i386 the jne is emitted before the addend load, so at stub entry TCG_REG_L0 is a pointer to the CPUTLBEntry and TCG_REG_L1 is the page-masked address - the stub must load addr_write and addend itself. Use BT rather than variable shifts (SHR needs CL): `bt rw, rp; jc demote` for the block map, and the memory form `bt [dirty0], page_idx; jnc demote` for the dirty bitmap (contiguous per the existing QEMU_BUILD_BUG_ON). Zero-extend the I32 guest address before adding the addend. Complete with tcg_out_qemu_st_direct using HostAddress{base=addr, index=addend}. Pick scratch registers from the call-clobbered set avoiding addr/data regs. Reuse the existing C refuters (xemu_sf_refute_st{b,w,l,q}) for mode 2. Land default-OFF on non-Apple (the existing #ifdef __APPLE__ default already does this) with XEMU_SUBPAGE_FAST=1 as the opt-in.
batches.validation: XEMU_SUBPAGE_FAST=1 XEMU_SUBPAGE_FAST_REFUTE=1 soak to 0 violations across static and loadvm-cycling routes - run alone, never stacked with XEMU_X87_REFUTE and XEMU_DSP_JIT_DIFF (the three-way refuter boot wedge is a recorded incident). Then an interleaved savestate A/B reporting draws/s (fps alone can hide this win) before any consideration of a Windows default flip.
batches.macos_risk: none - Apple keeps its existing default-on AArch64 stub untouched; the new emitter is compiled only in the i386 backend and lands default-off there.

batches.name: perf: Windows scheduling and UI pacing
batches.rationale: The fork gives PFIFO and vblank QOS_CLASS_USER_INTERACTIVE on macOS and nothing on Windows, where 6+ runnable threads share 4 physical cores on a Haswell and the scheduler has no hint about which is deadline-sensitive. Separately, XEMU_UI_FRAME_CAP_NS lives inside metal_render_frame, so the GL/DXGI path free-runs and pays a blocking PFIFO round trip per UI frame with vsync off. Both are cheap, env-gated, and mutually independent, but expected payoff on a symmetric x86 box is modest - hence this rank. Neither is a known dead end (nothing in the archaeology records a failed Windows thread-priority attempt), but a null result is the likely outcome and should be recorded as such.
finding_titles: PFIFO thread scheduling hint is Apple-only; Windows has no equivalent priority bump on the frame-critical thread
Vblank thread priority bump is Apple-only; no Windows equivalent (Invariant 12 has no non-Apple arm)
APU frame thread runs at default priority on Windows with no equivalent of the fork's Apple QoS bumps
UI frame cap and frame_seq dedup exist only in metal_render_frame; the GL/DXGI path free-runs and pays a blocking PFIFO round trip per UI frame
batches.approach: Prove the premise before coding: instrument the vblank thread's wake overshoot (now - next_vblank) and its BQL acquisition time, p50/p99 once per second. If overshoot p99 is already sub-millisecond (likely, given os-win32.c's timeBeginPeriod and SDL's high-resolution waitable timer) the priority idea is dead and only the frame cap remains. If it is real: add a single shared helper xemu_thread_set_frame_critical() (#if __APPLE__ -> pthread_set_qos_class_self_np; #elif _WIN32 -> SetThreadPriority(THREAD_PRIORITY_ABOVE_NORMAL) unless XEMU_THREAD_PRIO=0) so Invariant 12 stays a one-liner, and apply it to the vblank thread first, PFIFO second (PFIFO is compute-bound; lifting it above the vCPU thread on 4C/8T is a regression risk), APU frame thread only if the throttle pacing counters show a meaningful 'speedup' share. Never TIME_CRITICAL/HIGHEST; do not reach for MMCSS/avrt (SDL's WASAPI thread already registers with MMCSS). Separately, hoist the XEMU_UI_FRAME_CAP_NS block verbatim from metal_render_frame into render_frame() ahead of the presenter dispatch with default 0 (uncapped) - zero behavioural change on both platforms - and only consider a non-zero default for the vsync==false GL path (8000000 ns to match min_sync_interval_ns) after a separate A/B. Update Invariant 12 and audit row A6 if any arm lands.
batches.validation: State the prediction and kill threshold before each run (e.g. abandon if mean fps gain < 0.5% and no reduction in nsprof flip_idle p50/p99). Interleaved savestate A/B per arm, one variable at a time. Record a null result in the archaeology skill rather than silently dropping it.
batches.macos_risk: none - every Windows arm is #elif defined(_WIN32) with the __APPLE__ branch untouched, and the frame-cap hoist preserves metal_render_frame's behaviour and its default of 0 verbatim.

batches.name: perf: renderer micro-costs and memory footprint
batches.rationale: A measure-first bundle of small renderer costs and allocation sizing, grouped because each is individually below the fork's measurable threshold and none should be carried as complexity unless it shows up. Also closes a real footprint issue for low-VRAM Windows machines (this box has 12 GiB and surface_scale=2 so it absorbs it, but ~1 GiB of dedicated mapped staging plus a 128-entry double-image quarantine plus an always-allocated scratch image per surface is a hard wall on a 4 GiB card).
finding_titles: Bulk vkCmdResetQueryPool resets the whole 2048-query slot partition on every command buffer, not just the indices actually used
Surface-expiry throttle samples QEMU_CLOCK_REALTIME on every draw
Pipeline-cache serialize + file write runs synchronously on the PFIFO thread every 30 s; NVIDIA blobs are far larger than MoltenVK's
BUFFER_STAGING_DST/SRC grew 64 MiB → 512 MiB each and are now both persistently mapped: ~1 GiB of dedicated, committed, mapped host memory at startup
Every surface allocates a full-size scratch image on non-Apple, and the invalid-surface quarantine was raised 10 -> 128, multiplying dead-surface VRAM by ~25x
batches.approach: Order by measurement, drop anything inside noise. (a) Query reset: add a per-slot query_reset_hw initialised to queries_per_slot (fresh pool state is undefined), set from num_queries_in_flight at submit, and reset MAX(1, hw) indices at CB begin; re-init on pool recreation; do not read flight[slot].query_count at begin time (it is already zeroed by the drain). (b) Surface-expiry throttle: gate the QEMU_CLOCK_REALTIME read behind `++ticks >= 64 || pg->frame_time != last_expire_frame_time` so low-draw scenes still get a per-flip sample and the burst backstop still fires. (c) Pipeline cache: check the existing 'Saved pipeline cache (N bytes)' lines first - it is only 394 KB on this box today, so most likely do nothing; if an nsprof bucket shows max >= ~8 ms, keep vkGetPipelineCacheData on the PFIFO thread and hand the buffer to a single detached writer with a one-in-flight flag, joined before the synchronous shutdown save. Do NOT add a geometric backoff or a minimum-pipeline-delta threshold (the finalize save does not run on a normal quit, so the periodic path is the only save that happens). A cheap orthogonal win: skip the write when the O(1) size query matches the last saved size. (d) Right-size BUFFER_STAGING_DST from the documented worst case (it is single-surface and synchronous) with the derivation in a comment; leave BUFFER_STAGING_SRC's size alone unless finish-count measurement justifies shrinking a per-flight bump pool. (e) Replace the #if defined(__APPLE__) scratch-image gate with a runtime predicate that keeps the AMD-Windows staging workaround (vendorID 0x1002) and otherwise skips the scratch at scale 1, restoring upstream's deleted comment; make num_invalid_surfaces_to_keep heap-size-derived on non-Apple only (128 was tuned on a 192 GB M2 Ultra) and add a prune call to the near_budget branch of pgraph_vk_check_memory_budget, keeping the evict_submit_seq retirement watermark. Escape hatches: XEMU_SURFACE_SCRATCH=1, XEMU_QUERY_RESET_FULL=1.
batches.validation: XEMU_NV2A_NSPROF before/after for (a)-(c); drop anything inside noise. For (d)/(e), watch VK_FINISH_REASON_NEED_BUFFER_SPACE counts and vmaCreateImage/quarantine hit rates plus process working set. Full in-game route on the Azurik fixture; note this box runs surface_scale=2, so pin the scale in the benchmark config and also spot-check scale 1.
batches.macos_risk: gated where it matters - (a)-(c) are platform-neutral and at worst neutral on MoltenVK (the primer query and its index are untouched, so Invariant 3 holds). (d) is a footprint reduction on unified memory too. (e) keeps Apple's existing scale>1 scratch predicate byte-identical and applies the quarantine byte/heap cap only on non-Apple, since Apple's deferred zeta-shape reuse was tuned against the 128-entry pool.

batches.name: perf: persistent decode thread pool for the OpenGL texture path
batches.rationale: The GL renderer creates and frees a GThreadPool per upload - six times for a mipmapped cubemap - and for the very common levels == 1 case that is a full producer/consumer round trip with zero parallelism, plus real CreateThread cost on Win32 with its 8 MiB default stack reserve. The fork's own Vulkan renderer already does this correctly with a pool created once at init. Ranked low on the Windows list because Vulkan is the default renderer here, so this path is only hit as the documented triage workaround and as the init_renderer fallback - but it is exactly the path a Windows triager will be told to use.
finding_titles: GL texture upload creates and destroys a GThreadPool per upload (6x per cubemap); with levels==1 it is pure cross-thread overhead and zero parallelism
batches.approach: Port the Vulkan renderer's mechanism rather than inventing one: add GThreadPool *decode_thread_pool to PGRAPHGLState, created in pgraph_gl_init_textures with MIN(nproc, 4) and freed in pgraph_gl_finalize_textures; copy the DecodeTaskBatch{remaining, QemuEvent} + init/wait helpers from vk/texture.c and give GLDecodeTask a batch pointer so the worker decrements and signals. Replace both g_thread_pool_new/g_thread_pool_free pairs with push + batch wait. Decode inline on the caller thread when s.levels == 1 (a handoff can never win with one task) and for tiny levels, mirroring the VK width/height <= 16 rule. Push with a GError and fall back to inline decode on push failure. Pass PGRAPHGLState down from generate_texture. Optionally hoist the six cubemap faces into a single batch so a non-mipmapped cubemap gets real 6-way parallelism. Drop the 'NULL pool -> NULL upload' rationale from the write-up - it is false for a non-exclusive pool.
batches.validation: Interleaved savestate A/B with display.renderer = 'OPENGL' on a texture-streaming-heavy route; NV2A_PROF_TEX_UPLOAD gives the upload count to scale the expected saving (needs the profile-counter fix from batch 10 in a debug build). Uploaded bytes must be byte-identical - a screenshot diff on a fixed frame is a sufficient correctness check since only the threading topology changes.
batches.macos_risk: none - the same per-upload pool churn exists on the macOS GL renderer today (also non-default there); decoded bytes and upload order are unchanged and no Apple-specific code is touched.

batches.name: perf: async VK->GL compositor handoff via external semaphores (measure-first)
batches.rationale: The renderer already requires VK_KHR_external_semaphore_win32 at device selection and never uses it; the only ordering between the Vulkan composite pass and the GL presenter is the blocking aux-fence wait in pgraph_vk_end_single_time_commands, which stalls the PFIFO thread once per present. Apple already has the async alternative (compositor command-buffer ring + exported timeline) fenced behind HAVE_IOSURFACE_SHARING, and the CB ring itself compiles on all platforms - so this is a port, not a new design. Ranked last among the substantial perf items because it is the highest-effort item with two real hazards and because the payoff must be measured before any of it is built.
finding_titles: VK_KHR_external_semaphore_win32 is a hard device requirement but is never used; the VK->GL present handoff has neither the required GL semaphore nor a layout/ownership transfer
batches.approach: Step 1, zero code: run XEMU_NV2A_NSPROF on Windows and read the aux_fence bucket (NSPROF_AUX_FENCE_WAIT wraps exactly this wait) per flip in a heavy scene. State a kill threshold first (e.g. < 0.3 ms/present -> stop). Step 2 if it clears: create one exportable binary VkSemaphore at display init (VkExportSemaphoreCreateInfo, OPAQUE_WIN32), export with vkGetSemaphoreWin32HandleKHR, import once into the UI GL context with glGenSemaphoresEXT + glImportSemaphoreWin32HandleEXT after a one-time epoxy_has_gl_extension probe with synchronous fallback (mirroring the Apple present_timeline_event probe); extend async_compositor to this case and submit through pgraph_vk_begin_compositor_commands with pSignalSemaphores. Add a binary-signal sibling of pgraph_vk_end_compositor_commands_async (the existing one uses a timeline, which opaque Win32 GL semaphores cannot consume). Two hazards the naive version gets wrong: (a) pgraph_vk_sync skips render_display when < 8 ms elapsed, so a pull can return the texture with NO new signal - publish a 'composited this pull' flag and only glWaitSemaphoreEXT when set, or waiting on an unsignaled binary semaphore hangs; (b) the return direction is a WAR hazard - the next composite transitions disp->image UNDEFINED->COLOR_ATTACHMENT while GL may still be sampling the previous frame, so either signal a second semaphore after the GL draw and wait it in the composite submit, or give the display image a ring aligned with COMPOSITOR_CB_RING. Use srcLayouts = GL_LAYOUT_SHADER_READ_ONLY_EXT to match the final transition. Land behind XEMU_GL_ASYNC_COMPOSITOR, default off until measured. Do NOT move VK_KHR_external_semaphore_* to the optional extension list - it is upstream code, every relevant Windows ICD exposes it, and this port uses it.
batches.validation: nsprof aux_fence before/after plus an interleaved savestate A/B. Correctness: a long route with window resizes and renderer-menu interaction looking for a hang (the unsignaled-wait hazard) or tearing/stale frames (the WAR hazard); run once under the validation layer for semaphore-signal VUIDs.
batches.macos_risk: none - HAVE_EXTERNAL_MEMORY is 0 on Apple, so both the required-extension list and the entire GL-semaphore path compile out; macOS keeps its existing MTLSharedEvent/compositor-CB handoff untouched.

batches.name: perf: measure the DSP execution engine on Windows and document the knob
batches.rationale: On Windows both JITs are off: the fork's inline block JIT is aarch64-POSIX-only (DSP56K_JIT_SUPPORTED is 0), and upstream flipped audio.use_dsp_jit to false for its first release - so the MCPX DSP always runs the C interpreter, even though the dsp56300 subproject already ships and links a prebuilt x86_64-pc-windows-gnu library. Ranked last because the only recorded A/B (Apple: 19% vs 22% APU-thread utilisation) bounds the prize at ~3 points of one off-frame-critical-path thread, and the archaeology already establishes that APU-thread savings do not convert to fps. Worth an explicit measurement so 'Windows has no DSP JIT' is a known, documented state rather than a surprise.
finding_titles: Windows now runs the plain DSP56300 C interpreter: neither JIT engine is on by default
DSP runs fully interpreted on Windows: the inline JIT is aarch64-POSIX-only and the external dsp56300 engine defaults off, despite a Windows prebuilt existing
Docs still claim audio.use_dsp_jit defaults on / non-Apple hosts get the dsp56300 JIT by default
batches.approach: Do NOT flip the shipped default silently - upstream disabled it deliberately. (1) Measure: fixed savestate route with XEMU_APU_PROF=1, audio.use_dsp_jit false vs true, recording APU-thread utilisation and listening for artefacts. (2) Fix the stale docs regardless of the result: docs/optimizations.md ('default on', 'Non-Apple hosts get upstream's dsp56300 engine by default'), plus the four skill files that still say default true, with a dated drift entry per house style. (3) Add a README/knob-table row stating that Windows runs the DSP interpreter unless [audio] use_dsp_jit = true, which is the only DSP acceleration available there. (4) Only if the win is real and the engine is stable, propose the flip upstream rather than diverging, or land it as an explicitly Windows-gated default through change control with the A/B receipt.
batches.validation: XEMU_APU_PROF utilisation numbers for both engines on the same route, plus an audio-artefact listen test. Docs claims re-verified against config_spec.yml and dsp_want_external_jit_engine.
batches.macos_risk: none - config/docs only, and dsp_want_external_jit_engine checks dsp_jit.enabled first on DSP56K_JIT_SUPPORTED hosts, so nothing about use_dsp_jit affects the Apple inline-JIT selection (contract Invariant 5).

batches.name: Documentation and audit reconciliation
batches.rationale: Several audit rows and skill invariants are now factually wrong in ways that would mislead the next auditor: F2 claims x86_64's MXCSR is independent of the inline x87 (it is not), A5 claims non-Apple first-run picks OpenGL (config_spec's default is VULKAN on every platform, and get_default_renderer is never consulted), Invariant 2 cites begin_draw as the query guard's home and a no-crash validation that this pass contradicts, Invariant 12 has no non-Apple arm, and the 2026-08-09 optimizations entries overstate what the FIST/FRNDINT fallback and the sub-page knob actually do on Windows. Landing last so it records the as-shipped state after batches 1-21, but each earlier batch still carries its own doc edits.
finding_titles: renderer default flipped to VULKAN for every platform, not just Apple — get_default_renderer's __APPLE__ gate never fires on a fresh config
x86_64 SSE host-FP bracket omits the cached_fpuc_rc invalidation its aarch64 twin has, but on x86_64 the inline x87 path is MXCSR-based too
Physical-device preference matches by name only: two identical GPUs make the Vulkan device diverge from the GL adapter after the first run
Docs still claim audio.use_dsp_jit defaults on / non-Apple hosts get the dsp56300 JIT by default
batches.approach: Do NOT change the renderer default (that is a policy reversal that would also hide the Windows Vulkan path from the validation currently in progress); instead amend audit row A5 to say 'get_default_renderer FALLBACK ordering matches upstream; the configured first-run default is VULKAN on all platforms via config_spec.yml - see §K', and note in the README Windows section that Vulkan is the default with renderer='OPENGL' as the manual fallback. Rewrite F2 with the real mechanism. Update Invariant 2 (guard location, the framebuffers[-1]/descriptor_sets[-1] exposure, and the re-validation recipe) and Invariant 12 (add the non-Apple arm if batch 17 lands one, or record the null result). Correct the 2026-08-09 entries for FIST/FRNDINT and add a Windows section covering: the SPIR-V cache key, the nsprof GL limitation, the sub-page knob being aarch64-only, and the Windows fixture/harness recipe pointers. Optional, upstream-facing: the physical-device preference matches by deviceName only with no break, so two identical GPUs diverge the Vulkan device from the GL adapter and the VK->GL import assert aborts - record it as a known multi-GPU limitation with a suggested fix (add break; compare VkPhysicalDeviceIDProperties deviceLUID against GL_DEVICE_LUID_EXT under HAVE_EXTERNAL_MEMORY, reject in is_device_compatible so the existing OpenGL fallback fires) rather than implementing it on a single-GPU box.
batches.validation: Every claim re-checked against code with a recorded grep/file:line; add the re-verification commands to the audit's §J list. No runtime validation needed.
batches.macos_risk: none - documentation only.
